items.desc: Company: A leading quantitative proprietary HFT firm expanding into mid-frequency strategies across global equities and futures markets. Location: London The role: The firm is building a specialist machine learning team focused on large-scale sequential modelling for alpha generation. The team develops transformer-based and other deep learning models on market data, from representation learning through to forecasts that feed directly into live, risk-bearing equities and futures strategies. Responsibilities Design, train, and evaluate transformer-based and other sequential deep learning models (e.g. attention architectures, state-space models, recurrent networks) to forecast returns and related market quantities across equities and futures. Build and own the data and feature pipeline: how order book, trade, and bar-level data are tokenised and represented, how cross-asset and cross-sectional context is brought in, and how the models cope with non-stationarity and regime change. Develop rigorous training and validation frameworks for noisy, low signal-to-noise financial data, including leakage-safe cross-validation, walk-forward testing, and robust out-of-sample evaluation. Scale model training and inference on large GPU clusters, optimising for throughput, latency, and stability, working closely with ML infrastructure and engineering teams. Turn model outputs into tradable signals, working with portfolio construction and execution teams on turnover, transaction costs, and capacity. Iterate on live performance: monitor model behaviour and PnL in production, diagnose alpha decay and drift, and retrain and refine models over time. Requirements Advanced degree (PhD or MSc) in a quantitative discipline: Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, or similar. Expertise in modern deep learning, with hands-on experience building and training transformer-based or other sequential models at scale (e.g. attention mechanisms, self-supervised pre-training, state-space models). Demonstrable experience applying ML to financial time series in a systematic trading setting, ideally across equities and/or futures at mid-frequency horizons. Proficiency in Python and a major deep learning framework (PyTorch or JAX). C++ and experience with distributed training or high-performance computing environments are a plus. A track record of taking research into production and generating live PnL is highly valued. Publications at leading ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or experience at a top AI research lab are a plus. Experience with market microstructure or transaction cost modelling is preferred.

items.desc: Neurosoft Bioelectronics is developing next-generation AI for decoding neural time series (high-density subdural ECoG LFPs). We seek an intern machine learning scientist with interest in sequence modelling, state-space methods, self-supervised learning, and/or physics-informed machine learning to build foundation models that infer dexterous finger movements and continuous high DoF upper extremity kinematics, initially from only few minutes of brain data. The role spans research into modern system identification, representation learning, and real-time deployment of low-latency inference pipelines. Tasks Research design and benchmarking Kalman filters, RNNs, LSTMs, Structured State Space Models (S4/S5), Mamba, Neural ODEs, and related sequence architectures. Research developing large-scale self-supervised pretraining pipelines and subject-specific fine-tuning workflows. Research reproducing and exteding published SoTA neural decoding methods, beginning with LSTM baselines and modern SSM architectures. Research decoding individual fingers, grasp synergies, continuous gestures, and full 6 DoF hand pose. Research deploying streaming inference using ONNX, TensorRT, Triton, and GPU acceleration. Research maintainance of reproducible benchmarking, MLOps, and production research infrastructure. Requirements Familiarity with Python, C/C++, Java, MATLAB, LaTeX, HTML, JavaScript, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Familiarity with Signal Processing, Machine Learning, Familiarity with Animal Care, Rodent Injections, Microscopy, Sterilization Techniques Some capabilities in independent research, scientific writing, strategic planning, time management, presentation Optional: Theoretical foundations of time-series modelling, system identification, dynamical systems, differential equations, control theory, and Bayesian estimation. Optional: Recent implementation of Kalman filters, HMMs, linear/nonlinear SSMs, RNNs, LSTMs, S4/S5, Mamba, Neural ODEs, or Transformer-based sequence models. Optional: Any experience with contrastive learning, VAEs, foundation-model pretraining, transfer learning, domain adaptation, and few-shot learning. Optional: Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, CUDA, Docker, ONNX, TensorRT, Triton, GitHub, Linux, and MLflow. Benefits Growth: Opportunity to join an ambitious neurotechnology startup with exposure to multiple areas of company operations. Culture: A collaborative and dynamic team environment with direct interaction with founders and leadership. Flexibility: Hybrid work model with the possibility remotely and at the office in Geneva. Compensation: Entry-level salary range of 45'000 - 55’000 CHF per year. First promotional review after 3 months. Ownership: Equity participation through the employee option plan may be available. We view neural decoding as a problem of system identification: learning latent state-space representations that increasingly approximate the underlying continuous dynamical system generating voluntary movement of a particular individual. Your role is about implementing, testing, and benchmarking the methods developed in collaboration with our academic partners. Due to the novelty of this effort, this is a mandatory intake role across all seniority levels. At any point you take over an essential practice, tech stack, or reach an essential milestone, your compensation and authority will reflect that. Your role scope and growth are entirely metrics-driven and evaluated quarterly. This is a CSO-track role.

items.desc: About Cerrion Cerrion builds video AI that helps manufacturers detect, understand and respond to production problems in real time. Headquartered in Zurich and backed by Creandum and Y Combinator, our platform connects to factory cameras to identify process deviations, quality issues and safety risks, and trigger alerts or automated actions. Our technology is deployed in factories across more than 15 countries, helping production teams reduce downtime and waste. The Role We’re hiring an Applied Researcher to set and execute the research agenda for Cerrion’s video‑AI platform and turn bold hypotheses into measurable gains in accuracy, robustness, and latency. We’re looking for a superstar who brings founder‑style ownership across the end‑to‑end research lifecycle — problem framing, data curation, rapid prototyping, experiment design, and rigorous evaluation — balancing scientific depth with pragmatism and a strong bias for shipping. You’ll work directly with our technical leadership and the research team to prioritize the research roadmap, run a fast and reproducible experiment pipeline, and partner with Engineering to turn promising ideas into production‑ready models. Your Responsibilities Run Fast, Reproducible Experiments: Design and run searches; keep configs, seeds, and artifacts tidy for one‑click reruns. Diagnose Bad Runs: Trace failures across data, augmentations, labels, and training dynamics; implement quick fixes and verify with targeted evals. Curate & Improve Data: Define datasets, create focused error sets, manage sampling/imbalance, and partner on labeling/QA to close the loop. Own Evaluation: Build and maintain a rigorous eval suite (accuracy/robustness/latency/cost), plus small dashboards for trend tracking and failure clustering. Prototype to Production: Convert promising ideas into production‑ready models in partnership with Engineering (tests, packaging, canary, monitoring). Optimize for Cost & Latency: Profile training/inference, choose efficient architectures, and keep GPU hours and serving budgets in check. Communicate Clearly: Make sure the experimental environment is clean and documented so that the experimental knowledge is well-preserved. Build the Function: Establish research hygiene (coding standards, review, documentation) and help shape hiring as the team grows. Desired Skills And Experience Applied ML/CV Experience: 2+ years working with real‑world models (images or video), Kaggle experience would be a plus Relevant education: Masters or PhD in Computer Science or related field with strong computer vision or machine learning understanding Strong Python + PyTorch: Comfortable writing clean training/eval loops Experiment Operations: Hands‑on with ML experiment platforms (ClearML, etc.) Data‑Centric Mindset: Practical know‑how in augmentations, class imbalance, sampling strategies, label quality, and active‑learning basics. Evaluation Rigor: Fluency with mAP/F1/IoU/ROC‑PR, calibration, robustness tests, and dataset/version management for reproducible comparisons. Collaboration & Writing: Able to turn findings into clear recommendations and work closely with Engineering, Product, and GTM. Preferred ML Qualifications Video & Tracking: Experience with temporal models (2D/3D CNNs, transformers), multi‑object tracking, motion/occlusion handling. Foundation/Multimodal: Familiarity with pretraining, VLM adapters/LoRA, or lightweight finetuning of foundation models. Scale & Search: Distributed training (DDP/FSDP), HPO frameworks (Optuna/Ray Tune), and thoughtful compute budgeting. Model Optimization: Distillation, pruning, quantization; deployment with ONNX Runtime/TensorRT; edge/real‑time constraints a plus. Data Tooling: Labeling ops, weak supervision, synthetic data generation/augmentation pipelines. Domain Context: Prior work in video analytics for industrial or safety‑critical environments. Why Cerrion Ownership & impact: Own improvements to vision systems that run continuously in real factories and help production teams reduce downtime and waste. Growth path: Develop your expertise across applied computer vision, production software and MLOps, with support from an experienced technical team. Culture: We operate with flat hierarchies and a get‑things‑done mentality. You’ll work with ambitious colleagues from all over the world in a collaborative environment where the best idea wins. Compensation & equity: Competitive salary, meaningful stock option package and comprehensive benefits. Location: Modern office in the heart of Zurich; enjoy the quality of life of Switzerland and the dynamism of a high‑growth startup. Cerrion is an equal opportunity employer.  Qualcomm AI Research is seeking world-class researchers to help push the boundaries of artificial intelligence and machine learning. items.desc: CommonAI CIC is a non-profit membership organisation, founded on a belief in collaborative engineering for the safe and responsible development of foundational AI technologies. A place where AI startups, enterprises large and small, public sector bodies and academia can share resources and knowledge, to codevelop and grow businesses, fast. We are led by experienced founders, investors and engineers who believe that collaborative engineering drives faster AI innovation and are backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. The Opportunity We are seeking a Research Scientist to drive our research on new large language model architectures that reduce the cost of inference while retaining performance. The work treats the realities of serving hardware, such as memory bandwidth and data movement, as first-class design constraints. It runs on the UK's national AI supercomputers and on our own compute nodes. You will join a small research team, working with our Research Software Engineer and kernel engineer, and take early-stage ideas through to rigorous experiments, larger-scale runs and publication. As an AI-first company, we strongly believe in collaborative engineering powered by the tools we are helping to build. This role places a major emphasis on using LLMs, AI coding assistants, and autonomous agents for research and software development, and you will have a top-tier Claude Code subscription. What You'll Do Design and implement new model components, such as attention variants, structured or sparse layers, routing mechanisms, activations and training objectives. Run controlled pretraining experiments at matched compute, from small scale up to larger models. Analyse the structure that trained models learn, and what it means for efficiency and interpretability. Explore adapting existing open models through continued training or distillation. Work with our engineers to turn research ideas into reliable, reproducible training runs and efficient kernels. Write papers, release code and present results. Requirements A PhD in machine learning, computer science, physics or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Published or shipped research on new model components, such as attention mechanisms, activation functions, normalisation, mixture-of-experts routing, or structured or sparse layers. Hands-on experience pretraining transformer language models from scratch, including careful ablations at matched compute. Strong PyTorch (or deep JAX experience and willingness to work in PyTorch), including multi-GPU training. A working understanding of LLM inference costs, such as KV cache, memory bandwidth and why decoding is memory-bound. Rigour in experimental design: strong baselines, statistical comparison and honest reporting of negative results. A strong enthusiasm for using LLMs, coding assistants, and agents as core tools in your own research and development process. We also value: GPU kernel work (e.g. Triton, CUDA) for sparse or custom attention. Experience with sparsity, pruning, mixture-of-experts or distillation of LLMs. Knowledge of accelerator and cluster hardware, including memory hierarchies and interconnects. Experience running workloads on HPC systems with a batch scheduler such as Slurm. Mechanistic interpretability experience. A quantitative background from another field, such as physics, applied maths or neuroscience. Interest in hardware–model co-design. Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package and pension Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential people from across the tech sector, financial services, and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station CommonAI CIC is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace.

items.desc: Описание Multiverse Computing Multiverse Computing is a fast-growing deep-tech company founded in 2019 and recognized by CB Insights as one of the 100 most promising AI companies globally. We are the largest quantum software company in the EU, with 300+ employees worldwide and growing, delivering advanced solutions trusted by leading global enterprises across several critical industries, including finance, energy, manufacturing, telecom, and industrial sectors. Our mission is to enable organizations to gain a meaningful competitive edge through cutting-edge AI and quantum technologies. You’ll work alongside world-leading experts, developing solutions that deliver real-world value for global clients. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, ethics-driven culture grounded in sustainability, diversity, and collaboration - a place where ambitious, curious people take ownership, push boundaries, and grow. Come and join us. Задачи Build and maintain the training stack our researchers use every day: multi-node training and post-training pipelines (SFT, distillation, RL) built on Megatron-LM, Megatron Bridge and NeMo RL. Build scalable data pipelines for curation, filtering, deduplication, tokenization and synthetic data generation. Build and maintain evaluation pipelines, so benchmark results are reproducible and comparable across models and checkpoints. Build RL environments, verifiers and reward pipelines for reasoning, coding and agentic tasks, and keep rollouts fast and stable. Profile and optimise training and inference: GPU utilisation, memory, parallelism configuration, checkpointing, I/O. Package, optimise and benchmark models for deployment, including on non-NVIDIA and edge hardware. Turn research ideas (new architectures, compression methods, training recipes) into clean, tested, reusable code, and run experiments together with the research team. Keep our work reproducible through containers, configs, experiment tracking, CI, code review and documentation. Требования Master’s in Computer Science, AI, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent industry experience. 2+ years of industry experience building ML systems, including at least 1 year hands-on with transformer models or LLMs. Strong Python software engineering: clean, maintainable, tested code; git, code review, unit and integration tests, CI. Strong PyTorch and hands-on experience training or fine-tuning transformer models. Experience running multi-GPU jobs and a working understanding of distributed training (data, tensor and pipeline parallelism; FSDP or DeepSpeed). Comfortable with Linux, containers (Docker or similar) and shared GPU clusters (Slurm or Kubernetes). Experience building data pipelines that process large datasets. Solid ML fundamentals: you understand what happens inside training, not just how to launch it. Good debugging and communication skills. Fluent English. We don't expect anyone to have all of these. Our research covers many areas and nobody on the team is an expert in all of them. If you are strong in some and new to others, we still want to hear from you. Experience with the NVIDIA stack: Megatron-LM, Megatron Bridge, NeMo RL, NeMo Gym, NeMo Curator. Hands-on post-training: SFT, DPO, or RL (GRPO, PPO), or frameworks such as verl, TRL or OpenRLHF. Inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) for serving, synthetic data generation or RL rollouts. Deployment on edge or alternative hardware: llama.cpp, ExecuTorch, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, vendor NPU SDKs. Model compression: quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, FP8), pruning, distillation. GPU performance work: profiling (Nsight, PyTorch profiler), Triton or CUDA kernels. Evaluation tooling: lm-evaluation-harness, lighteval, NeMo Evaluator. Experiment tracking and MLOps (MLflow, Weights & Biases), cloud platforms (ideally AWS). Experience with Physical AI tooling: robotics simulation (Isaac Sim/Lab, MuJoCo) or vision-language-action models. Spanish. Merged contributions to major open-source ML projects (PyTorch, Megatron-LM, vLLM, Hugging Face, etc.). Knowledge of tensor networks or quantum-inspired methods. Publications or patents. Условия Indefinite contract. Equal pay guaranteed. Variable performance bonus. Signing bonus. We offer work visa sponsorship (if applicable). Relocation package (if applicable). Private health insurance. Eligibility for educational budget according to internal policy. Hybrid opportunity. Flexible working hours. Language classes and discounted lunch options. A high-performance, collaborative environment, operating at pace on cutting-edge technologies. Career plan. Opportunity to learn and teach. As an equal opportunity employer, Multiverse Computing is committed to building an inclusive workplace. The company welcomes people from all different backgrounds, including age, citizenship, ethnic and racial origins, gender identities, individuals with disabilities, marital status, religions and ideologies, and sexual orientations to apply.

items.title: Research Associate in Computational Pathology and Multimodal AI
items.card: You will develop and validate deep learning methods that combine routine histology with radiology, multiplex imaging, spatial transcriptomics and clinical data to predict how oral and head and neck cancers behave and how they respond to treatment. The group is led by Professor Ali Khurram , a Professor and consultant in oral and head and neck pathology. The group’s work includes multicentre validated tools for
items.desc: The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special. We are looking for a Research Associate to join the NEOPATH research group in the School of Clinical Dentistry, University of Sheffield. You will develop and validate deep learning methods that combine routine histology with radiology, multiplex imaging, spatial transcriptomics and clinical data to predict how oral and head and neck cancers behave and how they respond to treatment. The group is led by Professor Ali Khurram , a Professor and consultant in oral and head and neck pathology. The group’s work includes multicentre validated tools for detecting and grading oral epithelial dysplasia, and profiling tumour infiltrating lymphocytes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Current programmes, funded by Cancer Research UK, Stand Up To Cancer and MRC, address cancer risk in oral potentially malignant disorders, and response to treatment. Your research will centre on building and training models on large whole slide image, radiological and genomic cohorts for a range of cancer, linking image features to clinical outcomes and testing whether those models hold up on data from other centres and scanners. Alongside this, you will coordinate team meetings, work with our academic, clinical and patient collaborators, help develop grant applications and papers, and present our work at scientific and public events. The post would suit someone with a PhD in a computational or quantitative field, or someone from a pathology or biomedical background who has built substantial programming and machine learning skills. A background in histopathology, radiology, omics and bio-informatics is a clear advantage, because much of the work sits where pathology and computation meet. We will provide clinical training for strong candidates from a computational background. Main Duties And Responsibilities Design, train and validate deep learning models for diagnosis, grading and outcome prediction in cancer. Develop multimodal models that integrate histology with radiology, multiplex immunofluorescence or immunohistochemistry, spatial transcriptomics and clinical variables. Build and maintain reproducible pipelines for slide preprocessing, stain normalisation, tissue and cell segmentation, feature extraction and model evaluation, using version control and clear documentation. Curate and manage large imaging and clinical datasets in line with ethics approvals, data protection law and NHS information governance requirements. Carry out external validation across centres and scanners, and assess model calibration, bias and failure modes. Bring histopathological and computational thinking together, working with pathologists to design annotation protocols, check that model outputs make morphological sense and interpret explainability analyses. Support the principal investigator in the day to day coordination of the group, including organising team meetings, tracking milestones and keeping work aligned across projects. Act as a regular point of contact for academic, clinical and patient collaborators, and help sustain these working relationships. Contribute to the supervision and support of postgraduate students working on related projects. Contribute to grant and fellowship applications, including preliminary data, methods and supporting documents, and help identify suitable funding opportunities. Lead and contribute to manuscripts, technical reports, and code and data releases. Present the group's work at national and international conferences, seminars, and patient and public engagement events. Keep up to date with the literature in computational pathology and medical AI, and bring relevant new methods into the group. Follow University policies on health and safety, data protection, research integrity and sustainability. Carry out other duties as required, commensurate with the scope and grade of the post. Person Specification Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply. Closing Date: 8 December 2026 The Role This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a major international project funded by the Wellcome Trust and led by Dr Emmanuel Molefi entitled “Diversity in Chronobiology: Discovering dynamics and interactions in chronobiology using multimodal, multiscale, and multinational data”. items.desc: Wanna join the adventure? Loft Orbital flies other people's payloads on standardized satellites, giving our customers a fast, simple, and reliable path to orbit. Reactivity use cases are at the heart of Loft's vision, and we are scaling them: from single-satellite reactive loops, to two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue (a detection from one sensor automatically cueing an acquisition by another), and ultimately multi-satellite scenarios. items.card: Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You
items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

Elle compte environ 550 enseignants, enseignants-chercheurs et chercheurs et 600 personnels administratifs et techniques. Dans le classement de Shanghai et QS, elle apparaît parmi les tous premiers établissements français en termes de performance per capita. Son objectif est d'avoir un impact significatif en matière de recherche, d'innovation et de transfert de technologie tout en irriguant la fonction publique et le monde socio-économique de diplômés rompus à la complexité, capables de produire et transmettre des savoirs. L'ENS de Lyon met ses ressources au service d'une vision ouverte de la société et des enjeux contemporains qu'elle veut éclairer. Son budget annuel est d’environ 160 M €. L'ENS de Lyon est une école dynamique, où la qualité de vie au travail, le développement durable et l’égalité professionnelle représentent des dimensions centrales. Le Poste Persée est une Unité d'appui et de recherche, qui numérise, enrichit et diffuse le patrimoine documentaire au bénéfice de la recherche, principalement à travers le portail de publications scientifiques en accès libre. Persée est engagé dans le GIS CollEx-Persée, inscrit sur la feuille de route nationale des infrastructures de recherche, qui regroupe des bibliothèques de recherche et des opérateurs de l’IST dans le but de développer et d’outiller l’usage par les chercheurs des collections des bibliothèques. Le poste est proposé dans le cadre du programme de Numérisation enrichie de CollEx-Persée, qui en assure le financement. MISSIONS La Mission IA est une mission transverse de l’unité. Elle conçoit et met en œuvre l’application de l’intelligence artificielle aux chaînes de traitement documentaire, de l’expérimentation à la production, afin de livrer à grande échelle des métadonnées fiables, interopérables et réutilisables ( corpus as data ). items.desc:
OUR MISSION

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.



TEAM CULTURE

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. 

 - You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

 - No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

 - We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

 - Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

 - Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates. 
   The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

 - Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

 - We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.


REQUIREMENTS

 - At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

 - As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

 - Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:
   
   - Test Driven Development (TDD)
   
   - Trunk based development
   
   - Continuous integration
   
   - Domain Driven Design


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

 - Large parts of our training pipeline are built on top of Kubernetes.

 - We do not hire for skills in a particular technology or language, but rather ability to learn and mindset, yet experience with these technologies is a plus.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Become part of an AI revolution!

 - 30 days of paid vacation

 - Access to a variety of fitness & wellness offerings via Wellhub https://wellhub.com/de-de/

 - Mental health support through nilo.health http://nilo.health/

 - Substantially subsidized company pension plan for your future security

 - Subsidized Germany-wide transportation ticket

 - Budget for additional technical equipment

 - Flexible working hours for better work-life balance and hybrid working model

 - JobRad® https://www.jobrad.org/ Bike Lease

Note: We welcome applicants at every stage of their career. Your drive and willingness to learn are far more important to us than strict experience requirements.

items.desc: Systems Research Engineer - Distributed Systems / OS / AI Infrastructure Join a global technology organisation carrying out ambitious research into the computing infrastructure behind large-scale cloud and AI platforms. Working across operating systems, distributed computing, networking, storage and accelerator-based hardware, the company is exploring fundamental systems problems and turning the strongest ideas into technology used in real deployments. This research engineering role is a chance to combine original systems research with hands-on building. The work covers scalable infrastructure design, performance engineering, heterogeneous computing and the systems that underpin AI training and inference. The team welcomes people from many systems backgrounds. The position is a full time permanent position based on-site in Edinburgh. Role Overview You will take ownership of open-ended systems research problems: spotting where current infrastructure falls short, proposing new approaches and building working prototypes to test them. Your work will run from defining the problem and forming hypotheses, through implementation, benchmarking and in-depth performance analysis, to publishing at top-tier venues. You will work alongside senior researchers and architects to move proven concepts into production-grade technology. Key Responsibilities Find promising research directions in large-scale computing, then design, build and evaluate new systems, algorithms and abstractions. Profile complex software and hardware stacks to find performance limits, and develop new ways to improve throughput, scalability, efficiency and resource usage. Explore and prototype infrastructure for emerging workloads, including heterogeneous and accelerator-based computing, AI training and serving, large-scale data processing and cloud-native platforms. Write rigorous, original research for leading systems conferences such as OSDI, SOSP, NSDI, EuroSys, SoCC and MLSys. Work with researchers, architects and engineering teams across the wider organisation to validate ideas and turn successful work into deployable infrastructure. Required Experience PhD in computer systems, distributed computing or large-scale AI infrastructure. Open to new PhD Graduates 2026. Solid grounding in computer systems, covering one or more of: operating systems, distributed systems, computer architecture or cloud platforms. Strong systems programming skills in C/C++ (or a similar language), plus Python for prototyping and running experiments. Proven ability to build and assess systems through careful experimental design, benchmarking and profiling. An analytical approach to problem solving and a real curiosity about original systems research. Clear communication skills and comfort working within a multidisciplinary research group. Preferred: Papers published at, or the clear potential to publish at, leading systems conferences. Preferred: Experience in areas such as resource scheduling, performance engineering, heterogeneous computing or ML systems. Preferred: Knowledge of AI infrastructure, such as model serving, distributed training, accelerator platforms or inference optimisation. items.desc: About Sortrace Sortrace is a computer vision company in cleantech. Cameras on waste collection vehicles and trained vision models find material in the wrong waste stream when bins are emptied. Our user platform brings together deviations, images and insights, so our users can see what has been sorted incorrectly. We are live in production in Sweden, and we are a small team that makes decisions quickly. Do you want to work with advanced computer vision and develop AI models that are used in real-world applications? We are looking for a Computer Vision Engineer who wants to help further develop our AI-based image analysis solutions. You will work on model development on an existing technical platform, with a focus on developing, training, evaluating and optimizing computer vision and deep learning models. We are looking for someone with a strong technical interest, a good understanding of modern model architectures and, above all, hands-on experience working with computer vision. About the role As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will work on developing and improving our existing AI models and image analysis solutions. Your tasks will include: Developing, training and optimizing deep learning models for image analysis. Evaluating and further developing existing model architectures. Analyzing and improving the precision, performance and robustness of the models. Working with image datasets, data processing and data augmentation. Experimenting with different model architectures and training methods. Technical problem-solving and continuous improvement of our computer vision solutions. Qualifications We are looking for someone who has: At least 3 years of hands-on experience in computer vision and model development, or equivalent documented experience from professional projects, open source or advanced personal development projects. Experience developing, training, evaluating and optimizing deep learning models for image analysis. A good understanding of different model architectures in computer vision, for example CNN-based architectures and Vision Transformers. Good knowledge of Python. Experience with established deep learning frameworks, for example PyTorch or TensorFlow. Experience working with real-world image datasets, including data processing, data augmentation and model evaluation. The ability to independently adapt and further develop existing models based on technical requirements. We value practical skills and documented results. Your experience does not need to come from a specific job role. What matters is that you have worked hands-on with computer vision and can point to solutions you have developed or contributed to. Nice to have Experience with edge AI and running computer vision models on edge devices or embedded systems. • Experience optimizing models for limited computing capacity, for example quantization and optimizing inference performance. Experience with real-time image or video analysis. Who you are We believe you are a curious, solution-oriented developer who enjoys digging into technical problems. You have a genuine interest in computer vision and deep learning, you keep up to date with developments in the field, and you enjoy turning new ideas into practical improvements. You work in a structured and independent way, but you also appreciate discussing technical solutions and collaborating with others. What we offer At Sortrace, you will have the opportunity to: Work hands-on with advanced computer vision and deep learning. Further develop AI models on an existing technical platform. Explore and apply modern methods and model architectures. Influence technical solutions and contribute your own ideas. Work on interesting technical challenges where model precision, robustness and performance are central. How to apply Does this sound like the role for you? We would love to hear from you! items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Between a conversation and a model sit the formats and tokenizers that every part of our stack relies on. You will help own them, and the tooling around them, so that training, evaluation and production all speak exactly the same language.

You will work across the entire stack, spanning pretraining, post-training and deployment, and your decisions will reach every model we ship.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design, build and maintain core libraries for tokenization and model interfaces.

 - Evolve our formats and tokenizers as models and use cases change.

 - Turn research needs into robust, shared tooling.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong software engineering background, with excellent Python.

 - Excellent understanding of tokenizers: BPE and other tokenization algorithms, special tokens, chat templates, and tokenizer training; ideally hands-on experience with libraries such as tiktoken or Hugging Face tokenizers.

 - Experience building production-grade libraries used by many people.

 - A taste for correctness and attention to detail.

 - Good knowledge of how LLMs are trained and served.

 - Clear communication, low ego, and a collaborative mindset.

 - Nice to have

 - Open-source maintenance experience.

 - Experience with inference engines.




LOCATION AND REMOTE

This role is primarily based at one of our European offices (Paris and London). We will prioritize candidates who either reside there or are open to relocating. We strongly believe in the value of in-person collaboration to foster strong relationships and seamless communication within our team. In certain specific situations, we will also consider remote candidates based in one of the countries listed in this job posting — currently France & UK. In that case, we ask all new hires to visit our local office for the first week of their onboarding (accommodation and travelling covered), then at least 4 days per month




WHAT WE OFFER

items.desc:
Introduction 
 Help shape the future of healthcare AI, where innovation meets trust.
 At CERN, you will develop cutting-edge AI solutions that help prevent disease, improve prediction, and deliver trustworthy healthcare insights. You will work on technologies that make it possible to unlock the value of sensitive data without ever moving or exposing it, enabling collaboration where privacy is essential.
 As part of this role, you will help develop and deploy CAFEIN® , CERN's federated AI platform powering major European healthcare initiatives, including UMBRELLA and AIM-SAFE . You will design advanced federated learning algorithms and secure distributed AI systems that allow models to learn from data across institutions while keeping the data exactly where it belongs.
 Recognised as a lighthouse example of "data stays, AI collaborates" , CAFEIN® combines state-of-the-art federated learning with CERN's unique strengths in trust, open science, GDPR compliance, and international collaboration. The result is a pioneering framework that is redefining how AI can advance healthcare while safeguarding privacy.
 Join us to build AI that learns globally, protects locally, and improves lives.

 Develop and test federated learning software and algorithms.
 Implement and evaluate privacy-preserving techniques, including differential privacy and homomorphic encryption.

 Design and deploy Internet of Things (IoT)-based federated learning architectures.

items.desc: Reasonable is the applied AI research company building formal verification for super-human software development. Correctness guarantees for software developed by humans and machines are no longer impractical or prohibitively expensive. Code generated by AI can be provably correct, rather than plausibly functional. At Reasonable, we are doing the research, training the models, and developing the products required to make this a reality. Achieving this creates a new paradigm for high accountability software development and unlocks the full potential of AI for professional engineers. We’re a compact, talent-dense technical team, with deep domain expertise in machine learning, formal verification and mathematical models of program semantics. Join us to develop the next frontier of formal reasoning and software engineering. Proof follows function. We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Member of Technical Staff specialized in Post-Training and Evaluations to join our Reinforcement Learning & Formal Methods team. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing verifiable reasoning by designing and improving our fine-tuning pipeline. items.desc: At the Faculty of Medicine, Department of Health Science and Technology, a PhD stipend in AI and Medical Imaging for Stroke Prediction and Personalised Care is available for appointment from 1 February 2027 or soon thereafter. The advertised position is one of several PhD and postdoctoral positions established as part of the Centre for AI in Health at Aalborg University. The appointment is for a period of three years. The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD programme in Biomedical Engineering and Neuroscience at the Faculty of Medicine. Who we are: The Department of Health Science and Technology (HST) at Aalborg University is an interdisciplinary research and teaching environment where engineering, medicine and health sciences come together to improve people's lives. As a PhD fellow at HST, you will become part of an international research community with access to experienced supervisors, modern research facilities and strong interdisciplinary collaboration. You will work alongside researchers from a wide range of disciplines and engage with hospitals, industry and public-sector partners to address some of society's most important health challenges. The department is home to approximately 180 academic staff members, around 100 PhD fellows and more than 1,700 students. We offer a stimulating research environment that encourages scientific curiosity, collaboration and professional development. The Faculty of Medicine is committed to preparing PhD graduates for diverse career paths. Throughout your PhD, you will develop advanced research competencies alongside transferable skills that prepare you for careers in academia, industry and the public sector. Towards the end of your PhD, you will be offered dedicated career development support to help you plan your next career step. At HST, our values – Share. Care. Dare. – shape the way we collaborate, support one another and create knowledge with societal impact. Learn more about the department on our website and in our research portal. About the Centre for AI in Health: The Centre for AI in Health is a strategic initiative by the Faculty of Medicine that brings together researchers from the Department of Clinical Medicine and the Department of Health Science and Technology. The centre combines clinical, technical and methodological expertise to advance the development, evaluation and implementation of AI in healthcare. The successful candidate will become part of this interdisciplinary research community. Learn more about the Centre for AI in Health and the centre’s signature projects website. About the Project: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide. While many patients who experience a transient ischaemic attack (TIA) or minor stroke subsequently recover well, a substantial subgroup is at high risk of recurrent stroke and adverse outcomes. Identifying these patients early and ensuring timely intervention remains a major clinical challenge. At the same time, increasing amounts of data are becoming available across the patient pathway. These include prehospital assessments, neuroimaging, vascular imaging, clinical records and longitudinal follow-up data. The challenge is, how to integrate these heterogeneous data sources into clinically meaningful prediction and decision-support tools. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal learning and foundation models create new opportunities to address this challenge. The overall goal of this PhD project is to develop novel AI methods that support early risk stratification, clinical decision-making and personalised care for patients with TIA and minor stroke. The project is part of the Centre for AI in Health signature project AI for Cardiovascular and Stroke Care , which aims to develop AI solutions supporting prevention, prediction and time-critical clinical decisions across the care continuum. The project will leverage multimodal data collected across the patient pathway, including prehospital data, neuroimaging, vascular imaging, clinical records and longitudinal patient data. Particular emphasis will be placed on developing methods that are clinically relevant, robust, explainable and transferable across healthcare settings. Potential research directions include: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Neurovascular Imaging Learning clinically meaningful imaging representations from large-scale neuroimaging data. Multimodal Foundation Models for Risk Prediction in TIA and Minor Stroke Integrating prehospital, imaging, clinical and longitudinal patient data for personalised risk prediction. Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware AI for Neurovascular Decision Support Developing trustworthy AI methods for transparent and reliable clinical decision-making. items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. For more information, visit: www.interdigital.com. Summary This internship will explore neural-network-based representations for the encoding, representation, generation, and manipulation of haptic data. It will build on previous work on Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) for haptics and on probabilistic haptic rendering, with the objective of investigating learned representations that support both compact encoding and controllable transformation of haptic effects. The work will compare architectures such as autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and INRs for sample-based and/or parametric haptic data. Beyond reconstruction, the intern will investigate selected manipulation and generation tasks relevant to haptic authoring, including filtering, interpolation, completion/inpainting, temporal extension, and real-time procedural generation. Candidate methods will be assessed in terms of reconstruction quality, controllability, generalization, and computational cost. The internship may build on recent internal work on haptic effect analysis and temporal extension to explore data-driven approaches for generating missing or extended haptic content. Target use cases may include gaming and haptic authoring tools. The work may lead to prototype software, internal demonstrators, and potentially publication and/or patent contributions. items.desc: Meet Our Recruiter Matthew Mills Managing Director 07493 267443 matthew@mfkrecruitment.co.uk About the Role Machine Learning Engineer - Computer Vision & Deep Learning Salary: £50,000 to £95,000, depending on experience Location: West London Working arrangement: Predominantly office and customer-site based, with some remote working available Employment: Permanent, full-time MFK Recruitment is recruiting Machine Learning Engineers for an innovative UK technology company developing advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning systems for defence, security and other demanding real-world environments. We are recruiting at junior, mid-level and senior levels. Applications are welcomed from talented Machine Learning Engineers at different stages of their careers, with responsibilities and salary determined by experience and technical ability. These positions are specifically focused on computer vision, Convolutional Neural Networks and Transformer-based vision models . They are not general Data Science, NLP or LLM vacancies. The company develops technology across computer vision, machine perception and autonomous systems, translating advanced AI research into reliable products that operate in complex real-world environments. MFK Recruitment has successfully recruited four Engineers to this company over the past five years, and all four remain with the business. This reflects the quality of the technical work, company culture and long-term opportunities available. Machine Learning Engineer role As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will design, train, evaluate and deploy deep-learning models for computer vision applications. Your work will centre on CNNs, Vision Transformers and related architectures for areas such as object detection, tracking, segmentation, classification, localisation and visual perception. This is a hands-on position combining machine-learning research, model development and production software engineering. You will work with complex image and video datasets and help turn recent computer-vision research into accurate, robust and deployable systems. The company is building its team across junior, mid-level and senior levels: Junior Engineers will work alongside experienced colleagues, developing their skills while contributing to real-world computer-vision projects. Mid-level Engineers will take ownership of model development, experimentation and production delivery. Senior Engineers will lead complex technical work, influence architecture decisions and help mentor other members of the team. Responsibilities Design and develop deep-learning models for computer vision applications. Build and optimise CNN and Vision Transformer architectures. Develop models for object detection, tracking, segmentation, classification, pose estimation or related perception tasks. Design and adapt neural-network architectures, loss functions and training strategies. Build reliable data-processing, training, validation and evaluation pipelines. Prepare and manage image and video datasets for model development. Define appropriate evaluation metrics and analyse model performance. Implement and adapt techniques from recent computer-vision and deep-learning research. Optimise models for accuracy, robustness, latency and computational efficiency. Translate research prototypes into maintainable, production-quality software. Support the deployment of models across cloud, desktop and edge-computing environments. Work closely with Machine Learning Engineers, Software Engineers, Researchers, Technical Leaders and customers. Contribute to architecture decisions, technical planning, testing, code reviews and CI/CD practices. The level of ownership and technical leadership expected will reflect the successful candidate’s experience. Essential experience Practical experience developing deep-learning solutions for computer vision through commercial work, academic research or substantial personal projects. Strong understanding of Convolutional Neural Networks. Experience working with Transformer architectures for computer vision or multimodal perception. Experience using PyTorch. Strong TensorFlow experience may also be considered. Strong Python development skills. Experience with areas such as object detection, tracking, segmentation, classification or pose estimation. Experience training, validating and evaluating deep-learning models. Understanding of neural-network architectures, loss functions, hyperparameter optimisation and model-performance evaluation. Experience working with image, video or sensor datasets. An interest in implementing techniques from recent machine-learning and computer-vision research. Good software-engineering practices, including Git, testing and maintainable code. Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills. Desirable experience Real-time computer vision and video analytics. Multi-object tracking, multi-camera systems or multi-modal perception. C++ development. CUDA and GPU …

 Design and execute experiments to identify internal vectors and mechanisms that influence a model's outputs, especially where they appear reflective or pertain to its conception of itself and of other models.

 Publish and communicate research findings through peer-reviewed papers, internal technical reports, and presentations to academic and cross-disciplinary audiences.

 PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a related technical field, or equivalent research experience.

 Preferred qualifications:
 Postdoctoral or equivalent industry research experience in mechanistic interpretability.
 Experience or demonstrated interest working across the cognitive sciences, philosophy of mind, psychology, or neuroscience.
 Experience evaluating concepts of selfhood, metacognition, and theory of mind in artificial systems.

items.title: Machine Learning Scientist (m/f/d)
items.card: About the Role Over the past four years, Oldendorff has rebuilt its IT landscape to cutting-edge standards. In October 2024 we launched our Data & Analytics Department and, with it, the D&A Lab, our machine learning team. As an ML Scientist you will work with our business and D&A teams to turn data into models that drive smarter decisions across our global network and support our goal of carbon neutrality by 2050.
items.desc: Hamburg, Lübeck Founded in 1921, OLDENDORFF CARRIERS combines its history as a German shipowner with the network of one of the world's leading drybulk operators. We are currently operating around 800 owned and chartered vessels and transporting approximately 415 million tons of cargo annually. Our global operations focus on spot business, industrial contracts, and offshore transshipment, primarily carrying iron ore, coal, and agricultural products. Our 4,500 employees from 60 countries include more than 1,000 office-based colleagues across 20 locations and over 3,000 seafarers. Our customers can expect 100% performance. All the way. About the Role Over the past four years, Oldendorff has rebuilt its IT landscape to cutting-edge standards. In October 2024 we launched our Data & Analytics Department and, with it, the D&A Lab, our machine learning team. As an ML Scientist you will work with our business and D&A teams to turn data into models that drive smarter decisions across our global network and support our goal of carbon neutrality by 2050. The Data & Analytics Lab builds models that forecast and explain dry bulk shipping markets: freight rates, vessel movements, commodity flows and operational performance. Our core approach is Bayesian probabilistic modelling: structured, interpretable models that quantify their uncertainty and are benchmarked against standard methods. Our commercial teams use these forecasts in day-to-day decisions. Job Responsibilities Build models. Turn commercial questions into well-specified statistical or ML models and take them from research into production. Explore new methods. Scan the literature, decide what is worth trying and design rigorous experiments to test it. Raise modelling quality. Help define how we validate: backtesting, leakage checks, calibration, model criticism and comparison. Review and support. Review code and models for statistical soundness and engineering quality, and help colleagues grow. Communicate. Explain model behaviour and uncertainty to commercial teams and stakeholders so they can act on it. What You Bring Along A degree in Physics, Computer Science, Math or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience. Holding a PhD is a strong plus. Several years of hands-on experience in applied ML or statistical modelling, including projects you owned end to end. Strong practical grounding in Bayesian inference: hierarchical models, MCMC or variational inference, predictive checks, diagnostics and model comparison. Expert-level Python and the scientific stack (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch), with solid engineering background: Git, testing, packaging, reproducible experiments. Experience taking models into production and keeping them running. Clear communication in English, including with non-technical audiences. Nice to have: A probabilistic programming language: PyMC (preferred), NumPyro or Stan. Gaussian processes: kernel design, hyperparameter inference and scalable approximations. Probabilistic time-series forecasting: state-space and structural models, regime changes, forecast evaluation. MLOps tooling (MLflow, Databricks, Azure, Docker, CI/CD). Causal inference or decision-making under uncertainty. Having peer-reviewed publications in top-tier ML venues or STEM journals is a strong plus. Experience mentoring others. Background in commodities, shipping, energy or financial markets. What We Offer Our corporate culture is special: relaxed and international, open and traditionally with flat hierarchies. Since the very beginning, teamwork and quick decision making have been our success factors. Encouraging our employees to realize their ideas and initiatives is as important to us. Interested? If you want to know more about who we are: Oldendorff. Please contact Sophie Meyer in case of questions. Oldendorff Carriers does not accept paper applications for online postings.

items.desc: Welcome to the application portal for Perplexity Frontier Research . This initiative develops fundamentally new algorithms, models, and evaluations. We are building an automated scientist that can conduct deep research, and provide the best quality service at the lowest cost. We are hiring research scientists for permanent, full-time positions at the initiative. One application covers all focus areas. Please refer to the Perplexity Frontier Research homepage for full details on the initiative and application. When you're ready to apply, please complete and submit the application form. Please carefully follow all instructions. Our focus areas include orchestration, pre-training, continual learning, reinforcement learning, systems, and evaluations. We will be releasing our work as papers, blog posts, and code. We'll evaluate applications on a rolling basis, with priority consideration for submissions received by November 30, 2026. You should write your application without assistance from other humans or AI models. Submitting writing from other humans or AI models as your own will result in permanent disqualification from employment at Perplexity. Qualifications Strong foundations and engineering fluency: probability, optimization, linear algebra and algorithms, plus Python and a deep learning framework, with code that scales. Range: researchers who are proficient engineers, and engineers who are also researchers. Everyone here builds. Evidence of excellence: a result, a system, a proof, or a model that other people use or build on. A preference for understanding, written plainly: controls, ablations, honest baselines, and simple explanations. Agency, creativity, low ego: fix what's broken without being asked, ask questions that are not yet fashionable, and let ideas win on evidence. Helpful, not required: a PhD in a technical discipline, machine learning papers of outstanding quality, prior work in one of our focus areas, or large-scale empirical work with large models. Compensation Range: $220K - $485K

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



The Role

Mistral AI is looking for AI Scientists with deep machine learning expertise and hands-on engineering experience to expand what Mistral's agentic tools can do across the engineering lifecycle across CAE (CFD, FEA etc) and EDA/Semi.. 

Within AI4Engineering Science, your core work is building the pre and post-training data for Mistral's LLMs to reason about and execute real engineering tasks. Alongside this, you'll help shape the agent architectures and harness that let these models operate reliably inside multi-step engineering workflows, not just answer isolated questions.

You'll work closely with domain experts across CAE and EDA to ground this work in how engineers actually work, and with the broader research team to translate that domain grounding into training signal and evaluation benchmarks that measure genuine task competence.

What You Will Do

 - Design pretraining, SFT, and RL data for engineering tasks across CAD, CAE, and semiconductor/EDA

 - Define verifiers and evaluation criteria that capture what "correct" and "high-quality" actually mean for each engineering task, beyond surface-level plausibility

 - Design and improve agent architectures and harnesses: how models plan, call tools, recover from errors, and chain steps together across long-horizon engineering workflows

 - Build evaluation benchmarks and diagnostic tooling to identify where models fail on engineering tasks, and trace those failures back to gaps in data, reward design, or agent scaffolding

 - Collaborate with domain experts across CAEand EDA (and the science and solutions teams more broadly) to identify which engineering workflows are highest-value to target next

 - Contribute to Mistral's broader pre and post-training research, sharing findings and methodology across the science organization

What We're Looking For

 - Fluent English with excellent communication skills, able to explain technical ML and engineering concepts to both engineering and non-technical audiences

 - Deep, hands-on machine learning expertise, particularly LLM development

 - Demonstrated experience running, debugging, and validating real engineering workflows in at least one of CAD, CAE, semiconductor simulation, or EDA. 

 - You write clean, readable Python code and are comfortable in Linux/HPC environments

 - Self-directed, you don't need detailed roadmaps to make progress

 - Low-ego, collaborative, and eager to learn at the intersection of engineering and ML

It would be great if you

 - Have experience building or fine-tuning agentic systems (tool use, multi-step planning, agent orchestration frameworks)

 - Have experience with reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF/RLVR, or preference-based training

 - Have industrial or academic experience with CAE, or EDA tools (e.g. SolidWorks, CATIA, Fluent, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, STAR-CCM+, Cadence/Synopsys/Siemens EDA tools)

 - Have contributed to a large open-source or industry codebase

 - Have publications in engineering and ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, JFM, AIAA, etc.)

 




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

items.desc: Research Scientist in Provenance Research and Forest Tree Breeding (f/m/d) Location: Großhansdorf Start date: At the earliest possible date Organization: Institut für Forstgenetik (FG) Working hours: Full-time / part-time possible Application deadline: 10.12.2026 The Institute of Forest Genetics of the Johann Heinrich von Thünen Institute, Federal Research Institute for Rural Areas, Forestry and Fisheries, is seeking to fill a full-time position (currently 39 hours per week) as a Research Scientist in Provenance Research and Forest Tree Breeding (f/m/d) at its Großhansdorf location, starting as soon as possible. The position combines long-term employment prospects with opportunities for scientific development: 50% of the position is permanent and involves the management and further development of forest genetic field trials, as well as data analysis and data management. The remaining 50% is offered on a fixed-term basis for up to four years and is dedicated to scientific qualification, providing opportunities for independent research, externally funded projects, policy advice, and knowledge transfer. Our research group has a clear mission: to conserve genetic diversity, maintain the growth performance and stress tolerance of broadleaved and coniferous trees, and identify climate-adapted provenances, thereby making an important contribution to securing the future of Germany's forests. At the Thünen Institute of Forest Genetics, we maintain a nationwide network of field trials to assess genetic and phenotypic variation within native and non-native tree species and evaluate the suitability of different provenances under varying site conditions. Our research focuses on adaptive capacity and phenotypic plasticity under current and future climatic conditions. Breeding programmes for selected tree species aim to increase biomass production and the yield of high-quality timber while maintaining wood quality, vitality, and disease resistance. State-of-the-art phenotyping and genomic technologies enable the targeted selection of traits that enhance the economic viability and sustainability of forest management. The position is partly intended to support the successful candidate's scientific qualification and offers, among other opportunities, the possibility of pursuing a PhD. The Thünen Institute collaborates with several universities for this purpose. The fixed-term component of the employment contract is governed by the maximum permissible duration under Section 2(1) of the German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz, WissZeitVG). Employment is governed by the Collective Agreement for the German Federal Public Service (TVöD Bund). Subject to meeting the relevant collective agreement and personal requirements, remuneration will be based on pay grade E13 TVöD Bund , corresponding to an annual gross salary of €62,489.15 to €89,579.84 for full-time employment.
