items.desc: Are you passionate about uncertainty and explainability of large language models in healthcare? We invite applications for two PhD positions on language model reasoning for uncertainty communication and explanation in healthcare. Working at the UvA Join Us! We invite applications for two PhD positions within a new Horizon Europe project ‘Bringing Explainability, Verifiability and Trustworthiness into Multimodal LLMs in the Clinical Practice’. Our team is researching how uncertainty, interpretability and explanations work together to help users judge when to rely on automated decisions. The two successful candidates will join us in advancing the state-of-the-art of techniques for explainability and uncertainty representation in LLM-based reasoning agents, with a particular focus on challenging healthcare data. The research will explore how to best represent and communicate the state of uncertainty of a generative model, as well as how to best extract, organise and communicate supporting explanations of a model’s response. As healthcare data are composed of long, multimodal, structured and unstructured clinical documents, the project will also involve research into long-context reasoning and tool use. The two positions will contribute to these shared research themes, with room to develop distinct questions and approaches. We welcome applicants with a broad range of interests, including natural language processing, explainable AI, machine learning, human-computer interaction, and related fields. Possible directions include, but are not limited to: PhD 1: Structured and explainable representations of uncertainty (e.g., hierarchical Bayesian models, graph-based representations, structure prediction). Mathematical tools for uncertainty representation beyond probability (e.g., possibility measures, belief functions, ranking functions). Cognitively plausible approaches (e.g., from psychology and psycholinguistics) to uncertainty representation and communication. Evaluation of uncertainty quantification usefulness. PhD 2: Conversational and configurable evidence-grounded, uncertainty-aware explanations (e.g., informed by input/data/causal attribution). Explanation methods for long and multimodal clinical records, including how to locate, organise, and cite relevant evidence across documents. Developing XAI tool-using agents. Evaluation of explanation reliability and usefulness (incl., human-centred studies of how explanations support understanding and decision-making) The successful candidates will work in a team together with Wilker Aziz and Vlad Niculae, and two postdocs, within several larger collaboration networks: A Horizon Europe consortium with more than a dozen partner institutes from Europe, UK and Canada The Language Technology lab at the Informatics Institute at UvA The Natural Language Processing unit at the Institute for, Logic, Language, and Computation at UvA Potentially, the ELLIS international doctoral network. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. items.desc: Position description Category Engineering science Contract Internship Job title Internship in Artificial Intelligence-Saclay- H/F Subject Active Learning for Continual Category Discovery Contract duration (months) 6 mois Job Description As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Context : Most image-recognition systems are trained with labeled examples and a fixed list of categories. After deployment, however, new images continue to arrive. Their visual appearance may change because of a different style, camera, or environment, and the system may also encounter categories absent from its initial training data. In continual category discovery a model first receives labeled images from known categories, then successive collections of unlabeled images containing both known and genuinely new categories. It must recognize known categories, form groups for new ones, and retain what it has learned over time. The main challenge is that visual similarity does not always mean that two images show the same category. A known vehicle represented as a sketch may look less similar to photographs of the same vehicle than to a visually close but new vehicle category. The internship will investigate methods to resolve these ambiguities with limited expert feedback. What do we expect from you ? The intern will work on the following tasks : Conduct a literature review on methods for category discovery, visual domain adaptation and active learning Analyze when changed appearances of known categories are confused with genuinely new categories Select informative images for expert feedback under a limited query budget Use this feedback to improve category discovery and maintain categories over time Evaluate the approach against fully automatic and randomly queried baselines This internship offers an introduction to research in machine learning and computer vision. Depending on the results, it may lead to a scientific publication and may be pursued with a PhD focused on a similar topic. # Cea-List Methods / Means Python, PyTorch Applicant Profile Students in their final year of studies (M2 or last year of engineering school) Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning and computer vision Interest in visual representation learning, continual discovery, or active learning Python proficiency in a deep learning framework Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Master 2 Recommended training Informatique avec spécialisation en intelligence artificielle PhD opportunity Oui Requester Position start date 01/03/2027

items.desc: AI Fact-Checking & Response Evaluation Reviewer (German) Mission of the Role Apply independent judgment to identify AI blind spots, reasoning failures, factual inaccuracies, contradictory evidence, and quality gaps. Successful reviewers do not simply validate AI-generated conclusions, they critically evaluate them. Your role is to verify evidence, challenge unsupported assumptions, and ensure AI systems learn from accurate, reliable, and well-supported information. Your expertise will help build more reliable, trustworthy, and human-centered AI systems. About the Role At TrustScale, we believe AI improves when people are willing to question it. As an AI Fact-Checking & Response Evaluation Reviewer, you will evaluate AI-generated responses, verify evidence, challenge unsupported conclusions, and help define the standards that AI systems learn from. Good AI is built on good judgment. TrustScale is seeking experienced Spanish -language professionals to evaluate AI-generated responses, verify factual accuracy, assess supporting evidence, and help define the quality standards that AI systems learn from. As an AI Fact-Checking & Response Evaluation Reviewer, you will review AI-generated content, determine whether conclusions are supported by evidence, identify reasoning gaps, challenge unsupported claims, and help improve the reliability of next-generation AI systems. This is not a traditional annotation, translation, or data-entry role. This role requires individuals who are comfortable questioning conclusions, investigating claims, and making evidence-based decisions—even when those decisions differ from AI-generated recommendations. The strongest reviewers are naturally curious, skeptical of unsupported claims, detail-oriented, and confident applying their own judgment when evaluating information. This is a remote freelance opportunity with flexible hours and payment in USD. items.desc: Job number MED06074 Faculties Faculty of Medicine Departments Department of Infectious Disease Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Hammersmith Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 4 Jan 2027 About the role Supported by BBSRC funding, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the group of Dr Rachel Lai at Imperial College London. This 48-month position, available from January 2027, will investigate how metabolic rewiring and cellular ion fluxes govern innate immune responses and inflammation. Macrophages are essential sentinels of innate immunity, but their dysregulated activation drives severe inflammatory diseases. Macrophage activation requires the convergence of biophysical and biochemical inputs, including acute metabolic shifts, ionic fluxes and oxidative stress. Working within a dynamic, multi-institutional team, you will employ biological and analytical assays and tools to define the physiological checkpoints that determine how macrophages integrate these stress signals and transition from homeostasis to a proinflammatory state. What you would be doing You will lead studies investigating how metabolic and ionic shifts govern macrophage activation, taking responsibility for experimental planning and execution, data analysis and manuscript preparation. Working closely with members of the Lai group and collaborators across the multi-institutional team, you will develop and apply experimental approaches to deliver the project’s scientific aims. You will also supervise and train students, share expertise with colleagues and contribute to the day-to-day running of the laboratory. You will present findings at scientific conferences, prepare reports for research funders and contribute to future grant applications. What we are looking for We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with: A PhD in Immunology, Physiology, Cell Biology or a closely related discipline. Practical experience with primary macrophages or relevant cell-culture models, with strong knowledge of innate immunity and macrophage biology. Experience studying immunometabolism or cellular physiology, including functional immunology and biochemical assays. Ability to lead independent research and work collaboratively, with experience in experimental planning, data analysis and scientific writing. Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable but not essential: measuring cellular ion fluxes or transporter/channel activity, mass spectrometry-based proteomics or metabolomics, bioinformatics or computational analysis of omics datasets, or working with small-animal models. Holding a relevant UK personal licence would also be advantageous. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term post for 48 months. items.desc: Graduate Research/Algorithm Engineer (DSP, Sensor Systems) Whiteley, Fareham (3 days per week in office) Up to £38,000, or up to £42,000 with a relevant PhD Your new company You'll be joining the European headquarters of a high-growth, innovation-led semiconductor business developing next-generation human-machine interface technology. The Research team focuses primarily on capacitive touch sensing, helping to shape advanced touch ICs used within OLED display panels and other future-facing products. This is a highly collaborative R&D environment where ideas move from initial research and modelling through to system validation. Engineers work hands-on across hardware, firmware, software, data analysis and system modelling, using agile methods to solve complex technical problems and turn early concepts into robust product technology. The role is hybrid and you'll be required to work three days per week onsite in Whiteley. You must have a relevant Degree to apply, ideally at PhD level. Your new role This is a graduate or early-career opportunity to build specialist expertise in algorithm engineering, working on RISC-V-based capacitive touch controllers and the physical sensing technology behind them. The position is designed for someone with up to one year of relevant experience who enjoys combining mathematical problem-solving with hands-on experimentation. Working alongside experienced engineers, you'll investigate how physical sensors behave and turn measured signals into reliable algorithms. You'll contribute to touch-detection and signal-processing work involving filtering, calibration and noise rejection, while learning how sensor physics, mixed-signal electronics and digital processing interact in real products. Using MATLAB, Simulink and/or Python, you'll help build models of capacitive sensors, analogue front ends, ADCs and digital signal-processing chains. You'll collect and analyse measurements from prototypes and IC evaluation platforms, compare experimental results with model predictions, and create repeatable simulations and tests to quantify performance improvements. You'll also support algorithm verification, basic fixed-point evaluation and the handover of research into firmware or digital hardware implementation, collaborating with IC design, firmware and system-validation engineers throughout the process. What you'll need to succeed You'll hold a BEng/BSc, MEng/MSc or PhD in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Physics or Applied Physics, Signal Processing or a closely related subject. You'll have sound fundamentals in signals and systems, including sampling, filtering and time and frequency-domain analysis, supported by good numerical and mathematical reasoning. You'll also understand electronic circuits, sensors or physical measurement systems and be interested in how noise, interference and other real-world effects influence performance. Experience gained through university research, projects, placements or personal development involving MATLAB, Simulink or Python will be valuable. Exposure to FIR or IIR filters, FFTs, fixed-point arithmetic, analogue or mixed-signal electronics, ADCs, laboratory instrumentation, SPICE, FPGA or HDL development, Embedded C/C++, microcontrollers or RISC-V would be advantageous rather than expected in depth. Projects involving physical sensors, signal acquisition, sensor fusion or machine learning applied to measured data would be particularly relevant. Above all, you'll be curious, methodical and able to explain your technical reasoning clearly. What you'll get in return You'll join a technically ambitious R&D team where you'll learn directly from experienced algorithm, IC, firmware and validation engineers while applying your academic knowledge to real physical systems and semiconductor products. The base salary is up to £38,000 for a graduate or postgraduate candidate, rising to up to £42,000 for someone holding a relevant PhD. The benefits package also includes private health and dental cover, an EV car salary sacrifice scheme, mental health assistance programmes and wider wellbeing support, alongside hybrid working from modern offices in Whiteley. What you need to do now To find out more or to be considered, please apply directly or get in touch for a confidential discussion with Max Wilcock, Senior Business Director, on 0333 010 5724. At Hays Technology, we're shaping the future of recruitment. As demand for specialist engineering talent continues to grow, we work closely with organisations and individuals to create opportunities where people can make a real impact.

items.desc: As a researcher at Flanders Make, you will help develop next-generation operational intelligence platforms for manufacturing ecosystems. You will research and implement interoperable software frameworks that enable companies to securely exchange and operationalize data, knowledge, and manufacturing capabilities across organizational boundaries. You translate cutting-edge concepts such as data spaces, semantic interoperability, and AI-driven reasoning into real industrial applications, contributing to resilient, sustainable, and flexible manufacturing ecosystems. Your work will support advanced industrial use cases such as Manufacturing-as-a-Service, resilient supply chains, circular value chains, and cross-company operational coordination throughout the product lifecycle. You will contribute to European ecosystem initiatives and frameworks such as Gaia-X, Manufacturing-X, Catena-X, and emerging Digital Product Passport ecosystems. Your role You will join an interdisciplinary research environment where experts in software engineering, AI, systems engineering, optimization, and manufacturing technologies collaborate on real industrial challenges. Together with industrial and academic partners, you will design and validate software frameworks for federated operational intelligence across manufacturing ecosystems. These frameworks enable semantic interoperability, capability matchmaking, distributed decision-making, and operational coordination between companies in complex manufacturing value chains . FUNCTION You will: Design and develop operational intelligence platforms for cross-company collaboration; Translate manufacturing data and knowledge management challenges into reference architectures and semantic models; Implement solutions based on Data spaces, Knowledge graphs, Digital twins and/or Distributed architectures; Develop decision-support and coordination mechanisms (e.g. capability matchmaking, distributed optimization); Contribute to emerging European initiatives such as Gaia-X, Manufacturing-X and Catena-X; Collaborate with industrial and academic partners across Europe; Share results through demonstrators, publications, and presentations. PROFILE You combine strong technical expertise with systems thinking and a passion for applied research. Required: A Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI or related field; Minimum 3 years of industrial experience or research experience; Strong skills in software engineering and modelling; Experience in one or more of the following: Semantic web technologies (RDF, OWL, SPARQL, SHACL, ...) Knowledge graphs / graph-based reasoning (GraphDB, Neo4j, N3, Apache Jena, ...) Data space technologies (EDC-Eclipse Dataspace Components, Solid, ...) Distributed systems and interoperability. Nice to have: Knowledge of Gaia-X, Catena-X, Manufacturing-X or IDS; Experience with digital twins, Asset Administration Shell, or AI reasoning; Experience with industrial data exchange. You are: Passionate about applied research and innovation; Able to bridge research and industry; Proactive and curious in fast-evolving domains; A strong collaborator in international teams. OUR OFFER At Flanders Make, you will: Work on real industrial impact with leading companies; Collaborate with top European research partners; Join an international, interdisciplinary team; Benefit from a flexible and open working environment; Receive an attractive salary with benefits.

Déployer, optimiser et évaluer les modèles sur du matériel neuromorphique (parmi Synsense SPECK, Innatera Pulsar, BrainChip AKIDA, cartes FPGA), y compris les mesures de consommation et de latence par rapport à des références DNN. Contribuer au jeu de données de référence multimodal et aux publications de logiciels open source. Publier dans des conférences et revues de premier plan (CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, IEEE TPAMI, ICRA) et contribuer à l’identification de brevets avec IMRA Europe / AISIN. Votre Profil Compétences Solide formation en réseaux de neurones impulsionnels, vision événementielle ou calcul neuromorphique. Une expérience pratique du matériel neuromorphique est un atout important. Maîtrise de Python et des frameworks d’apprentissage profond (PyTorch de préférence), à l’aise avec le déploiement embarqué. Autonomie, esprit d’équipe et intérêt pour l’interface entre recherche académique et industrie. Our vision is to cut global emissions by 1% by 2050, the equivalent of planting more than half a billion trees every year. We work with leading companies in Italy and abroad. We are a small team that aims for excellence and ownership from day 0. The job in one paragraph Our platform is built for the manufacturing shop floor, making advanced tools accessible to machine operators and engineering teams: a user uploads a part and the technical needs, and the platform reads the tolerances, checks manufacturability, estimates the cost, and runs physical simulations such as cooling and warpage. Deep learning you have trained and debugged yourself; geometric deep learning (graphs, point clouds, neural operators) is a big plus. Gradient boosting and classical statistics as daily tools; uncertainty quantification. Comfortable with simulation data and sensor time series, and with SQL on a real database. Experience with Physics Informed Machine Learning is a strong plus. Manufacturing experience is a plus. English as the working language; Italian a plus. items.desc: LUXUAV designs and manufactures UAV systems in Luxembourg for commercial and security applications across Europe. These systems rely increasingly on onboard perception and AI , developed, trained, and deployed under strict operational, security, and regulatory constraints. We are building an in‑house, sovereign AI capability. All model development, training, and deployment are performed on‑premise, using proprietary and sensitive aerial datasets. This role exists to ensure that the AI embedded in our systems is reliable, controllable, and fit for operational use. We are looking for an Autonomy Algorithm Engineer who will join our team to develop the core state estimation, navigation, control, and mission-level autonomy algorithms enabling fully autonomous UAV flight. This role covers SLAM, Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), Kalman filter design, GNSS-denied navigation, and mission-level behavioral autonomy for operations in contested, GPS-degraded, and communications-denied environments. Responsibilities: State Estimation & GPS-Denied Navigation Design Kalman filter (extended and unscented) and factor-graph estimators fusing inertial, GPS, vision, barometer and radio-based positioning into a robust six-degree-of-freedom pose estimate. Build and tune visual-inertial odometry and visual SLAM (simultaneous localisation and mapping) pipelines: ORB-SLAM3, VINS-Fusion, LIO-SAM or custom (for localisation in GPS-denied and contested environments). Ensure the estimator degrades gracefully and recovers from sensor dropout, GPS jamming and spoofing, including data-driven detection of these conditions to trigger fallback modes. Where it measurably beats the classical baseline, introduce learned components into the estimator: adaptive noise models, inertial error correction or neural feature matching. Flight Dynamics & Trajectory Algorithms Develop motion prediction, trajectory estimation and adaptive filtering for dynamic flight, sensor degradation and environmental uncertainty. Create estimators supporting target tracking, collision avoidance and cooperative swarm behaviour, interfacing with the flight controller over MAVLink/PX4. Apply learned or hybrid dynamics models where physics-based models under-perform: aggressive manoeuvring, aerodynamic interaction or degraded actuation. Mission-Level Autonomy Design mission behaviours - persistent surveillance loiters, autonomous threat-response replanning, return-to-safe-area under sensor failure or loss of communications and adapt them in flight as sensors degrade, threats emerge or target assignments change. Apply reinforcement learning to mission decisions taken on incomplete information (adaptive loiter, sensor tasking, threat response), feeding the estimator's own uncertainty into the decision rather than assuming perfect knowledge of the world. Train those policies in simulation, transfer them to hardware, and measure them honestly against conventional rule-based planners before they fly. Bound every learned behaviour with hard safety limits and a deterministic fallback, so aircraft behaviour stays predictable and certifiable. Develop terminal guidance algorithms for precision terminal-phase operations, including proportional and augmented navigation under high-dynamic flight. Integrate geofencing, airspace deconfliction and dynamic no-fly zone enforcement to EASA U-Space requirements. Integration & Validation Integrate estimation modules with the flight stack (PX4/ArduPilot) and ROS 2 autonomy pipelines. Validate in simulation (Gazebo, MATLAB/Simulink, PX4 software-in-the-loop) and on hardware-in-the-loop rigs before field trials. Deploy any neural inference to onboard computers (NVIDIA Jetson class) within real-time, power and thermal budgets. Analyse telemetry against measurable targets, localisation drift, convergence time, robustness to sensor failure, and iterate. Document designs, derivations and interfaces to support certification. Experience & Skills: Required Master's or PhD in Robotics, Control Systems, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field. 3+ years developing state estimation or autonomous navigation for drones, robotics or autonomous vehicles. Proven Kalman filter design (extended and unscented), sensor fusion architecture and probabilistic motion modelling. Deep knowledge of SLAM — visual, LiDAR or fused — and visual odometry. C++ and C (Eigen, Ceres, GTSAM) and Python (NumPy, SciPy). Working knowledge of machine learning and practical use of PyTorch or similar: building datasets, training, validating, and judging whether a model genuinely generalises. Understanding of reinforcement learning basics — framing a decision problem, designing a reward, choosing between value- and policy-based methods — plus the judgement to recognise when a conventional algorithm is the better answer. items.desc:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're seeking an experienced ML Infrastructure & Acceleration Engineer to own the GPU infrastructure that powers our LLM training and serving, and to make every workload on it faster and cheaper. You'll run our H200 cluster end to end, deploy models to production, and profile and optimize our training and inference pipelines down to the kernel level when it matters. You understand GPUs from the cluster scheduler to the memory hierarchy, you measure before you optimize, and you're motivated by turning raw compute into faster iteration for our ML team. You thrive in environments where infrastructure reliability and efficiency directly shape how quickly research reaches millions of users.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

GPU Cluster & Infrastructure:

 - Own our H200 GPU cluster end to end: Kubernetes and Slurm for training and inference workloads, with multi-tenant scheduling, quotas, and resource isolation

 - Keep large distributed training runs healthy: node health checks, NCCL and interconnect debugging, automated job recovery, and checkpoint management

 - Track and optimize GPU utilization and cost across training and inference, with dashboards and budget alerting

 - Manage infrastructure-as-code and provisioning for GPU environments

 - Define and monitor SLIs/SLOs for cluster availability and production model serving

Deployment & Serving:

 - Deploy LLMs to production using vLLM or SGLang, with CI/CD, model versioning, and safe rollouts and rollbacks

 - Monitor serving latency, throughput, errors, and cost, and act on regressions

ML Acceleration:

 - Profile training and inference end to end (PyTorch Profiler, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute) to find and remove bottlenecks

 - Improve training throughput and MFU: parallelism strategies (FSDP, tensor and pipeline parallelism), communication/compute overlap, mixed precision and FP8, activation checkpointing, torch.compile

 - Optimize inference: quantization (FP8, INT8, INT4), speculative decoding, prefix caching, continuous batching, KV cache tuning, and parallelism layouts

 - Write or integrate fused and custom kernels (Triton, CUDA) where off-the-shelf implementations fall short

 - Build benchmarking tooling so every optimization ships with measured gains

Enablement & Best Practices:

 - Partner with ML engineers and researchers to make training and serving efficient by default

 - Establish best practices for using the cluster and guide teams in their adoption




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years in ML infrastructure, MLOps, HPC, or platform engineering with focus on GPU workloads

 - Hands-on experience operating multi-node GPU clusters with Kubernetes and/or Slurm, including debugging hardware, networking (NCCL, InfiniBand/RoCE), and job failures

 - Production experience deploying and optimizing LLM inference with vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM

 - Proven track record of profiling and accelerating GPU workloads, with measured results in throughput, latency, MFU, or cost

 - Solid understanding of monitoring and observability for GPU systems (Prometheus, Grafana, DCGM, or similar)

 - Naturally curious with a track record of proactively identifying and implementing improvements




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience writing custom kernels in Triton or CUDA, and familiarity with fused kernels such as FlashAttention

 - Performance tuning of distributed training frameworks: FSDP, Megatron-LM, or DeepSpeed

 - Experience with low-precision training and inference (**FP8**, INT4) and model compression for production deployment

 - Deep knowledge of GPU architectures: memory hierarchy, tensor cores, roofline analysis

 - Experience with multi-tenant GPU scheduling and fair-share resource allocation

 - Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, or Triton

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises. La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement. Nous recherchons une Ingénieure ou un ingénieur de recherche et développement en IA embarquée pour rejoindre le département INFRES à Télécom Paris. Le recrutement s’inscrit dans les activités de formation et d’expérimentation en systèmes embarqués et connectés de Télécom Paris, en lien avec le financement CMA5G et les thématiques 5G, Edge AI et Internet des objets (IoT). Le poste vise à concevoir, intégrer et maintenir des plateformes matérielles et logicielles, des bancs d’essai et des démonstrateurs utilisés dans les travaux pratiques, les projets étudiants et les expérimentations menées avec les enseignants-chercheurs. Vos principales missions seront de : Développer et maintenir des plateformes expérimentales en IA embarquée et systèmes connectés. Contribuer aux prototypes, essais et démonstrateurs des activités de recherche et de formation. Participer à la préparation et à l’accompagnement des travaux pratiques et projets. Vous êtes titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac+5 minimum en informatique, électronique ou systèmes embarqués. Vous maîtrisez les langages C/C++ et Python, l’environnement Linux et les outils de gestion de versions tels que Git. Vous disposez de compétences en débogage, tests et intégration matériel-logiciel, ainsi que d’une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais technique. Des connaissances en systèmes embarqués, microcontrôleurs, firmware ou intelligence artificielle embarquée seront appréciées. Autonome, rigoureux et doté d’un bon esprit d’équipe, vous savez analyser et résoudre des problèmes. Vous possédez également de bonnes qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, indispensables pour accompagner les apprenants, préparer des démonstrations et transmettre vos connaissances. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers). items.desc: Thames Valley Integrated Care Board is looking for a Deep Learning Engineer to apply deep learning and machine learning to direct care applications across our Connected Care ecosystem. Connected Care is Thames Valley's expert-led, integrated healthcare-data ecosystem. Since 2016 it has grown from a simple shared care record into a powerful intelligence tool enabling provider collaboration and proactive, direct patient care across the Thames Valley system. This is a direct care function, not a commissioning role. Your focus will be on future disease progression, predictive case finding and population needs — building models that help clinicians and care teams identify risk earlier and target interventions more effectively. You'll create, validate and deploy these models working closely with clinical colleagues, and integrate them with our population health system and data integration platform so that model outputs feed directly back into the information clinicians see. You'll be applying deep learning directly to patient outcomes — helping clinicians spot disease progression and case-find earlier — as part of one of the largest Connected Care programmes in the country, supporting 2.5 million people across Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire. Location: One of Thames Valley ICB's offices Function: Connected Care Infrastructure Directorate: Strategy & Commissioning Designing, developing and deploying deep learning models for future disease progression, predictive case finding and population needs, using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and Azure Machine Learning. Working closely with clinical colleagues to validate models, ensuring they are safe, trusted and clinically relevant before deployment. Integrating models with our population health system and data integration platform so that predictive insights reach clinical records and care workflows. Implementing model monitoring, validation, explainability and drift detection approaches. Building natural language processing (NLP) models to derive insights from clinical and operational text data where relevant. Providing technical leadership on model architecture, MLOps and AI deployment approaches. Ensuring compliance with NHS standards, information governance, clinical safety (DCB0129/DCB0160) and responsible AI principles. We value and promote diversity and are committed to equality of opportunity for all. We believe that the best employers are those that reflect the communities they serve. We want to increase the diversity of our NHS leadership and particularly encourage applications from women, people from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, LGBT communities, younger candidates and from people with lived experience of disability, who we know are all under-represented in these important roles. We are committed to delivering a trustworthy, flexible and responsible staff culture. At our Organisation, our selection process ensures we recruit candidates with the right skills and values. We monitor AI use in applications and remain alert to misuse that misrepresents abilities. You must declare any AI use when submitting your application. The Deep Learning Engineer – Connected Care will play a lead technical role in the design, development, deployment and operational management of advanced deep learning and machine learning capabilities across Thames Valley ICB’s Connected Care ecosystem. The post holder will develop predictive, generative and intelligent analytical solutions to support population health management, operational improvement, commissioning, service transformation and clinical decision support. Working under the direction of the Head of Connected Care – Data Platform, Integration & AI, the post holder will provide technical leadership in the safe, ethical and governed application of deep learning technologies, ensuring compliance with NHS standards, information governance, clinical safety and responsible AI principles. The role will support the delivery of NHS priorities by enabling staff productivity, reducing unwarranted variation, improving access and supporting proactive, person-centred care through intelligent systems that augment decision-making rather than replace professional judgement. You'll be an experienced deep learning / machine learning engineer, comfortable working closely with clinicians to build models that are trusted enough to influence direct patient care. You'll have: A degree or master's in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, software engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent senior experience. Extensive experience designing, training and deploying deep learning or machine learning models in production environments. Experience using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or Keras. Experience with predictive modelling, NLP, time-series analysis and model evaluation. Knowledge of information governance, clinical safety and responsible AI approaches.

Programma ‘Talent voor semicon’ Waar technische innovatie en ontwikkeling samenkomen. Onze uitdaging? Tot 2030 zijn in de Brainport-regio 26.000 extra werknemers technisch personeel in de semicon-sector nodig, waarvan ruim 10.000 mbo’ers. Het Versterkingsplan Microchip Talent, ofwel programma ‘Talent voor semicon’ speelt hierop in door niet alleen nieuwe studenten aan te trekken, maar ook bestaande werknemers te behouden en nieuwe talenten bij- en om te scholen. Door onze krachten te bundelen, benutten we elkaars expertise optimaal en vergroten we onze impact. Summa ICT: Waar technische innovatie en ontwikkeling samenkomen Bij Summa geloven we in een leven lang ontwikkelen. Onze studenten en cursisten ontdekken en benutten hun talenten in het hart van de Brainport-regio, een gebied vol innovatie en technologische vooruitgang. Summa ICT speelt hierin een cruciale rol: wij ontwikkelen vernieuwend ICT onderwijs dat direct aansluit op de praktijk en de behoeften van het bedrijfsleven. Binnen programma ’talent voor semicon’ in Eindhoven bouwen we verder aan een leerklimaat dat talentontwikkeling naar een hoger niveau tilt. En daar hebben we jou voor nodig! items.desc: Lead Computer Vision Engineer / CTO - Edge AI (Football Tech) We are looking for the person who will actually build our system FAIR SYSTEMS makes refereeing decisions in amateur football objective. No VAR room, no TV production, no professional club budget. Just multiple cameras around an ordinary pitch, AI running locally, and a verdict on the referee's watch within seconds. A prototype is running. It works. Now it has to become a product that is reliable every Saturday, in the rain, on a hundred pitches at once. We are looking for one person to make that happen: the person all of our core technical knowledge comes from. What we are building Multiple synchronised PoE cameras around the pitch Local inference on NVIDIA Jetson: detection, tracking, pose estimation 3D reconstruction from image space to pitch coordinates A rules engine that derives match situations from that: offside, goal, throw-in A decision within seconds on the referee's app and smartwatch Privacy by design: raw footage stays on the edge, only events and short clips go to the cloud. No facial recognition. The problems that will land on your desk This is where we are honest, because this is the job: Offside is a millimetre and millisecond problem. Sub-frame timing, calibration that holds up all day, and a system that knows when it is not sure. Multi-camera synchronisation and calibration on pitches that are not level, where the goalpost sits slightly differently every time, and where nobody shows up with a tape measure. Occlusion. Twenty-two players in similar shirts constantly blocking each other. Holding on to tracking identity is harder here than in most industrial applications. Latency budget on edge hardware. Everything that makes your model better makes it slower. That trade-off is yours to make. From demo to pitch. Power cuts, network drops, backlight, fog, a camera that gets knocked sideways. Remote monitoring, OTA updates, fleet management. Calls that have to be explainable. A referee needs to defend the decision to an angry assistant referee. That puts demands on what the system returns, not just on accuracy. Building a data flywheel that makes the system better every match weekend, without needing an annotation team of thirty people. What your role is You are our technical core. Concretely: You define the architecture: edge, cloud, and the dividing line between them You write code yourself, and a lot of it. For now this is not a management role. You make the build-or-buy calls and defend them You translate "the referee has to trust this" into technical requirements You hire the first engineers around you once that is possible, and you decide who they are You have a seat at the table on the direction of the company, not just on execution Who we are looking for Must have: Demonstrable experience with computer vision in production , not just notebooks and papers, but systems running outside the building Multi-view geometry : camera calibration, homography, triangulation, coordinate transformation Multi-object tracking and the mess that comes with it: re-identification, occlusion, ID switches Edge deployment : NVIDIA Jetson, TensorRT, CUDA, DeepStream or equivalent. You know what quantisation does to your accuracy. The ability to hold an entire system in your head: from sensor to API to app You are the owner, not the executor. If something does not work, you are the one who goes and finds out why. Strong plus: Sports analytics, broadcast tech, ADAS or autonomous driving, drones or robotics. All domains where these problems have already been solved once. Experience with hardware in the field : mounting, weatherproofing, power, networking MLOps: annotation pipelines, retraining, model versioning You have been the first or second technical person at an early-stage company before An affinity with football (not required, but fun) What you do not need: A PhD. Where you learned it does not matter to us. Our exact stack. If you have built systems like this, you will pick up our tools in a week. What we offer A market-rate salary and a substantial equity stake. You build something of your own without burning through two years of savings. Full technical autonomy. You decide the stack, the architecture, the approach. Remote within Europe , with one caveat: a system that stands on a football pitch is a system you occasionally have to see standing on that pitch. Expect a handful of days per quarter in the Netherlands, certainly in the beginning. A problem that is genuinely hard, in a market almost nobody is looking at. The big players build for the top of the pyramid. The bottom, where most matches are played and most arguments start, is empty. What we are honest about There is a working prototype and there are pilots, we are building rapidly with a roadmap to 2030. In the first months we experiment a lot on multiple football clubs where amongst some of the largest clubs in the world. There is no engineering team around you yet. You build it. If …

items.desc:
Amazon Ads Brand Safety & Suitability protects advertisers from exposure to unsafe, unsuitable, or policy-violating content across web, mobile app, CTV, and audio advertising inventory. Our mission is to ensure that every ad impression delivered through Amazon's demand-side platform appears adjacent to content that meets advertiser trust expectations while giving brands granular controls to define suitability on their own terms. We operate at the intersection of advertiser trust, publisher quality, and supply integrity.
AI is fundamentally changing the content landscape. Content is now generated at unprecedented scale, faster, cheaper, and increasingly sophisticated. Low-quality, deceptive, AI-generated, and synthetic content evolves in real time, constantly adapting to evade detection. The volume and velocity of new content entering the advertising system has outpaced traditional classification approaches.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist to work on the next generation of AI-powered Brand Safety and Content Classification systems designed to protect advertisers and elevate supply quality at internet scale. This is not a traditional classification problem. You will build systems that make millisecond-level decisions across billions of content signals while continuously adapting to emerging content risks driven by generative AI. You will own the science strategy for LLM-powered classification and semantic understanding, real-time multimodal content evaluation, adversarial ML and adaptive model resilience, proactive risk intelligence and content risk hunting, AI-generated and synthetic content detection, and large-scale abusive content system identification and disruption.
You will define how modern AI separates high-quality advertising inventory from unsafe, unsuitable, and policy-violating content, across web, mobile app, CTV, and audio surfaces.
What Makes This Role Unique
Generative AI has dramatically lowered the cost of producing deceptive, policy-evasive content, and the adversary evolves daily. Your detection systems must reason contextually, adapt rapidly, and generalize beyond previously seen content risk patterns. Static models fail here; you will build living systems that learn and respond in real time. You will do this at internet scale, developing low-latency ML and LLM-powered systems evaluating content safety, brand suitability, misinformation risk, and emerging content risk vectors across massive real-time traffic streams, making billions of decisions per day with single-digit millisecond latency constraints. This role sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and large-scale production engineering, combining deep science, system-wide impact, and business-critical outcomes. The models your team ships directly influence billions of dollars in advertising spend and the trust of the world's largest brands in Amazon DSP.
The Science Problems Are Genuinely Hard
You will tackle challenges including detecting sophisticated AI-generated and synthetic content, understanding nuanced contextual brand risk, identifying coordinated MFA space before they scale, balancing precision, recall, latency, explainability, and fairness, designing adaptive models resilient to adversarial evolution, and leveraging LLMs for semantic understanding in real-time, latency-constrained environments.
Why This Matters
Few roles offer the opportunity to work at the intersection of frontier AI, internet-scale production systems, adversarial environments, and business-critical impact, while tackling open-ended scientific challenges with real-world societal relevance. As AI reshapes the internet, the systems your team builds will define what trustworthy, high-quality digital systems look like for the next decade.
Key job responsibilities
 - Own the science strategy for AI-powered brand safety classification.
 - Build LLM-powered content classification systems making billions of decisions/day at single-digit millisecond latency
 - Develop multimodal evaluation pipelines reasoning across text, images, audio, and video in real time
 - Design adaptive ML systems resilient to adversarial evolution, semantic understanding for nuanced contextual brand risk.
 - Define measurement frameworks and drive continuous improvement
 - Translate research into production, own the path from prototype to deployed model
 - Publish at peer-reviewed venues; contribute to the scientific community in adversarial ML, NLP, and content safety
- Collaborate with software engineering teams to integrate successful experiments into large-scale, highly complex Amazon production systems.
- PhD, or a Master's degree and experience in CS, CE, ML or related field
- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and …

You will examine how mechanical and chemical cues are
items.desc: Job number NAT02328 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 14 Dec 2026 About the role How does a compact nervous system combine different sensory cues to make a life-changing decision? We are seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to join the Chatzigeorgiou Laboratory at Imperial College London and work on a Leverhulme Trust-funded project investigating multisensory decision-making in the larval tunicate Ciona intestinalis. You will examine how mechanical and chemical cues are integrated to control settlement, combining quantitative behaviour, controlled stimulus delivery, whole-brain calcium imaging, neural perturbation and computational analysis. With only 231 neurons and a synaptic-resolution connectome, Ciona offers a powerful opportunity to uncover general principles of sensory integration in a minimal chordate nervous system. What you would be doing Lead experiments defining how mechanical and chemical cues interact to regulate larval swimming, settlement and metamorphic commitment in Ciona intestinalis. Develop high-throughput behavioural assays using millifluidic or microfluidic arenas and quantitative tracking. Perform whole-brain calcium imaging during precisely controlled unimodal and multimodal stimulation. Analyse behavioural and imaging datasets to identify nonlinear integration, cue hierarchy and temporal decision dynamics. Use targeted optogenetic and/or chemogenetic perturbations to test causal circuit mechanisms. Generate transient transgenic Ciona larvae and contribute to animal culture and experimental workflows. Publish findings in high-quality international journals and share data and code through open, reproducible workflows. Present work at national and international conferences and workshops. Work closely with the PI, students and project collaborators across experimental and modelling work packages. Help supervise students and contribute to the growth of the Chatzigeorgiou Laboratory at Imperial. What we are looking for We are looking for a scientist who has: A PhD in neuroscience, neurobiology, animal behaviour, physiology, quantitative biology or a closely related discipline. Evidence of high-quality research and strong publication potential or a publication record appropriate to career stage. Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in rigorous experimental design and statistical analysis. Practical experience in fluorescence microscopy, functional imaging and/or calcium imaging. Practical experience working with an experimental model organism. Experience in quantitative behavioural analysis and handling complex datasets. Enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research spanning behaviour, neurobiology, imaging and computation. Strong communication, organisational and collaborative skills. Desirable experience includes: Experience with microfluidics or controlled mechanical and chemical stimulation. Experience in transgenesis and genetically encoded calcium indicators. Experience working with Ciona, marine organisms or other non-traditional model systems. Experience in computer vision or machine learning, such as DeepLabCut, and analysis of calcium-imaging data. What we can offer you Opportunity to work on an ambitious Leverhulme Trust-funded project addressing fundamental questions in sensory neuroscience, behaviour and evolution. Access to a uniquely tractable chordate model, whole-brain imaging, controlled-stimulus platforms and connectomic resources, with close interaction between experimental and modelling researchers. The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . This is a full-time post (35 hours per week). This role is for a fixed-term contract for 3 years from 1 March 2027 If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr. Marios Chatzigeorgiou – m.chatzigeorgiou@imperial.ac.uk . items.desc: Hours of work: Full-time Tenure: Permanent A Research Coordinator position is available in the group of Professor. Andrew Cooper at the University of Liverpool. The Research Coordinator will bring their expertise to strengthen the relevant areas of our research programme, particularly by providing specialist advice and leadership in artificial intelligence and machine learning for functional materials discovery . This will include managing the teams working on the development and application of advanced AI methods for scientific research, including machine learning, large language models, machine reasoning, knowledge representation, and optimisation algorithms. A PhD in Chemistry, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Physics or Materials Science and expertise in AI and machine learning as applied to scientific problems are essential, together with the ability to lead a team of researchers working on projects in this area. You will oversee and coordinate the AI and machine learning aspects of our research programme, while also ensuring integration with the other research areas in the Cooper Group (i.e., chemistry, robotics, automation and materials discovery). In addition, the post-holder will contribute directly to the research programme through the development and application of advanced AI methods, help identify and develop new research opportunities, coordinate access to national computing resources, and support the preparation of high-quality research publications and funding applications. Beyond the research, you will take responsibility for supporting the preparation of research publications, reports and grant applications, while contributing to the recruitment, supervision and mentoring of PhD students and postdoctoral researchers. You will also help manage the computational resources and software infrastructure associated with this research area, ensuring that projects are delivered to the highest standards and that research findings are disseminated effectively and in a timely manner. items.desc: Internship – Time Series Foundation Models for Forecasting Duration: 6 months Start date: April 2027 (flexible) Location: Paris 7e ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. Your Role How Much History Does an LLM Need? Memory-Augmented Language Models for Financial Text Financial text about a company accumulates continuously over years. Today's language models typically process this history either by feeding in as much as fits in their context window, or by splitting it into independent chunks. Both approaches have well-known limitations, especially as history grows long and needs to stay historically consistent. This internship explores an alternative: building a compact, incrementally updated memory of a company's disclosure history, one that is updated as new documents arrive rather than fully re-read each time. The central question is twofold: Does a long disclosure history help understand or predict a company's future, compared to only recent information? If so, what is the best way to represent and maintain that history over time in a language model? Key Responsibilities Design and compare strategies for incrementally updating a compact memory representation as new documents arrive. Build comparison baselines, including a retrieval-based system. Evaluate the resulting representations both for faithfulness to the source documents and for usefulness on a downstream financial prediction task. Read and implement research papers (a significant part of the work). Your Skills Required Final-year engineering or Master's student in NLP, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, or Computer Science. Strong Python skills, including PyTorch. Solid understanding of LLMs and sequence modeling. Ability to read and implement research papers. Fluent English Appreciated Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, agent memory systems, or reinforcement learning for LLMs. Interest in financial applications (a bonus). Prior knowledge of finance is not required. French is a bonus. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT We are continuously striving to be an equal opportunity employer and we prohibit any discrimination based on sex, disability, origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, or religion. We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success. CFM is a signatory of the Women Empowerment Principles.

items.desc: CMP Phar.ma Srl, nata nel 1969, produce macchine per l'ispezione farmaceutica e l'industria veterinaria. Nel 1982 diventa la prima società al mondo a lanciare sul mercato una macchina automatica per l'ispezione a raggi laser di fiale; in breve tempo, grazie ad una costante attività di ricerca e sviluppo, si consolida sul mercato internazionale perfezionando l’offerta con una vasta gamma di ispezionatrici automatiche e semi-automatiche per il controllo di fiale, flaconi, siringhe pre-riempite, sacche infusionali e liofilizzati. Nel 2018 Marchesini Group firma l’acquisizione della maggioranza di CMP Phar.ma, grazie alla quale arricchisce ulteriormente il suo già amplissimo portafoglio prodotti. L’obiettivo è di rispondere a 360 gradi alle più diversificate richieste della clientela anche nell’ambito dell’ispezione e del controllo e di consolidarsi come produttore di linee complete in grado di realizzare e monitorare tutto il processo di confezionamento dei farmaci. L’acquisizione di CMP Phar.ma è stata resa possibile anche grazie all’importante contributo del partner SEA Vision, che ha compartecipato all’operazione. Posizione: Per il nostro stabilimento di Costabissara siamo alla ricerca di un* AI / Computer Vision Engineer da inserire all'interno dell'area Pharma. La risorsa si occuperà della progettazione, dello sviluppo, dell'addestramento e dell'ottimizzazione di modelli di Deep Learning applicati a sistemi di visione artificiale, contribuendo alla realizzazione di soluzioni innovative e alla loro integrazione in ambienti produttivi. Cerchiamo un professionista con almeno 3-5 anni di esperienza nello sviluppo di soluzioni di Computer Vision e Deep Learning, con solide competenze di programmazione e una concreta esperienza nella gestione di progetti dalla fase di ricerca e sviluppo fino al rilascio in produzione. La persona lavorerà su progetti applicativi, affrontando problematiche legate all'analisi di immagini, all'addestramento dei modelli, alle prestazioni e all'ottimizzazione dei sistemi di inferenza. Requisiti: Esperienza in Deep Learning e Computer Vision Solida esperienza di almeno 3 anni nello sviluppo e nell'addestramento di modelli di Deep Learning per applicazioni di visione artificiale. Capacità di lavorare con dataset reali, anche limitati o scarsamente annotati. Conoscenza delle tecniche di Data Augmentation e delle metodologie per migliorare le prestazioni dei modelli in presenza di dati non ideali. Esperienza nella valutazione delle prestazioni dei modelli attraverso metriche specifiche e metodologie di validazione. Sviluppo e integrazione in produzione Esperienza concreta nell'integrazione e nel deployment di modelli di Intelligenza Artificiale in ambiente produttivo, sia per la fase di training sia per quella di inferenza. Capacità di ottimizzare i modelli con particolare attenzione alla riduzione della latenza e al miglioramento delle prestazioni computazionali. Esperienza nello sviluppo e nel deployment di applicazioni cross-platform in ambiente Windows e Linux. Capacità di redigere report tecnici dettagliati per ciascun caso d'uso, documentando metodologia adottata, caratteristiche dei dataset, processo di training, risultati e metriche di valutazione. Linguaggi e tecnologie Ottima conoscenza di C++ (standard C++14/17 o superiori). Ottima conoscenza di Python. Ottima padronanza delle librerie e dei framework: PyTorch OpenCV TensorRT LibTorch Preferibile conoscenza della programmazione CUDA e degli strumenti e framework dell'ecosistema NVIDIA. Completano il profilo Approccio analitico e orientamento alla risoluzione di problemi complessi. Laurea in scienze informatiche/ingegneria informatica, matematica o fisica. Autonomia nella gestione delle attività di sviluppo e ricerca. Capacità di lavorare in team multidisciplinari. Precisione, metodo e attenzione alla qualità del codice e della documentazione tecnica. Attitudine alla sperimentazione e all'aggiornamento continuo sulle tecnologie di Intelligenza Artificiale. Altre informazioni: Entrerai a far parte di una realtà internazionale e tecnologicamente avanzata, in continua evoluzione, dove potrai contribuire concretamente allo sviluppo di progetti complessi per importanti clienti del settore farmaceutico. Offriamo: Inserimento in un contesto tecnologicamente stimolante e orientato all'innovazione. Opportunità di lavorare su progetti concreti di Intelligenza Artificiale e Visione Artificiale. Contratto a tempo indeterminato. Orario full time: dal lunedì al venerdì, 08:00–12:30 / 13:30-17.00. Ticket restaurant giornalieri. Inquadramento e trattamento economico commisurati all'esperienza e alle competenze maturate. Il presente annuncio è rivolto ad entrambi i sessi, ai sensi delle leggi 903/77 e 125/91 e a persone di tutte le età e tutte le nazionalità, ai sensi dei decreti legislativi 215/03 e 216/03.

items.desc: Bristol, London, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, York Job Summary The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) works on issues that affect daily life across England. Our work covers the environment, farming, food production, rural communities, animal health and protection from natural risks such as flooding. The Farming Directorate is responsible for delivering a major part of the UK Governments programme of restoring nature, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving animal health and welfare as well as maintaining sustainable food production. By changing how government works and the offers we make available to farmers, we are: Improving productivity across the farming sector Re-purposing funding to focus on the environment Working with farmers to deliver the targets set out in the Climate Change and Environment Acts We have an opportunity to join the Metrics and Reporting team within the Evidence and Analysis function. The team's work helps the directorate understand outcome progress, evidence decision-making and meet reporting requirements. The post holder will help to develop and maintain both internal reporting processes and external publications, including the Farming Sector Environmental Objectives and official statistics on the Farming Investment Fund (FIF). They will gain experience in programme evaluation, government statistics and work with modern analytical techniques, alongside data science and data engineering teams. This position would be suited to analytically-minded candidates interested in deriving robust, impactful analysis on directorate and environmental outcomes from real-world information. We recognise that people with protected characteristics may experience challenges in the job market and in career progression. We want to make sure that everyone has equal opportunities. Defra has many staff networks and trade unions that represent staff and help to positively change how we work. We support flexible working and want to ensure that our staff have a good work-life balance. We provide support for employees with disabilities and health conditions. If you need support at interview, please let us know so that we can provide this. We are keen to make our workforce as diverse as possible, and we hope to attract applications from underrepresented groups. items.desc:
We are looking for a passionate, talented, and inventive Applied Scientist with a strong machine learning background to help build industry-leading language technology powering Alexa for Shopping, our AI-driven search and shopping assistant, helping customers with their shopping tasks at every step of their shopping journey.
This innovative role focuses on developing and optimizing language model-powered (LLM/SLM) conversational experiences. The core emphasis is to get the best performance out LLMs/SLMs via careful and methodical instruction design, contextual grounding, informed choices of MCP tools and agent/multi-agent systems, context engineering, model fine-tuning, evaluation frameworks, and experimentation to systematically improve quality, robustness, and customer impact. The work combines scientific rigor with product intuition to systematically raise the bar for conversational AI performance at Amazon scale.
Our mission in conversational shopping is to make it easy for customers to find and discover the best products to meet their needs by helping with their product research, providing comparisons and recommendations, answering product questions, enabling shopping directly from images or videos, providing visual inspiration, and more. We do this by leveraging advanced analytics, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), A/B testing, causal inference, and data-driven insights to continuously improve our systems.
Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Scientist on our team, you will develop and maintain LLM agents, including automated eval pipelines, LLM-as-a-judge methodologies, rubric design, and dataset curation to measure nuanced aspects of response quality.
You will partner with the wider org to experiment with techniques such as retrieval augmentation, context enrichment, prompt decomposition, and model fine-tuning or post-training strategies, if and when applicable. Where latency and cost constraints demand it, you will lead post-training of small language models (SLMs) — including supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation, and distillation — to deliver low-latency conversational and shopping experiences.
You will apply applied machine learning and deep learning techniques as last-mile improvements to shopping experiences, that might span ranking, relevance, personalisation, and multimodal understanding. You will design and evaluate agentic architectures that balance the needs of diverse shopping use cases, making principled choices across paradigms such as single-agent and multi-agent systems, memory management strategies, and tool orchestration to optimise for quality, latency, and reliability at scale. You will leverage petabytes of data and identify opportunities to leverage machine learning models aimed at making conversational systems more performant.
A day in the life
Perform hands-on analysis of large-scale multimodal interaction datasets to develop insights into how customers engage with conversational AI systems and how to improve response quality and customer experience.
Use statistical methods, experimentation, and data-driven analysis to develop scalable approaches for measuring, evaluating, and optimizing large language model (LLM)-based shopping assistant systems, leveraging structured and unstructured contextual signals.
Conduct deep-dive analyses to identify opportunities for improving conversational relevance, grounding, customer satisfaction, and downstream business impact.
Collaborate with Product management and Engineers to translate analytical insights into production systems, working closely on model evaluation and deployment.
Communicate results and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences, including through presentations, written reports, and data visualizations.
About the team
The Alexa for Shopping Science team, based in London, works alongside ~150 engineers, designers and product managers, shaping the future of AI-driven shopping experiences at Amazon. The team works on every aspect of the conversational AI system, from making it agentic, enabling customers to set price alerts or empower the assistant to act on their behalf and automatically purchase products when the price is right, to understanding multimodal user queries and generating answers that combine text, image, audio and video, including deep research reports that scour the web and the Amazon catalog to provide detailed and personalised shopping guidance. We utilize and advance state-of-art techniques in the fields of Natural Language Processing, gen AI, Information Retrieval, Machine/Deep Learning, and Data Mining. We validate our work by actively participating in the internal and external scientific communities.
- Master's degree or above in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields

Research Assistant - FCLG Operationalisation Project 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Research Assistant - FCLG Operationalisation Project
 100%, Singapore, fixed-term 
 Drucken 
 The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.
 Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .
 The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.
 Project background
 The “Mind the density - Quantifying design scenarios that soften high-density living” project is a multi institutional and multi disciplinary project with researchers from the Singapore-ETH Centre, National University of Singapore, and the Singapore Management University.
 Previous projects at the Singapore-ETH Centre targeted the lack of data convergence in urban planning and the application of the latest developments in geospatial data science to urban design and planning. Data commonly reside in silos (across different fields, agencies, and stakeholders), and analytical and AI methods do not fully exploit these multimodal datasets. Their research outputs tackled this problem directly by releasing open, converged datasets and developing methods that leverage different dimensions such as text, subjective indicators and imagery. In addition, work on design data semantics enhanced the meaning of data science applications for particular urban design solutions and actions. Moreover, they also investigated how the built environment affects people's behaviour, cognition, perception and emotion. They focused on the human and building scale, examining how indoor and outdoor environments influence experience.
 This project integrates these expertise to operationalise evidence on human responses to high-density environments in Singapore. The project will generate large-scale preference data across controlled design conditions, and will conduct focused empirical studies of behavioural, cognitive, physiological and subjective responses. This combined evidence will support agency decision-making on design interventions that improve experience in high-density environments, identify thresholds, compare interventions, and produce decision-support evidence, planning parameters and implementation guidance.
 Lead PI: Filip Biljecki (NUS) and Zdravko Trivic (NUS)
 Job description
 As a research assistant, you will be involved in a multidisciplinary and collaborative research study to operationalise human-centred urban analytics and cognition methods as evidence-backed decision support and implementation guidance for high-density urban form and design interventions. You will integrate analytical methods to quantify how urban form and design interventions affect perception, cognition and behaviour, producing URA-relevant guidance for high-density environments. You will also be involved in large scale field data collection through online surveys and lab-based physiological studies, and collaborations with researchers from various disciplines and government agencies stakeholders. You will do this under the guidance of Assoc. Prof. Filip Biljecki (National University of Singapore) and Asst. Prof. Matias Quintana (Singapore Management University).
 Your key responsibilities will be:
 1. Co-developing the research of work package 1. This work includes, a.o.:

 Co-developing applications, features, datasets, and use cases on public datasets of street-view imagery and longitudinal cohort studies.
 Co-developing and publishing journal and/or conference articles.
 Presenting your research to international audiences and visitors.

 Participating in and contributing to team meetings.

 Presenting the project internally and externally, and preparing material for such presentations.
