items.card: You Will Make an Impact You will research and build models for noisy, rapidly changing real-world data, including: detecting weak signals in noisy environments; filtering, denoising and signal pre-processing; spectral and time-frequency analysis; modelling non-stationary signals; signal detection and statistical estimation; adaptive filtering and online learning; combining multiple noisy information sources;
items.desc: About VNT Technologies VNT Technologies is a quantitative research and technology firm focused on developing algorithmic trading infrastructure. We combine mathematical modelling, software engineering, and low-latency technologies to build systematic trading architecture for financial markets. If you're excited about solving hard technical problems, extracting meaningful signals from noisy data, and seeing your research make an impact, you belong with us. Why Join Us Great minds think alike : a small, exceptional team with opportunities to learn from talented peers. Real ownership from day one: your work has visible impact on the business. Hard, interesting problems: a fascinating business domain with no shortage of deep challenges in quantitative research and low-latency engineering. High performance - high rewards: We set ambitious goals, high standards and recognize strong results with highly competitive base salary and bonus. About the Position VNT Technologies is looking for an exceptional Signal Processing Researcher with a strong background in signal processing, statistical modelling, or related fields. No experience in finance or trading is required. We are particularly interested in people who have worked with: radar or sonar systems; audio and speech signal processing; active noise cancellation; digital signal processing (DSP); telecommunications and wireless signals; sensor fusion; signal pre-processing and post-processing; detection, estimation or tracking problems. Our work involves extracting weak and short-lived signals from extremely noisy data. Many of the underlying problems may be closer to radar, communications and signal processing than to traditional finance. How You Will Make an Impact You will research and build models for noisy, rapidly changing real-world data, including: detecting weak signals in noisy environments; filtering, denoising and signal pre-processing; spectral and time-frequency analysis; modelling non-stationary signals; signal detection and statistical estimation; adaptive filtering and online learning; combining multiple noisy information sources; identifying regime changes and unusual events; evaluating whether observed patterns are real, robust and exploitable. You will work with large real-world datasets and have the ability to test ideas quickly. Successful research can move from an initial hypothesis to a live production system. What You Bring to the Team We care more about how you think than about your previous industry. You may be a strong fit if you have experience in one or more of the following: digital signal processing; radar or sonar; audio processing and active noise cancellation; wireless communications; sensor fusion; control systems; applied mathematics or statistics; physics or electrical engineering; time-series modelling. What We're Looking For strong mathematical and analytical ability; experience working with noisy real-world signals; strong Python, MATLAB, C++ or similar technical skills; ability to design rigorous experiments and distinguish genuine signal from noise; curiosity and willingness to apply ideas outside your previous domain. What Does Not Matter Years of experience — mastery takes time, but we don’t put arbitrary numbers on it. Your previous industry — finance or trading experience is not required. The bar is high, but don’t be intimidated — different people shine in different ways. If you’re curious, driven, and enjoy solving meaningful problems, you’ll fit right in. Life at VNT Technologies Diverse paths, shared passion. Some of our team are Cambridge and Oxford graduates, International Olympiad medallists and PhDs. Others built exceptional expertise through hands-on experience and deep curiosity. What unites everyone is a passion for solving hard problems. Work-life balance matters. We expect a significant contribution from every team member, and we don't believe overworked or burned-out people can give us any edge. A friendly, collaborative and flat culture where good ideas can come from anyone. What We Offer Base salary range: €5,000 - €10,000 gross per month based on your qualifications, competencies, and professional experience. Year-end performance-based bonus. Small but important perks — parking, private health insurance, high-end equipment, tooling of your choice, and more. Regular team buildings to strengthen our teamwork. Real ownership and real impact from day one. A friendly, collaborative culture where good ideas can come from anyone. Office at the heart of the business district - “Europa” Business Center, Vilnius, Lithuania. We look forward to hearing from you. Submitting an application acknowledges that VNT Technologies may contact previous employers and professional references with your consent during the evaluation process before the final decision about hiring is reached.

items.desc: KTP Associate - Data Scientist (Engagement Analytics) The Role The University of Stirling’s Marketing, Entrepreneurship and People subject group at the University of Stirling Business School is seeking an ambitious and talented KTP Associate to join a 24-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP), in partnership with Kortext. Please note that this vacancy is being advertised by Kortext on behalf of the University of Stirling. The successful candidate will be employed by the University of Stirling, which will manage the recruitment process, selection activities and employment contract. Applications will be submitted through the KTP recruitment scheme and will be reviewed and managed by the University of Stirling. This exciting role offers the chance to embed cutting-edge academic thinking into commercial practice, supporting the evolution of Kortext stream into a second-generation engagement intelligence and analytics platform designed to support successful student outcomes through maximising student retention. Key Responsibilities Conduct Diagnostic and Competitor Analysis - undertake a comprehensive review of Stream 1.0 and analyse competitor approaches to establish a robust technical and commercial foundation for future development Design and Develop the Stream 2.0 Framework - create a proprietary, research-led framework that identifies, measures and operationalises student engagement risk indicators Build Predictive Modelling Solutions - translate psychological and behavioural research into observable data signals, computational logic and scalable predictive models Lead Research-to-Model Implementation - establish a structured pipeline that converts academic research findings into commercially viable and technically robust solutions Validate and Optimise Processes - develop and implement scalable validation processes to ensure models are accurate, reliable, actionable and aligned with institutional practices Drive Business Integration and Stakeholder Alignment - work closely with Kortext, higher education institutions and internal stakeholders to ensure Stream 2.0 delivers meaningful customer value and is fully embedded within operational processes Manage Academic Collaboration and Knowledge Exchange - collaborate with University of Stirling academics, contributing to research dissemination, knowledge transfer activities, publications and conference presentations Essential Criteria Masters (or equivalent) or bachelor’s degree in a quantitative subject (mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science) An ability/aptitude to develop algorithms and use tools and software relating to data science An ability to interpret and analyse data, draw conclusions and make recommendations Strong interpersonal skills with an ability to communicate and relate to a variety of professionals at different levels Ability to explain complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences Evidence of commitment to new skill development and continuous learning Demonstrable ability to self-manage complex tasks and deadlines Desirable Criteria A PhD in a highly quantitative discipline (mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science) Experience of using a wide range of research methodologies (including qualitative approaches) in developing research projects Experience of project management Project description Deliver a scalable, next-generation engagement analytics platform that pinpoints student risk earlier and more accurately – enabling faster intervention, better outcomes and stronger support for every learner. About the business Founded in 2013, Kortext is a global leader in digital learning and student engagement solutions. We support institutions worldwide with our AI-powered, cutting-edge content discovery and study products, market-leading learner analytics, and streamlined workflows. items.desc: About The Hiring Team Level Infinite is Tencent’s global gaming brand. It is a global game publisher offering a comprehensive network of services for games, development teams, and studios around the world. We are dedicated to delivering engaging and original gaming experiences to a worldwide audience, whenever and wherever they choose to play while building a community that fosters inclusivity, connection, and accessibility. When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it. Job Title: Systems Engineering Opportunities: Mechanical Systems Engineer or Engineering Data Scientist Salary: £41,593 + Dependent Upon Experience Location: Peterborough, UK Benefits 25 days annual leave Up to 10% Bonus Contributory pension scheme - Caterpillar will double the employee's contribution up to 10% Contributory share scheme - Caterpillar will match 50% of the employee's contribution. Optional flexible benefits including access to health and dental care plans, EV car lease, holiday purchase. Please note these roles require a 5-day per week on site presence. One application, two opportunities The Systems Engineering department within IPSD-M (Industrial Power Systems Division – Medium Engines) in Peterborough is recruiting into two teams: the L4M Mechanical Systems team and the Engineering Data Systems (EDS) team. We invite you to apply based on your interest in either or both roles. After an informal conversation we will agree with you on which role best fits your skills, experience, and ambitions and we’ll then invite you to a targeted selection interview for that role. About The Systems Team Our Systems teams own how our engines and powertrains perform, last and deliver customer value, from setting requirements at the start of a New Product Introduction (NPI) program through to data-driven services that support products in the field. We work alongside system and virtual and physical validation specialists in Peterborough and with engineering colleagues in the US, China, and India on diesel, hybrid and alternative fuel powertrain projects. With many exciting projects in flight, demand on the team is high. L4M Mechanical Systems team The Mechanical Systems team is accountable for mechanical system functionality, reliability and durability for NPI programs and current production engines. The team is involved from the start of a program, setting requirements and technical objectives, to planning and delivering validation on engine and machine, with a focus on early risk identification, robust mitigation and technical issue management. Engineering Data Systems (EDS) team The EDS team blends big data analytics with mechanical engineering expertise to help product development teams extract maximum knowledge from test, field, and simulation data, and works with Service and Aftermarket teams to deliver digital services that improve the performance, life and ease of maintenance of our products. The Opportunity Mechanical Systems Engineer (L4M) Identify mechanical system integration requirements, cascade Product Objectives to Technical Objectives and make system-level trade-offs Create engine system FMEAs and facilitate system and component Design Verification Plans (DVP) Plan and manage engine build and test programs, on our test facility and in application with customers Review engine and machine data from validation tests and the field, and support technical issue resolution Engineering Data Scientist Apply data science techniques to large engineering datasets, including time series, to resolve product and business problems Build visualisations, web apps and dashboards that put frequently used analytics in engineers' hands Package analytics as condition monitors for production and deploy physics-based reduced order models Communicate and document analytical solutions, and help shape future data infrastructure and tools What We Are Looking For We welcome mechanical or controls engineers who are passionately data driven, and data scientists, mathematicians, physicists or software engineers who are passionate about mechanical engineering or mechatronics. All candidates will bring: An engineering or STEM degree and/or relevant experience in an engineering field Experience of industrial power systems, engines, or machine applications A systems approach to problem solving and product development The ability to interrogate data and draw sound engineering conclusions Good written and verbal communication, and confidence presenting to peers and customers Ownership and initiative, working autonomously and as part of a team Desirable experience for each role includes some of the following; you do not need all of them: Engine design, development or simulation; industrial diesel engines Code development Planning validation and test requirements; DFMEA creation and facilitation Database management and SQL query Root cause investigation, 6 Sigma, Lean and continuous improvement …

items.desc: Data Scientist // St Albans // £100k package (£60k base salary + ~£40k bonus) Love cricket? How about getting paid to predict it? 🏏 I'm working with a sports analytics company using AI, machine learning and advanced statistics to predict cricket matches across the world. From predicting match winners to analysing player performances and calculating live probabilities as the action unfolds! They're a small, incredibly talented team with access to some of the best cricket data in the world. And they're looking for another Data Scientist to join them! What would you be doing? You'll be using Python, statistics and machine learning to improve their proprietary cricket prediction models, answering questions like: What's the probability of India beating England? How does a player's performance change depending on the opposition or venue? How many runs is a team likely to score as a match unfolds? How can we make live match predictions more accurate? You'll have the freedom to experiment with new techniques, build your own models and take ownership of projects from idea through to production. They're also genuinely AI-first, using tools like Claude and ChatGPT extensively to accelerate development. What are they looking for? Strong Python programming skills. Solid mathematics, probability and statistics knowledge. Experience with statistical modelling and/or machine learning. MSc or PhD in Maths, Physics, Statistics, Data Science or a similar quantitative subject (or equivalent experience). Hands-on experience with AI coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. Experience with Bayesian statistics, PyTorch or scikit-learn would be a bonus. And if you love cricket, even better! They're also open to exceptional recent PhD graduates with interesting projects to demonstrate. Why join? Exceptional earning potential Work on cricket every day AI-first environment Small, talented team 25 days holiday + bank holidays, private healthcare and paid conferences The office is in St Albans, just a 10-minute walk from the station, with free parking available. You'll work on-site three days per week. Click "easy apply" and I'll be in touch ✉️

items.desc: Telegram WhatsApp Цена — один из самых сильных рычагов маркетплейса: от неё напрямую зависят GMV, маржинальность и то, насколько выгодно покупать у нас. Команда ценообразования строит систему динамического ценообразования. Система регулярно пересчитывает рекомендации для большого числа SKU и управляет скидками так, чтобы расти в продажах и не терять в марже. В скоупе — прогноз спроса, оценка эластичности, оптимизация цены и скидки при бизнес-ограничениях и постоянные A/B-эксперименты с аналитиками и продуктом. Чем предстоит заниматься: ㅤ Модели спроса и цены: прогноз спроса, оценка влияния цены и скидки на продажи, рекомендации по оптимальной цене Качество моделей: feature engineering, offline-валидация, анализ ошибок, выбор и сравнение ML-подходов Данные: подготовка датасетов и признаков, EDA, контроль качества входных данных Эксперименты: вместе с аналитиками проектировать и разбирать A/B-тесты, оценивать влияние на GMV, маржинальность и продажи Прод и надёжность: развивать ML-систему, которая пересчитывает цены на большом ассортименте; следить за поведением моделей после запуска и разбирать инциденты Инженерная культура: code review, обсуждение архитектуры, документация решений и результатов экспериментов ㅤ Наш стек: ㅤ ML/DS: Python, pandas/polars, NumPy, scikit-learn, CatBoost/LightGBM, PyTorch Данные: ClickHouse, Trino, Airflow Прод: Git, Docker, CI/CD A/B-эксперименты: GrowthBook ㅤ Что мы ждём: ㅤ 3+ года коммерческого опыта в ML/DS: обучал модели и доводил их до прода или до регулярного использования Уверенный Python и основной DS-стек; опыт с градиентным бустингом и/или PyTorch Уверенный SQL, опыт работы с большими данными Понимание A/B-тестов: статистическая значимость, доверительные интервалы, power и MDE, корректная интерпретация результатов Умение писать поддерживаемый код: Git, Docker, базовое понимание CI/CD и оркестрации пайплайнов Самостоятельность: умеешь разбить задачу на части, предложить варианты решения и довести выбранный до результата Умение объяснять ограничения и результаты моделей аналитикам, разработчикам и продукту Оцениваешь модели не только по offline-метрикам, но и по влиянию на бизнес ㅤ Будет плюсом: ㅤ Опыт с demand forecasting, price elasticity, оптимизацией цен или скидок Понимание causal inference: почему нельзя просто обучить модель «цена → спрос» на исторических данных Опыт в e-commerce или ритейле ㅤ Процесс найма: ㅤ HR-интервью (30 мин): команда, контекст, твой опыт и ожидания Тех-1 (60 мин): Python, SQL, теория ML Тех-2 (60 мин): ML System Design Финал (60 мин): интервью с руководителем ㅤ Почему это интересно: ㅤ Даем широкую зону ответственности и возможность влиять на архитектурные и продуктовые решения. А ещё рады обсуждать твои инициативы и реализовывать их Уникальная культура – мы сохранили дух стартапа, при этом уже отстроили зрелые процессы Формируем измеримые цели всей командой и не просто выполняем их "для галочки", а замеряем эффективность и общее влияние нашей работы на бизнес Работа в командах сильных специалистов, где ценится глубина экспертизы и инженерное мышление Команды слушают и слышат друг друга, выступая в роли партнеров, а не исполнителей ㅤ Что мы предлагаем: ㅤ Удаленка из любой точки мира или уютный офис в Ташкенте У нас можно расти в инженерном или управленческом треке, а еще выстроена регулярная оценка перформанса Платим на уровне топовых компаний российского рынка Обучение и развитие — мы поддерживаем как внутри компании, так и за ее пределами (митапы, конференции, профессиональное обучение, публикации). А еще помогаем развивать личный бренд База — комьюнити профессионалов с желанием делать круто. Приятный бонус — ДМС в привязке к вашей локации, обучение и другие плюшки

items.desc: À propos de nous Rejoindre l’Université de Haute-Alsace, c’est s’engager pour le service public et participer à un projet porteur de sens aux côtés de plus de 1000 collègues. Garantissez aux générations futures un avenir riche en compétences et en opportunités professionnelles et évoluez au sein d’une université d’excellence, qui s’engage et innove en continu pour répondre aux mutations de la société et aux attentes du monde socio-économique. Le poste est affecté au sein de l’IRIMAS, unité de recherche de l’Université de Haute-Alsace. Mission Concevoir et mettre en œuvre des méthodes d’intelligence artificielle et de science des données adaptées aux problématiques des équipes de recherche de l’IRIMAS, de l’analyse du besoin à l’évaluation et à la valorisation des solutions, en veillant à leur robustesse, leur reproductibilité et leur réutilisation. Activités principales Analyser les besoins des équipes et les conseiller sur les méthodes, outils et architectures adaptés Concevoir, développer et évaluer de nouveaux algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle, notamment en apprentissage automatique, en apprentissage profond et, selon les projets, en IA générative ou à base d’agents Concevoir et développer des outils fondés sur des agents d’IA répondant aux besoins des équipes Préparer les données, définir les protocoles d’entraînement et de validation, évaluer les modèles et documenter leurs limites Développer des prototypes réutilisables, contribuer à leur intégration logicielle et adapter les méthodes aux ressources de calcul, notamment aux GPU Contribuer aux projets scientifiques, à la recherche de financements et aux publications, et conseiller et former les équipes Participer à la configuration des équipements et à la mise à jour du site de l’IRIMAS. Des déplacements ponctuels sont à prévoir, notamment pour participer à des conférences, rencontrer les partenaires et assurer la promotion de l’Institut. Le poste est proposé dans le cadre d’un contrat d’un an, renouvelable. Une évolution vers un CDI pourra être envisagée ultérieurement, sous réserve des résultats obtenus et des conditions réglementaires applicables. Profil Vous possédez un doctorat en informatique, intelligence artificielle, science des données ou domaine connexe. Une expérience en recherche et développement de méthodes d’apprentissage est souhaitée. Une expérience en projets collaboratifs ou publications scientifiques serait appréciée. Une possédez une maîtrise de l’apprentissage automatique et profond, de Python et d’un langage compilé (C ou C++), ainsi que des connaissances en science des données, évaluation des modèles, Linux, gestion de versions, tests et documentation ; notions de calcul haute performance appréciées. Vous maîtrisez un anglais professionnel permettant de lire, rédiger et présenter des travaux scientifiques. L’Université de Haute-Alsace laisse toute latitude au candidat de joindre tous les documents jugés pertinents à son CV et valorisant sa carrière. Lors des auditions, le jury de recrutement se réserve la possibilité de procéder à une mise en situation professionnelle. Pour candidater, le dossier devra comporter les pièces suivantes : Un CV détaillé ; Une lettre de motivation ; Trois lettres de recommandation ; Les coordonnées de 3 personnes de référence pouvant être contactées ; Les rapports des rapporteurs de la thèse de doctorat, le cas échéant ; Le cas échéant, les relevés de notes des années de Master. Le dossier devra être suffisamment détaillé pour permettre d'apprécier le parcours académique, les expériences professionnelles et les compétences scientifiques du candidat. items.desc: Role Title: AI Benchmark Researcher (Remote) Role Type : Full-time Location: Remote Role Overview We are seeking an analytical researcher and red-teaming specialist to build evidence-based web-research benchmark tasks that reliably expose weaknesses in state-of-the-art (SOTA) AI models (e.g., Claude Opus 5 Max). In this role, you will discover hard-to-surface facts, build precise research tasks around them, test them directly against leading LLMs, and diagnose the exact failure mechanisms in the model's search and reasoning paths. Your work will directly shape AI evaluation frameworks, ensuring next-generation frontier models are tested against rigorous, non-trivial real-world research scenarios. Job Requirements : 1. Core Experience: 1+ years in investigative research, fact-checking, AI benchmark task authoring, red-teaming, or technical QA review. 2. Benchmark Familiarity: Proven experience authoring, testing, or reviewing tasks for AI benchmarks such as GAIA, BrowseComp, SimpleQA, SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, or Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE). 3. Analytical & OSINT Skills: Intermediate-to-advanced web search and Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) skills; ability to navigate academic archives, local records, or obscure databases. 4. Model Trajectory Debugging: Strong analytical capability to inspect model reasoning chains, search logs, and source selection to diagnose root causes of failure. 5. Precision Writing: Ability to author clear, unambiguous benchmark prompts with bulletproof, primary-sourced answer keys. Job Responsibilities: 1. Obscure Fact Discovery: Deeply research niche topics to identify factual ground truths that cannot be surfaced via simple, direct search queries. 2. Source Verification: Rigorously verify facts against primary or highly credible sources, cross-check for contradictory evidence, and document exact source URLs. 3. Task Construction: Draft clear, answerable benchmark tasks designed specifically to expose structural weaknesses in model research strategies. 4. Red-Teaming & Model Testing: Execute tasks against designated SOTA models to confirm they reliably trigger intended model failures. 5. Failure Diagnosis & Debugging: Trace model run logs, search trajectories, and intermediate outputs to pinpoint exactly where and why the model failed (distinguishing genuine model limitations from ambiguous prompts). 6. Pattern Scaling & Review: Apply validated "model-breaking" research patterns across new domains and, for strong performers, review tasks authored by peer trainers. Strong Plus (Preferred Qualifications) 7. Bachelor or higher degree from relevant engineering domain is a must for this position. 8. Prior experience specifically designing prompt-injection or reasoning-trap tasks that break SOTA models. 9. Advanced OSINT capabilities or published investigative/academic research demonstrating deep source verification. 10. Niche domain expertise in areas rich with hard-to-find records (e.g., local government filings, regional sports history, legal archives, historical patents). 11. Experience serving as a lead reviewer, benchmark auditor, or quality owner on AI evaluation projects. Offer Details: 1. Guided by its mission to enrich lives through communication and intelligent innovation, Huawei stands at the forefront of global digital transformation. As a leader in Information and Communications Technology (ICT), the company pioneers breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and smart devices—building the intelligent foundation of a fully connected world. 
 Through its Carrier, Enterprise, and Consumer business groups, Huawei delivers resilient digital infrastructure, advanced cloud and AI platforms, and transformative devices that enable progress at every level. Supporting 45 of the world’s top 50 telecom operators and serving one-third of the global population across more than 170 countries, Huawei is shaping a future where connectivity becomes a powerful catalyst for opportunity and sustainable growth. 
 This spirit of bold innovation is embodied by Huawei Technologies Switzerland AG. From its research hubs in Zurich and Lausanne, pioneering teams push the boundaries of High-Performance Computing, Computer Architecture, Computer Vision, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Neuromorphic Computing, Wireless Technologies, and Networking—architecting the intelligent systems that will define tomorrow’s digital era. 
 About the role 
 The Future Storage systems Lab at Huawei Research Center in Zurich is looking for a Researcher to push the frontier of future storage systems. You will conduct cutting-edge research on control theory, developing efficient algorithms which run on-device, and making them predictable and reliable enough to be trusted in a product. 
 To meet needs of hyperscalers in the big data era, cost-effective storage solutions are required. This is achieved using a tiered storage: Solid-state drives are reserved for performance-critical, frequently accessed data. Hard disk drives (HDD) cost roughly about 3-5× less than SSD, making them the right choice for large, less frequently accessed data. For long-term archive and backup, LTO tape costs 10-20× cheaper than SSD and 3-4× cheaper than HDD, while also providing offline, air-gapped protection and an archival life of up to 30 years. 
 Your research will be primarily applied to magnetic storage devices. These devices combine physics, signal processing and mechatronics. From a control perspective, they must deliver precise and accurate positioning despite operating in a disturbance-rich and noisy environment. Your role will be to investigate, from a control theory perspective, which technologies can be used to meet the ever-growing performance requirement of magnetic storage devices, and your work will help shape next-generation Huawei warm and cold data storage products. 
 This is a role for someone who wants to publish at top venues and see their research ship. 
 Responsibilities: 
 • Conduct original research aimed at improving magnetic storage devices including, but not limited to, system identification & model validation, state estimation and controller synthesis. 
 • Transfer research results into Huawei products in close collaboration with product, hardware, and software engineering teams. 
 • Publish at leading conferences and journals and contribute to the research community. 
 • Mentor interns and junior researchers, and collaborate with academic partners in Switzerland and abroad. 
 Requirements: 
 • PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Control Theory, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field. 
 • Experience with advanced feedback and feedforward control methods. 
 • Experience with nonlinear state estimation. 
 • Curiosity, independence, and the drive to turn research into real-world impact. 
 Nice to have: 
 • Experience with rapid prototyping and dealing with actual hardware (integrating sensors, troubleshooting, etc). 
 • Experience with developing digital twins. 
 • Experience with machine learning frameworks combining neural networks and control theory. 
 Why join us: 
 • Collaborate with world-class scientists and engineers in an open, curiosity-driven environment; 
 • Access to state-of-the-art technology and tools; 
 • Opportunities for professional growth and development; 
 • Competitive salary and a high quality of life in Zurich, at the centre of Europe; 
 • Last but certainly not least: be part of innovative projects that make a difference.

Join our Team
 About this opportunity 
 Ericsson’s Early Career Program is an 18-month journey for you who are recently graduated or have up to five years of relevant experience. Through three rotations, including one international and market exposure, you will tackle challenges that matter, work alongside people who expect you to contribute, question, and move things forward. 
 The Innovate track is designed for you who are driven by building what’s next. You’ll rotate across Research, Product Development, Data, and AI contributing to solutions that don’t just support the business but move it forward. 
 This isn’t a programme where you sit on the sidelines. From day one, you’re hired into a role, trusted to contribute, supported to grow, and expected to make an impact. Find out more about the Early Career program here . 
 Your journey within the Early Career Program will start as a LLM Post-Training Engineer at BNEW SAN AI Accelerator!
 The AI Accelerator within BNEW SAN is transforming Customer Support and Network Deployment with agent-centric AI. As an LLM Post-Training Engineer, you’ll help adapt foundation models for telecom use cases through fine-tuning, alignment, and data work—making AI agents more reliable and useful while supporting the journey toward autonomous network operations.
 What you will do
 Working with experienced engineers and domain specialists, you’ll contribute to the areas below and grow your ownership over time.
 Domain Knowledge Injection via Fine-Tuning
 Contribute to developing and running supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pipelines that adapt base LLMs with domain knowledge for Customer Support and Network Deployment use cases.
 Experiment with parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques—including LoRA, QLoRA, and adapter-based methods—and help evaluate trade-offs in model quality, compute, and latency.
 Work with the AI & Domain Specialist and AI Data & Integration Engineer to review fine-tuning datasets for quality, domain coverage, and training-ready formats.
 Help document and organize fine-tuned model variants, adapter checkpoints, and training configurations to support reproducibility and model lifecycle management.
 Policy-Reward Training & Alignment
 Support experiments with policy-reward training approaches, including methods such as GRPO and SAPO, with guidance from experienced teammates.
 Help prepare and evaluate reward signals and preference datasets that capture domain-specific quality—including correct, safe, and operationally appropriate behavior in telco contexts.
 Contribute to improving alignment strategies by reviewing evaluation results and production feedback with the team.
 Keep up with post-training research and share promising techniques for the team to assess.
 Automatic Dataset Curation & Synthetic Data Generation
 Contribute to building and maintaining data-curation pipelines by helping source, filter, deduplicate, and format datasets for SFT and reward training.
 Help develop and evaluate synthetic-data approaches to create diverse training examples where real-world data is limited, sensitive, or imbalanced.
 Work with domain experts to review synthetic examples for quality and relevance to real telco operational scenarios.
 Help develop and run data-quality checks that maintain dataset integrity through curation and generation.
 Training Run Management & Experiment Tracking
 Support training runs by helping configure jobs, schedule and monitor workloads, and manage GPU resources.
 Maintain clear experiment records with training configurations, dataset versions, evaluation results, and model artifacts to make results reproducible.
 Track and summarize key training metrics—such as loss curves, reward trends, benchmark scores, and alignment quality—for the AI System Architect and engineering team.
 Work with experienced teammates to investigate training instability, overfitting, and performance bottlenecks, and help test potential improvements.

 We welcome early-career candidates and do not require professional experience in LLMs or model training. We are especially interested in candidates who have explored how to train large language models through academic work, research, projects, internships, or self-directed learning.

 A collaborative mindset and the ability to communicate ideas and learn alongside technical and domain-specialist teammates.

 Academic or research experience focused on large language models or model training, including fine-tuning or post-training. Experience with SFT or parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA is a plus.

Kreatywność, odwaga i innowacyjność to nasze DNA. Działamy w obszarach mediów, reklamy i e-commerce, łącząc te elementy w sposób, który angażuje i inspiruje. Tworzymy, testujemy, wprowadzamy zmiany tam, gdzie mają sens. Budujemy rzeczy od zera i szukamy nowych rozwiązań. Nad czym pracuje nasz zespół? Ile warto zapłacić za wyświetlenie reklamy? Nasze modele odpowiadają na to pytanie miliardy razy dziennie. Budujemy mózg biddera RTB, który kupuje powierzchnię reklamową dla klientów e-commerce. Pracujemy w skali, która robi wrażenie: setki tysięcy zapytań na sekundę, dziesiątki miliardów decyzji ML dziennie, a cały proces inferencji musi zmieścić się w kilkudziesięciu milisekundach. To jeden z kluczowych produktów reklamowych WP, więc jakość Twoich modeli przekłada się na przychody i marżę. Jako Data Scientist masz pełny ownership: od postawienia hipotezy i analizy danych, przez trening modeli i testy A/B, po wdrożenie na produkcję i monitoring. Sam prowadzisz swój projekt od początku do końca bez przekazywania go dalej i czekania na efekty. Mierzymy się z trudnymi problemami z obszaru real-time ML, optymalizacji i statystyki, a narzędzia AI są naturalną częścią naszego codziennego warsztatu. Jeśli zależy Ci na realnym wpływie na produkt działający w dużej skali, to miejsce dla Ciebie! Jakie działania będą należeć do Ciebie? Projektowanie i wdrażanie modeli ML rozwiązujących problemy biznesowe (predykcja, ranking, modelowanie zachowań użytkowników). Tworzenie i wdrażanie algorytmów optymalizacyjnych oraz rekomendacyjnych (np. ustalanie stawek w aukcjach, alokacja budżetów, personalizacja treści), wprost przekładających się na kluczowe wskaźniki biznesowe. Projektowanie algorytmów z wykorzystaniem najnowszych publikacji naukowych — czytamy je i sprawdzamy możliwości zastosowania opisanych metod w naszych rozwiązaniach. Analiza dużych zbiorów danych w poszukiwaniu zależności i informacji, które pozwolą poprawiać jakość modeli i algorytmów. Łączenie informacji z różnych źródeł danych i odkrywanie nieoczywistych powiązań przydatnych w modelowaniu. Jakie kompetencje są dla nas ważne? Minimum 3 lata doświadczenia komercyjnego w budowaniu modeli ML i wdrażaniu ich na produkcję jako Data Scientist, ML Engineer lub na podobnym stanowisku. Bardzo dobra znajomość Pythona i narzędzi takich jak PyTorch, LightGBM, XGBoost czy Polars. Umiejętność pisania czytelnego kodu i testów oraz doświadczenie w pracy z Gitem i w przeprowadzaniu code review. Doświadczenie w pracy z dużymi zbiorami danych z wykorzystaniem SQL (np. w ClickHouse lub StarRocks) oraz Apache Spark, PySpark lub podobnych narzędzi. Solidne podstawy z zakresu rachunku prawdopodobieństwa, statystyki i optymalizacji, zdobyte np. na studiach matematycznych, fizycznych, informatycznych lub pokrewnych. Umiejętność samodzielnego przekładania problemów biznesowych na zadania ML i jasnego przedstawiania wyników także osobom nietechnicznym. Znajomość języka angielskiego na poziomie B2, pozwalająca swobodnie korzystać z dokumentacji technicznej i publikacji naukowych. items.title: Research Associate in Brain Organoids and Organ-on-Chip Platforms
items.card: About the role Are you a talented cell and developmental biologist ready to work at the interface of biology and microelectronics? As a Research Associate in Brain Organoids and Organ-on-Chip Platforms, you will lead the biological arm of a new programme combining semiconductor-based lab-on-chip technology with human brain organoids. You will bring the biological expertise that our engineering team needs, and in
items.desc: Job number ENG04102 Faculties Faculty of Engineering Departments Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 7 Dec 2026 About the role Are you a talented cell and developmental biologist ready to work at the interface of biology and microelectronics? As a Research Associate in Brain Organoids and Organ-on-Chip Platforms, you will lead the biological arm of a new programme combining semiconductor-based lab-on-chip technology with human brain organoids. You will bring the biological expertise that our engineering team needs, and in return gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge chip technology, co-author high-impact interdisciplinary papers, and help shape the direction of a growing research area. Within two years, you will deliver validated brain-organoid protocols and device-compatible culture methods for our semiconductor platforms. The group of Prof. Pantelis Georgiou develops lab-on-chip systems based on semiconductor technology. We design, fabricate and test integrated sensing and microfluidic platforms built on CMOS technology, taking ideas from concept through to working devices for biological applications, clinical validation and translation. We are now extending this work to complex three-dimensional human brain organoid models, in collaboration with colleagues in Medicine. Imperial offers an outstanding environment for this work, with access to world-class cleanroom, imaging and bioengineering facilities and a strong community in engineering, neuroscience and stem cell biology. What you would be doing You will establish and characterise robust brain organoid culture in our laboratory and work alongside engineers and device physicists to integrate organoids onto chip platforms, creating organ-on-chip systems that enable sensing, stimulation and monitoring of organoids. You will be responsible for: Generating and maintaining brain organoids (for example cortical or region-specific organoids) from human pluripotent stem cells, with reproducible quality control Characterising organoids using immunostaining, imaging, gene expression and functional assays Working with engineers to design biocompatible chip interfaces, culture conditions and protocols for long-term organoid culture on devices Testing and validating device performance with living tissue, and feeding results back to the design cycle Analysing and interpreting data, and writing papers, reports and conference presentations Helping train and supervise PhD and MSc students in cell culture and biological methods Contributing to grant applications and collaborations What we are looking for You will hold (or be about to obtain) a PhD in a relevant discipline such as stem cell biology, neuroscience, developmental biology, tissue engineering or a related field. You will have demonstrable hands-on experience of culturing human pluripotent stem cells and generating 3D neural models, and you will be keen to work in a multidisciplinary team with engineers. You do not need a background in electronics or microfabrication; we will teach you what you need, however prior experience with commercial MEA platforms may be useful. You will be an excellent communicator, with the ability to manage work to deadlines. What we can offer you An exciting opportunity to develop a new programme at the interface of biology and microelectronics, working with a welcoming multidisciplinary team, state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technologies. As a member of Imperial research staff, you will have the opportunity to: continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity, grow your career with access to Imperial’s dedicated career support for researchers, plus opportunities for promotion and progression, develop your skills and explore your career prospects with 10 development days per year, benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package, be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . Please include in your application a CV with publication list and cover letter (maximum two pages) describing your experience with organoids and your interest in working with engineering platforms. If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Prof Pantelis Georgiou (pantelis@imperial.ac.uk) Available documents Attached documents are available under links. Clicking a document link will initialize its download. Please note that job descriptions are not exhaustive, and you may be asked to take on additional duties that align with the key …

items.desc: Job Details Section Sustainable Electronic Technologies Location: Highfield Campus Salary £37,369 to £39,560 per annum Full Time Fixed Term until 31/01/2029 Closing Date: Monday 07 December 2026 Interview Date To be confirmed Reference 3550026FP You will join the 2D-MINDs team, led by Dr Soumya Sarkar within the Sustainable Electronic Technologies research group in the School of Electronics and Computer Science (ECS) at the University of Southampton. You will also be part of the interdisciplinary ECS Centre for Neuromorphic Technologies (CeNT). The position is funded by the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship “2D semiconductors for intelligent non-volatile memory devices” (2DMINDs) . The post will be full-time for a period until 31/01/2029 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for another 12 months. You will investigate two-dimensional semiconductors and ferroelectric materials to develop non-volatile memory that co-locates storage and processing for low-power AI hardware. Your research will combine materials characterisation, interface engineering and device fabrication at Southampton Nanofabrication Centre to develop foundry-compatible fabrication protocols alongside specialist electrical and optical characterisation facilities. Training and support will be provided to develop the skills required for your research. The role is well suited to candidates who wish to develop their expertise in emerging memory devices and neuromorphic technologies within a supportive, interdisciplinary research environment. We welcome applicants with complementary experimental backgrounds; experience across all the areas listed below is not expected. You should be a resourceful and passionate researcher who will plan and conduct experiments, develop measurement techniques and generate high-quality research data. You will contribute to the project’s scientific direction, prepare manuscripts, undertake short research visits to project partners (University of Cambridge, NPL), present findings at international conferences, write project reports and support the supervision of master’s and PhD students. The role offers support for conference travel, collaboration, industry engagement and outreach. Extensive leadership training and transferable skills development will support your progression towards research independence and future leadership in ferroelectric neuromorphic devices. Essential requirements A PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in materials science, physics, electronic engineering or a related discipline. Experience in one or more of the following: fabrication and characterisation of devices based on 2D semiconductors, or ferroelectric materials. Strong experimental and analytical skills, with the ability to plan research, interpret results and solve technical problems. Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams. Desirable experience Ferroelectric transistors, tunnel junctions or diodes, or other non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices. E-beam lithography, thin-film deposition or dry-transfer assembly of van der Waals heterostructures. Temperature-dependent electrical transport or pulsed electrical measurements. Optical spectroscopy, including Raman, photoluminescence or reflectance, or scanning probe microscopy, including AFM, PFM or KPFM. Contributing to academic publications, collaborative research or student supervision. We warmly welcome applicants from all backgrounds, particularly those underrepresented in the field. ECS holds an Athena SWAN Silver award in recognition of its continued commitment to improving equality for women in science and engineering. We have a range of staff development programmes and a unique mentoring and wellbeing scheme. We recognise that research careers follow different paths and welcome applications from candidates whose PhD completion or career progression has been affected by caring responsibilities, health conditions or other personal circumstances. International applicants are encouraged to apply. Informal enquiries should be directed to Dr Soumya Sarkar (soumya.sarkar@soton.ac.uk). Apply by uploading your CV and a cover letter detailing how your skills and experience match the requirements of the role. As a university we aim to create an environment where everyone can thrive and are proactive in fostering a culture of inclusion, respect and equality of opportunity. We believe that we can only truly meet our objectives if we are reflective of society, so we are passionate about creating a working environment in which you are free to bring your whole self to work. With a generous holiday allowance as well as additional university closure days we are committed to supporting our staff and students and open to a flexible working approach. Functional Safety Expert (ISO 26262) - Hardware Development Publication: November 2026 Functional Safety Expert (ISO 26262) – Hardware Development We are looking for a Functional Safety Expert (ISO 26262) with a strong background as an Electronic Engineer to join our Hardware development team. You will be the hands-on reference point for the practical implementation of functional safety on strategic automotive projects, working directly on hardware development for Inverters and Battery Management Systems (BMS). Role Objective The ideal candidate will be directly responsible for deriving and validating functional safety requirements in compliance with the ISO 26262 standard. You will work closely with other hardware designers to co-design the safety architecture, performing the FuSa analyses required by the standard, and coordinating HW testing, HW-SW integration, and fault injection for final validation. Key Responsibilities Operational Functional Safety (ISO 26262): Requirements Definition & Decomposition: Translate Technical Safety Requirements (TSR) into detailed Hardware Safety Requirements (HSR) at the component level. Hands-on Safety Analysis: Execute, compile, and maintain qualitative and quantitative analyses first-hand, including FMEDA (Failure Modes, Effects, and Diagnostic Analysis), DFA (Dependent Failure Analysis), and FTA (Fault Tree Analysis). Metric Calculation & Modeling: Calculate and numerically verify compliance with the hardware metrics required by the standard (Single Point Fault Metric – SPFM, Latent Fault Metric – LFM, Probabilistic Metric for random Hardware Failures – PMHF) based on the target ASIL (up to ASIL D). Technical Documentation: Draft and constantly update the hardware Safety Case documentation, preparing it for internal and external audits. Hardware Development & Lab (Inverter & BMS): Architectural Co-design: Actively collaborate in defining safe electronic architectures for traction Inverters and BMS (e.g., cell monitoring circuits, galvanic isolation, power stages, shutdown circuits). Component Selection & Analysis: Evaluate and select suitable electronic components (e.g., automotive-grade microcontrollers, monitoring ASICs) by analyzing their safety manuals and integrated diagnostic functions. Testing, Lab & Validation: Define Hardware Safety Verification and Validation plans and physically execute/coordinate Fault Injection Testing in the laboratory using measurement instrumentation. Requirements Education & Experience: Marter Degree in Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics, or equivalent fields. Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in electronic hardware development and FMEDA calculation within the Automotive sector. Consolidated practical experience in applying the ISO 26262 standard (specifically Part 5: Product development at the hardware level ). Technical Skills: In-depth knowledge and analysis capability of electronic architectures for Inverters and BMS. Operational mastery of reliability analysis tools (e.g., Ansys Medini Analyze or equivalent software). Knowledge of main electronic design and simulation tools (e.g., Altium Designer, Cadence, SPICE). Experience working in a testing laboratory and autonomous use of related instrumentation (oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, battery simulators). Soft Skills & Languages: Strong attention to detail, pragmatism, and an analytical/hands-on approach. Ability to work in synergistic way and to interface with clients and auditors for the technical defense of the analyses performed. Excellent knowledge of the English language (written and spoken), required for technical documentation and international relations. Nice to have: Official certification as a Functional Safety Engineer/Professional (e.g., TÜV, SGS-TÜV Saar). Knowledge of complementary standards such as Automotive SPICE (ASPICE) or ISO 21434 (Cybersecurity). items.desc: Offre de stage PFE – IA parcimonieuse et géométries variables Sujet : Explorer les méthodes de construction de modèles de substitution pour des cas à géométries variables Lieu : Toulouse Durée : 5 à 6 mois Début : à partir de février 2027 Entreprise : ADAGOS – Créateur de NeurEco® À propos d’Adagos Adagos est une société innovante issue de la recherche toulousaine, spécialisée dans les intelligences artificielles parcimonieuses et explicables appliquées à la modélisation de systèmes physiques complexes. Sa technologie brevetée NeurEco permet de générer automatiquement des modèles compacts, interprétables et prédictifs à partir de données issues de simulations, d’essais expérimentaux ou d’environnements opérationnels. NeurEco est aujourd’hui utilisée par des acteurs tels que Thales, Framatome, Dassault et Stellantis dans des applications de jumeaux numériques, de capteurs virtuels et d’optimisation énergétique. Sujet du stage Dans de nombreuses applications industrielles, la géométrie fait partie intégrante des paramètres de conception : profil d’aile, forme de carrosserie, canaux de refroidissement, position de perçages… Construire un modèle de substitution dans ce contexte est difficile : les maillages changent de taille et parfois de topologie d’une simulation à l’autre, et la géométrie ne se résume pas toujours à quelques paramètres scalaires. L’objectif du stage est de dresser un panorama des méthodes permettant de construire des modèles de substitution sur des géométries variables, de les comparer sur des cas représentatifs et d’identifier les stratégies les mieux adaptées à l’approche compacte et parcimonieuse de NeurEco. Travail proposé Le ou la stagiaire sera amené(e) à : réaliser un état de l’art des approches de représentation de la géométrie et des champs physiques associés : paramétrisation explicite (paramètres CAO), morphing de maillage et réduction de dimension (POD/PCA), fonctions distance signée et projection sur grille de référence, nuages de points, réseaux de neurones sur graphes, opérateurs neuronaux (FNO, Geo-FNO, etc.) ; sélectionner ou constituer des jeux de données de référence (bases publiques telles qu’AirfRANS ou DrivAerNet, ou cas générés par simulation paramétrique) ; implémenter et comparer plusieurs chaînes de construction de modèles de substitution, pour la prédiction de quantités d’intérêt scalaires (coefficients aérodynamiques, efforts, températures maximales…) comme de champs complets ; étudier comment encoder la géométrie sous une forme compacte exploitable par NeurEco, et évaluer les compromis entre précision, taille du modèle, volume de données nécessaire et temps d’inférence ; analyser la capacité de généralisation des modèles à des géométries éloignées de celles vues à l’apprentissage. Le ou la stagiaire pourra également participer à des projets industriels réalisés en collaboration directe avec les clients d’Adagos. Environnement technique Langage : Python, C++ (optionnel) Librairies : PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, scikit-learn, PyVista, meshio Données : simulations paramétriques (aérodynamique, thermique, mécanique des structures, etc.) sur maillages non structurés Profil recherché Étudiant(e) en dernière année d’école d’ingénieur ou de master 2 en mathématiques appliquées. Bonne connaissance de la simulation numérique (éléments finis, volumes finis) et des bases de l’apprentissage automatique. Intérêt pour la réduction de modèles, l’apprentissage sur données géométriques et la lecture de la littérature scientifique récente. Une capacité à interagir avec des interlocuteurs techniques et à comprendre les enjeux industriels sera également appréciée. Ce que nous offrons Un stage au cœur de l’innovation en IA pour la simulation numérique. Une formation pratique à NeurEco, utilisée dans plusieurs projets industriels stratégiques. Un encadrement scientifique de qualité. Une ambiance de travail stimulante, au sein d’une équipe passionnée. Une expérience concrète au contact de projets clients, permettant de relier la recherche et les applications industrielles. Des opportunités d’embauche à l’issue du stage. Candidature Envoyer CV et lettre de motivation à : contact@adagos.com Objet : Candidature Stage PFE – Géométries variables et NeurEco

items.desc: Accepting Applications Until 27 November 2026 Job Description Machine Learning Engineer Global’s central Data Science function is recruiting a Machine Learning Engineer to work across our data and product portfolio. As a Machine Learning Engineer at Global, you’ll be part of the engineering bridge between data science and production—taking models built by our data scientists and making them robust, scalable and maintainable across audience targeting, advertising measurement and content intelligence. You’ll work with colleagues across Data Science, Machine Learning Engineering and Data Engineering, bringing your own ideas to how we build and improve our models. The role is based in central London (Holborn, with occasional travel to Leicester Square). Key Responsibilities Model Productionisation, Serving & Lifecycle Management (70%): Take models built by our data scientists and turn them into reliable, testable production systems; build the serving infrastructure to deliver them across batch and real-time use cases; build and maintain consistent feature pipelines; keep models healthy once live through monitoring, drift detection and periodic retraining; and help audit and migrate existing models to modern standards without disrupting live products. Standards & Enablement (15%): Apply and contribute to the engineering standards for how models are built, tested and deployed, aligned to the MLOps platform; help create reusable templates and documentation that enable data scientists to work independently; and feed your experience back to help shape the platform direction. Cross-functional Partnership (15%): Work with Data Science, MLOps, Data Engineering and Product to understand new products early and ensure models are handed off in a deployable, maintainable form. What You’ll Love About This Role Think Big: This is a true AI and data-driven space—the models you ship influence what millions of listeners hear and how brands invest their media budgets. Own It: You’ll take ownership of getting models into production and keeping them healthy, and your voice will count in how we build going forward—not just maintaining what exists. Keep it Simple: You’ll build on and contribute to reusable patterns and templates rather than one-off solutions. Better Together: You’ll work with Data Science, MLOps, Data Engineering and Product, with plenty of opportunity to broaden your experience across Global’s data products. What Success Looks Like In Your First Few Months, You’ll Have Built a working understanding of Global’s engineering and data science tools and how they connect. Established strong working relationships with Data Science, MLOps and the wider engineering team. Contributed to the audit of existing ML models in production, assessing stability, maintainability and risk. Taken a model (or part of one) to a more robust, documented state, and contributed reusable components others can use. What You’ll Need Production ML experience: You’ve delivered ML projects in a commercial environment, contributing to deployment, CI/CD and lifecycle management. You’ve delivered models across different mediums, such as batch models running on a schedule and models served via APIs. Strong Python: Solid Python written to production standards: you unit test your code, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and code defensively so that simple edge cases don’t break production environments. Experience with PyTorch or similar ML frameworks is a plus. Model evaluation & monitoring: You can investigate why models underperform across data, features and architecture, and explain the trade-offs behind your choices. You understand how to monitor models in production, detect model and data drift, and put safeguards in place to defend against it. Orchestration: Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow or similar, and an understanding of how to schedule, monitor and maintain dependable data and model pipelines. Real-time ML & reproducibility: A good understanding of production inference patterns and reproducible environments (Docker, MLflow or equivalent), and a willingness to deepen it. Cloud & data tooling: Familiarity with a SQL data warehouse-style system, and experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP or Azure. Experience with AWS, including SageMaker, Snowflake and Kubernetes is a plus. Engineering mindset: A focus on reliability, maintainability and continuous improvement, with an appetite to learn from more experienced colleagues and share what you learn.

items.desc: Introduction Thesis work is an excellent way to get closer to Scania and build relationships for the future. Many of today's employees began their Scania career with their degree project. Background Within Scania's battery manufacturing, simulation is used to analyse and test manufacturing and logistics solutions in a virtual environment before implementing changes in production. This makes it possible to evaluate different solutions without interfering with ongoing production. Simulation typically requires specialised knowledge and competence to create, validate, verify, update and interpret simulation models and their results. This limits how broadly simulation can be applied in the organisation. The thesis work will investigate how Large Language Models (LLMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can support simulation work and make it more efficient and accessible. Objective The objective is to evaluate how LLM/AI can support high-fidelity simulation in battery manufacturing and to develop a demonstrator showing where the technology can provide value, its limitations and what level of trust can be assigned to the results. Job Description The thesis worker(s) will work with factory simulation models and investigate how LLM/AI can support selected parts of the simulation process. The work will include: Understand the current simulation process and select relevant use cases. Develop and evaluate high-fidelity factory simulation models. Apply LLM/AI support to selected parts of the simulation process, including creation and modification of models, changes to input data, rerunning simulations, and analysis and reporting of results. Compare LLM/AI-assisted work with conventional simulation work. Evaluate benefits, limitations, risks and the level of trust that can be assigned to the results. Identify where human validation is required and where LLM/AI should not be used. Develop and demonstrate the final solution. Document conclusions and recommendations in a final report to Scania and present the results to relevant parts of the organisation. Education/program/focus Relevant Master's programme with a focus on simulation, data science or engineering. Number of students: 1-2 Start date for the thesis work: January 2027 Estimated time required: 20 weeks (800 hours per student) Contact persons and supervisors Anders Siljeström, Logistics Engineering Manager, anders.siljestrom@scania.com, +46855371808 Jesper Gans, Logistics Developer, jesper.x.gans@scania.com, +46765356769 Application Your application must include a CV, personal letter and transcript of grades. A background check might be conducted for this position. We are conducting interviews continuously and may close the recruitment earlier than the date specified. Publication date until:2026-11-22

items.desc: Werkomgeving De Algemene Dienst Inlichting en Veiligheid (ADIV) QUAERO ET TEGO: IK ONDERZOEK EN BESCHERM De bedreigingen voor onze samenleving veranderen voortdurend. De ADIV is de Belgische referentiedienst voor inlichtingen wat betreft Defensie en het buitenland. Met onze inlichtingen dragen we bij tot het beschermen van de belangen van Defensie, ons land en zijn bevolking. We hebben een diepgaand inzicht in de huidige en toekomstige uitdagingen op het gebied van inlichtingen, veiligheid en cyberspace. Dankzij een geïntegreerde aanpak, zowel nationaal als internationaal, werken we samen met onze verschillende partners om de interne veiligheid te handhaven en te versterken. De Directie Support is verantwoordelijk voor het beheer van de personele, materiële en budgettaire middelen van de eenheid. De afdeling zorgt voor een soepele dagelijkse werking van onze eenheid. De ADIV werkt samen met nationale en internationale partners om de stabiliteit van de natie te waarborgen, haar belangen te beschermen en haar fysieke en digitale veiligheid te verzekeren. Het verzamelen van informatie en gegevens vormt de kern van al onze processen en maakt deel uit van ons DNA. Binnen de ADIV staan onze ICT-teams ten dienste van de verschillende directies om hen de technologische ondersteuning te bieden die nodig is voor de uitvoering van hun opdrachten. Ons werk wordt gedreven door een voortdurende zoektocht naar verbetering en technologische innovatie. Ons digitale transformatieprogramma heeft als doel de infrastructuur te moderniseren, de verschillende diensten en toepassingen te integreren en de prestaties op alle domeinen te verbeteren. We bouwen aan de werkomgeving van morgen: flexibel en afgestemd op de behoeften van onze verschillende teams en opdrachten. Meer specifiek is Platforms & Services verantwoordelijk voor de verbetering van de applicatielaag van de ADIV, die haar operaties en haar inlichtingen- en veiligheidsprocessen ondersteunt. AI-modellen ontwerpen, ontwikkelen, trainen, valideren en optimaliseren die aansluiten bij operationele behoeften. Gestructureerde en ongestructureerde gegevens verzamelen, voorbereiden, transformeren en exploiteren voor het trainen van modellen. Dataverwerkingspijplijnen en trainingsomgevingen ontwikkelen en onderhouden binnen beveiligde on-premise infrastructuren. AI-modellen integreren in toepassingen en systemen die door de afdeling worden ontwikkeld. Test- en evaluatieprotocollen opstellen om de kwaliteit, robuustheid en prestaties van modellen te waarborgen. Bijdragen aan de planning en het wijzigingsbeheer van modellen, data en bijbehorende tools. Technische en functionele documentatie van AI-oplossingen opstellen en onderhouden. AI-modellen implementeren, opvolgen en operationeel onderhouden. AI-platformen en -tools onderhouden en hun beschikbaarheid en prestaties waarborgen (L3-support). Toezien op de naleving van de regels inzake informatieveiligheid en van de vereisten inzake vertrouwelijkheid, integriteit en beschikbaarheid van gegevens. Actief deelnemen aan het homologatieproces van systemen die gevoelige of geclassificeerde gegevens verwerken. Advies verstrekken aan de verschillende hiërarchische niveaus over de opportuniteiten, beperkingen en risico's van artificiële intelligentie. Junior ingenieurs of ontwikkelaars begeleiden en coachen. Je kunt bedrijfsbehoeften analyseren en AI-modellen ontwerpen die aansluiten bij de doelstellingen van de organisatie. Je beheerst Python en de belangrijkste bibliotheken en frameworks, zoals Scikit-Learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas en NumPy. Je kunt gestructureerde en ongestructureerde gegevens verzamelen, voorbereiden, opschonen, verrijken en benutten. items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Ready to join one of our Graduate Programs in Spain? 
 AIRBUS offer more than 70 vacancies for our full time graduate program in Spain - #Discover II 2026/2027 - Starting date March 2027 until February 2028 . 
 We are looking for recent graduates from different disciplines interested in developing their professional career in the aeronautical sector. The current context demands different ways of looking, thinking and relating.
 The selection process will be during November 2026 until February 2027. 
 What does this internship consists in? 
 Together with Camilo José Cela University, Airbus has developed an exclusive program (Discover) designed for those interested in the best training in new areas of knowledge essential to be able to develop as professionals of the future.
 You will have the opportunity to study a Master, organized in three training blocks, that will allow you to Discover the skills most in demand today. It will be combined with an 11 month internship at Airbus in an area related to your degree, where you can learn and complete your academic background.
 The start of the internship will be in March 2027, and will last 11 months (August disabled for all purposes). It is a full-time experience (40h/week), in which you will receive an attractive study grant.
 Internship Job Description: 
 - Tasks: We are working in the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to aid in the design and development of the Communications Systems in the products being delivered for all Airbus Defense airborne platforms (Eurofighter, Multi-Role Tanker Transport Aircraft, A400M, C-295, Spanish Trainer, etc.). The intern will work in the development of the infrastructure, environment and AI tools.
 - Knowledge to be acquired by the student: the intern will get acquainted with the processes and tools being used in the development of Communications products in Airbus Defense and will gain practical knowledge in the usage of AI tools for real products.
 Required skills: 
 As a successful candidate, you will be able to demonstrate the following skills and experience:
 - Degree in Computer Sciences, Mathematics, Physics or Engineering.
 - Knowledge in AI, programming, implementation of containers, etc.
 - Level B2 English and Spanish.
 - Skills valued:
 - Analytical and problem-solving skills.
 - Team spirit and great collaboration skills.
 - Ability to work in complex and international environments.
 Why should you apply? 
 - Foster your professional development with a strong academic background and an in-depth collaboration in AIRBUS projects.
 - Expand your network within the aeronautical industry.
 - Meet our people working with passion and determination to make the world a more connected, safer and smarter place.
 - Be part of our diversity and teamwork culture that propel us to accomplish the extraordinary - on the ground, in the sky and in space.
 For any inquiries concerning this selection process, please contact us at randstad-airbus@randstad.es
 Are you interested? Apply and make it fly!

Lieu : Sophia Antipolis, France 
 Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance 
 Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. ​
 Nos engagements, vos avantages 
 Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée
 Un package de rémunération attractif
 Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes
 Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs
 Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu
 Votre quotidien 
Au coeur de la Silicon Valley de la région PACA, notre site regroupe nos activités développe des sonars de pointe équipant les sous-marins et les bâtiments de surface ainsi que des activités de services numériques. Pionnier dans le domaine des produits de simulation, le site mobilise une expertise approfondie en acoustique et en traitement du signal. 
 Au sein de l’équipe Etudes Générales Sonar basée à Sophia Antipolis dans le laboratoire des Traitements pour Sonars Passifs, vous avez la responsabilité des études amont, du développement et de la validation des algorithmes de traitement du signal et de l'information pour les sonars de la ligne de produit sous-marin.
 Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes :
 Définir fonctionnellement les algorithmes de traitement du signal et de traitement de données puis réaliser et valider les chaînes de référence fonctionnelles correspondantes 
 Développer les modules de traitement en C/C++ pour intégration dans le logiciel opérationnel 
 Assurer le support fonctionnel auprès du domaine Sous-marins pour garantir la validation des algorithmes de traitement et la tenue des performances 
 Proposer des moyens de standardisation de chaînes fonctionnelles permettant une meilleure capitalisation et une réduction des risques techniques en phase d'intégration 
 Conduire des études avancées dans le cadre de l’évolution des produits et des solutions futures (ETO, PTD, SFR&D) 
 Participer à la validation en mer sur des bâtiments opérationnels pour démontrer et argumenter auprès des clients les engagements de performances contractuels 
 Votre profil : 
 Votre priorité est de développer vos compétences en traitement du signal et en ingénierie algorithmique ? 
 Vous avez l’ambition de concevoir et optimiser des algorithmes performants ? 
 Vous avez envie de découvrir des environnements innovants où mathématiques appliquées et informatique se conjuguent ? 
 Vous disposez d’un bac +5 en traitement du signal, en ingénierie algorithmique, en informatique ou dans un domaine apparenté, et avez de l’expérience sur : 
 • la conception d’algorithmes, 
 • l’analyse de systèmes et les mathématiques/statistiques appliquées, 
 • les langages de programmation, 
 • la mise en œuvre et l’optimisation des algorithmes. 
 Le travail en équipe ainsi que la collaboration avec des clients internes et externes sont des atouts que l’on vous reconnait ? 
 Alors ce poste est fait pour vous ! 
Thales, entreprise Handi-Engagée, reconnait tous les talents. La diversité est notre meilleur atout. Postulez et rejoignez nous ! 
Le poste pouvant nécessiter d'accéder à des informations relevant du secret de la défense nationale, la personne retenue fera l'objet d'une procédure d’habilitation, conformément aux dispositions des articles R.2311-1 et suivants du Code de la défense et de l’IGI 1300 SGDSN/PSE du 09 août 2021.
