items.card: Vos missions Évaluer la vulnérabilité du système de reconnaissance actuel en concevant et générant des attaques adversariales (symétriques et asymétriques telles que deepfakes audio/vidéo, voice conversion, ou port de masques). Tester la résilience du système multimodal face à des conditions environnementales dégradées (bruit acoustique, basse luminosité, qualité vidéo réduite). Développer des contre-mesures axées
items.desc: Lieu : Palaiseau, France Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. Nos engagements, vos avantages Notre savoir-faire technologique Notre attention portée à l’équilibre des collaborateurs Un environnement inclusif et bienveillant Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu (Thales Solidarity, indice CAC 40 ESG…) Votre quotidien Thales Research&Technology, notre centre de recherche dans les domaines matériels, et CortAIx Labs, notre centre de recherche en IA et digital ont pour mission de proposer des innovations de ruptures, de maintenir et d’accroitre l’avance technologique et d’en assurer la compétitivité pour le groupe. Un stage précédent a permis de développer et de valider une approche de reconnaissance du locuteur par fusion multimodale (audio et vidéo). Il a été prouvé que l'ajout de la modalité vidéo améliore les performances de reconnaissance par rapport à une approche purement audio. Cependant, dans des conditions réelles et adversariales, un système biométrique doit faire face à de multiples tentatives de fraude (spoofing). Avec la démocratisation des intelligences artificielles génératives (deepfakes, voice conversion, lip-sync), un attaquant peut tenter d'usurper l'identité d'un locuteur en falsifiant l'audio, la vidéo, ou les deux de manière asymétrique (ex: une personne porte un masque ou modifie sa voix tout en gardant son visage). L'objectif de ce stage est d'évaluer la robustesse du système actuel face à ces attaques et de développer des contre-mesures intelligentes, notamment en repensant la stratégie de fusion multimodale pour détecter ces fraudes. Objectifs Concevoir et générer différentes attaques (symétriques et asymétriques) pour tester la vulnérabilité du système actuel. Étudier la cohérence temporelle et la "preuve de vie" (Liveness) entre l'audio et la vidéo pour détecter les rejeux été les deepfakes. Tester la résilience du système dans des conditions environnementales dégradées (bruit, luminosité faible). Proposer et implémenter une stratégie de fusion dynamique capable d'ajuster le poids de chaque modalité en fonction de leur niveau de confiance respectif. Vos missions Évaluer la vulnérabilité du système de reconnaissance actuel en concevant et générant des attaques adversariales (symétriques et asymétriques telles que deepfakes audio/vidéo, voice conversion, ou port de masques). Tester la résilience du système multimodal face à des conditions environnementales dégradées (bruit acoustique, basse luminosité, qualité vidéo réduite). Développer des contre-mesures axées sur la "preuve de vie" (Liveness) en analysant la cohérence temporelle audio- vidéo (synchronisation labiale) et en explorant la détection de signaux vitaux (rPPG). Concevoir et implémenter une stratégie de fusion multimodale dynamique, capable d'ajuster le poids de chaque modalité en temps réel selon son niveau de confiance afin de contrer efficacement les fraudes. Votre profil Etudiant en dernière année (Bac+5) d'une école d'ingénieur ou équivalent, vous recherchez un stage de fin d'études de 6 mois. Vous avez de solides compétences en programmation (Python, PyTorch ou TensorFlow) ? Vous avez des connaissances de base en apprentissage profond (réseaux de neurones, CNN, RNN/Transformers) ? Vous avez une appétence pour le traitement du signal audio/vidéo et/ou la cybersécurité (connaissance des deepfakes est un plus) ? Vous êtes connu pour votre curiosité, autonomie et rigueur scientifique ? Alors n'hésitez plus, ce stage est fait pour vous ! Tous nos stages sont conventionnés et soumis à une gratification dont le montant est déterminé selon votre niveau d’études. Thales, entreprise Handi-Engagée, reconnait tous les talents. La diversité est notre meilleur atout. Postulez et rejoignez nous !

items.desc: Software Engineer (Python / AI) Dublin | €85,000- €100,000 + Equity | Fully Onsite Want to build real AI products, take ownership of what you ship, and join a startup that's scaling quickly? I'm working with a well-funded, high-growth AI startup in Dublin that's building some seriously interesting technology. They've recently surpassed $1 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), are onboarding major enterprise customers across the UK and Ireland, and are now growing their engineering team to keep up with demand. This isn't a business experimenting with AI or trying to figure out where it fits. They've built a product that customers are paying for, they're scaling quickly, and there's a huge amount still to build. They're looking for a Software Engineer with strong backend fundamentals who wants to get stuck into building products, solving difficult problems and helping shape the next stage of the company's growth. What makes this interesting? You'll be joining a small, talented engineering team where you'll have genuine ownership over what you build. There's no sitting around waiting for tickets to be assigned. You'll be involved in designing solutions, making technical decisions, building features and seeing your work go into production. Some of the projects you'll be working on include: Multi-Agent AI Systems: Building and improving AI agents that automate complex workflows, manage communications and make intelligent decisions. AI-Native CRM: Developing a completely new approach to CRM, moving away from traditional record-keeping towards proactive, intelligent systems that drive actions. Telephony Infrastructure: Building and scaling in-house communication infrastructure, tackling challenges around real-time systems, different technologies and international markets. Multimodal AI: Developing products that work across voice, WhatsApp, SMS, email and chat, bringing multiple communication channels into one intelligent platform. APIs & Integrations: Building integrations with third-party platforms and developing a unified API layer to support a growing enterprise customer base. LLM Evaluation: Building frameworks to test, compare and evaluate AI models, helping decide which models and agents deliver the best results. You'll be working on real technical challenges, with the freedom to influence how things are built. What they're looking for Ideally, you'll have 2-5 years of commercial software engineering experience, with a strong focus on backend development. The key things: Strong backend engineering fundamentals and the ability to write clean, reliable, production-ready code. Experience with Python , or strong experience in another backend language and the willingness to work primarily with Python. A track record of building products and taking ownership of features from start to finish. Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity and the ability to pick up new technologies quickly. An interest in AI, particularly LLMs, AI agents and the possibilities of agentic systems. A genuine desire to work in a fast-growing startup where you can make an impact. Experience building AI agents, working with LLMs or developing complex integrations would be a big advantage, but you don't need to have done all of this before. Equally, startup experience would be great, but it's not essential. If you've worked in a strong product environment, enjoy building things and want more ownership, they'd love to hear from you. Let's talk about the startup environment I want to be upfront about this because it's an important part of the opportunity. This isn't your typical 9-5 engineering role. The company is growing quickly, the team is lean, and there's a huge amount of work happening as they scale. They're looking for people who genuinely enjoy building, want to take ownership and are excited by the challenge of helping grow a technology business. You'll be working alongside the team in their Dublin office five days a week. That's intentional. They want engineers collaborating closely, solving problems together, moving quickly and learning from each other. There will be periods of longer working days, particularly at this stage of growth. The ambition isn't for that intensity to last forever, but right now they're building something significant and want people who are excited to be part of that journey. In return, you'll get a level of ownership, technical exposure and influence that can be difficult to find in a larger organisation. What's on offer? items.card: Vos missions : imaginer, expérimenter, développer Intégré·e à un projet R&D en cours, vous participerez au développement de nouveaux outils et workflows IA dédiés à la création, depuis l'exploration d'une idée jusqu'à son intégration dans un prototype utilisable par un designer. Imaginer → Explorer → Assembler → Prototyper → Tester → Simplifier → Intégrer Concevoir de nouveaux workflows créatifs : imaginer comment
items.desc: Imaginer Les Nouveaux Outils Du Designer L'écosystème de l'IA évolue vite : nouveaux modèles open source, contrôle géométrique, vision par ordinateur, reconstruction 3D... Ces avancées ouvrent de nouvelles manières de dessiner, transformer, contrôler, visualiser et explorer un design. L'enjeu dépasse la simple génération d'images : comment masquer la complexité technique pour mettre la puissance de l'IA au service du geste créatif ? Nous recherchons un·e stagiaire curieux·se, créatif·ve et explorateur·rice pour intégrer un projet R&D dédié au design automobile, à la croisée de l'IA générative, de la computer vision, du développement Python et de la création automobile. Vos missions : imaginer, expérimenter, développer Intégré·e à un projet R&D en cours, vous participerez au développement de nouveaux outils et workflows IA dédiés à la création, depuis l'exploration d'une idée jusqu'à son intégration dans un prototype utilisable par un designer. Imaginer → Explorer → Assembler → Prototyper → Tester → Simplifier → Intégrer Concevoir de nouveaux workflows créatifs : imaginer comment l'IA peut enrichir ou transformer certaines étapes du processus de design : dessin, contrôle géométrique, exploration visuelle, transformation d'image, analyse, représentation 3D ou rendu. Assembler et détourner des briques open source : expérimenter avec Qwen, Stable Diffusion, ControlNet, LoRA, VLM/LLM, computer vision, Gaussian Splatting, reconstruction 3D ou d'autres technologies, et chercher comment les connecter ou les utiliser au-delà de leur usage initial. Développer et prototyper : construire ces expériences avec ComfyUI, Python, Diffusers, PyTorch, OpenCV ou des APIs, modifier des pipelines existants et développer les briques manquantes lorsque nécessaire. Adapter et spécialiser les modèles : expérimenter l'entraînement de LoRA, ControlNet ou ControlNet-LoRA, le conditionnement visuel, la segmentation ou d'autres approches permettant d'obtenir davantage de contrôle et de cohérence. Transformer l'expérimentation en outil de design : évaluer les résultats du point de vue du créatif et chercher à rendre les technologies développées simples, fluides et contrôlables, en masquant autant que possible leur complexité technique. Cette démarche s'accompagnera naturellement d'une veille active de l'écosystème open source : découvrir de nouveaux modèles, méthodes, repositories et outils, évaluer leur potentiel et identifier les briques susceptibles d'améliorer ou de faire évoluer les workflows développés. Profil Profil recherché : un profil explorateur École d'ingénieur, d'informatique, école de design ou formation hybride (design computationnel, creative coding...) : votre curiosité, votre capacité à expérimenter et vos projets personnels comptent autant que votre diplôme. Culture Generative AI & open source : vous êtes familier·ère de ComfyUI, Hugging Face, GitHub, Stable Diffusion/Qwen et de technologies comme ControlNet, LoRA, VLM/LLM. Vous aimez explorer de nouveaux outils et comprendre comment les combiner. Prototypage : Python est ici un outil d'exploration et de création. Vous savez naviguer dans un repository, adapter du code existant, connecter des APIs et construire rapidement une expérimentation avec des outils comme Diffusers, PyTorch ou OpenCV. Culture visuelle et outils créatifs : vous avez une sensibilité à l'image, au dessin, aux proportions, aux volumes, à la perspective et à la 3D. Une pratique de Photoshop, du sketch numérique, de la 3D ou d'autres outils de création visuelle constitue un vrai plus. Intérêt pour le design automobile : vous êtes curieux·se des problématiques propres au car design et comprenez que le respect d'une intention, d'une géométrie ou d'un geste créatif peut être plus important qu'un résultat simplement spectaculaire. État d'esprit : autonome, curieux·se et analytique, vous aimez expérimenter, comparer plusieurs approches et vous demander : « Cette technologie a été conçue pour cela… mais que pourrait-on en faire d'autre ? » Comment candidater ? Au-delà du CV, nous serons attentifs aux projets et expérimentations qui témoignent de votre curiosité et de votre capacité à explorer par vous-même : workflows ComfyUI, entraînements LoRA, prototypes Python, contributions ou explorations GitHub, expérimentations 3D, projets mêlant IA et création, détournements ou assemblages de technologies open source. Quelques exemples accompagnés d'une courte présentation de votre démarche, des choix techniques effectués et des résultats obtenus permettront de mieux apprécier votre profil. items.desc: At Casino Vibe , we create entertainment for players who love casino gaming. About the Role We're looking for an AI Engineer specialized in building production-grade agentic systems on Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK. This is a builder role, not a prompting role: you'll design multi-agent architectures, custom tools, and deterministic guardrails that turn LLMs into reliable automation for real business workflows. Responsibilities Design and orchestrate multi-agent architectures : decompose complex workflows into isolated subagents (explore, verify, write), each with its own context, reporting only conclusions to the orchestrator Parallelize agent work while protecting the main agent's context window from pollution Design and build custom tools (MCP servers, functions, APIs): define what to expose, at what granularity, with model-readable descriptions and context-efficient outputs Iterate on tool ergonomics based on observed agent behavior — diagnose why an agent fails or loops, and fix it at the tool/architecture level Implement context management strategies: summarization, delegation, persistent memory (CLAUDE.md, knowledge files) Build deterministic guardrails with hooks (pre/post-command validation, logging, output checks) Script the glue: automation in Python/Bash/Node around agentic pipelines Must-Have Requirements Hands-on experience with Claude Code and/or Claude Agent SDK in real projects (not tutorials) Proven tool design experience: you've built MCP servers or custom tool integrations and can show them Demonstrated subagent/multi-agent orchestration : you can explain how you split tasks, isolated contexts, and merged results Strong scripting skills: Python, Bash, Node Solid software engineering fundamentals: Git, testing, CI/CD, API design Fluent English (written and spoken) Based in Malta or Europe, Fully Remote Nice to Have Published MCP servers, Claude Code plugins, or skills (public repos are your CV) Experience with hooks and deterministic guardrails around LLM systems Familiarity with evals and benchmarking of agent performance Experience integrating agents with business tools (Slack, CRM, ticketing, databases) How We'll Evaluate You Live exercise : a real automation task in Claude Code (1–2h, screen share) — architecture decisions matter more than speed. Deep-dive interview: walk us through an agent you built — what tools you gave it, how you managed context on long tasks, what guardrails you set.

items.desc: Founding Machine Learning Engineer London (2–3 days per week in office) Up to £120k + equity I'm working with an early-stage startup building AI-driven products at scale, and I'm looking for a founding Machine Learning Engineer to join a small, highly technical team. You’ll be the person who makes their models actually work in production - designing and building robust data/ML pipelines, deploying deep learning and LLM workloads efficiently on self‑hosted GPUs, and using modern “agentic coding” workflows to move fast without creating mountains of technical debt. What you’ll do: Design, build and own end‑to‑end ML and data pipelines (from data ingestion to production serving). Deploy and run deep learning models (including LLMs/embeddings) efficiently across multiple GPUs. Implement and optimise large‑scale batch and/or streaming computations (millions of items, daily). Use modern AI‑assisted / agentic development workflows (context management, tool use, code generation) to accelerate high‑quality engineering. Ship reliable production software: testing, monitoring, observability, and performance tuning. Work hands‑on across the stack of ML systems (training, evaluation, serving) rather than narrow research. Collaborate closely with the founders on technical direction and architecture, acting as a core early team member. What I'm looking for: Master’s (or equivalent) in a STEM field (e.g. Computer Science, Maths, Physics, Engineering). ~3–6 years of post‑graduate experience as a Software/ML/MLOps Engineer (not a pure research role). Strong Python engineering skills and a solid grasp of core computer science. Proven experience building and shipping production software and data/ML pipelines. Hands‑on experience running deep learning models on GPUs (multi‑GPU and/or distributed setups). Understanding of modern ML/LLM concepts (embeddings, tokenisation, context, serving) and how to make them efficient in practice. Comfort working independently in a small, fast‑moving startup environment, taking ownership across the whole pipeline rather than a tiny slice. Nice to have: Experience with LLM serving and optimisation on self‑hosted GPU clusters. Prior early‑stage startup experience. Broad systems understanding (from storage/query to model serving and APIs). How they work: Early founding role with significant impact on product and architecture. 2–3 days per week in their London office; the rest can be remote. Lean, engineering‑driven culture focused on building things well the first time and avoiding unnecessary technical debt. If you’re a hands‑on engineer who loves building real systems with modern ML (rather than writing papers) and you want to be an integral early member of a company, I’d like to hear from you.

items.card: You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition
items.desc:
Mission 
 We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student in the Laloui Group at EPFL inLausanne. The group brings expertise in geomaterials and their mechanical behaviour to research at theinterface of material science and engineering applications.
 You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition and excavationmaterials into materials suitable for digital fabrication under ambient conditions.
 Digital fabrication methods, including extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying, offer opportunities to controlmaterial placement and curing, create complex geometries and reduce material consumption. Integratingbiomineralization into pumpable, extrudable and sprayable granular materials remains largely unexplored. ThisPhD will investigate the coupled biogeochemical, rheological and mechanical mechanisms governing particledeposition, mineral precipitation and hardening.
 Main duties and responsibilities 
 As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:
 Take full responsibility for your dissertation and the progress of your research.
 Conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at EPFL and ETH Zurich and, whereapplicable, industry partners.
 Design and execute experiments, and analyze and interpret experimental results.
 Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present your findings at internationalconferences.
 Participate in teaching and supervise student projects.
 More specifically, within this project, you will:
 Investigate the rheology and processability of granular materials, including yield stress, plastic viscosity,thixotropy, water content, ageing and particle interactions.
 Study microbial activity and biologically driven mineral precipitation, and determine how evolving mineralphases affect mechanical hardening and material performance.
 Characterize the coupling between biogeochemical reactions, rheological properties and mechanicalbehaviour over space and time.
 Connect experimental findings to extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying in collaboration with thedigital fabrication team at ETH Zurich.
 Profile 
 An MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering or aclosely related discipline.
 A background in mechanics and the strength of solid materials, or materials science applied to the builtenvironment, is particularly welcome.
 Experience in rheology, granular or cementitious materials, experimental mechanics, materialcharacterization, geomechanics, mineralogy, or organic and inorganic chemistry is an advantage.Expertise across all these fields is neither expected nor required.
 Interest in experimental and interdisciplinary research, and in translating fundamental physical andchemical understanding into new construction technologies.
 Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team across disciplines and institutions.
 Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eagerness to learn, good organizational skills and rigor in experimentalwork.
 A high level of motivation for academic research.
 Fluency in English is essential.
 We offer 
 At EPFL, we believe that people achieve great results when they feel supported, respected and enabled tosucceed. By joining our community, you will help shape the future of society through education, research andinnovation. We offer an inspiring, international and collaborative environment where your work has real impact and your ideas are valued. Combined with flexible ways of working and attractive employment conditions, weaim to create an environment where everyone can contribute, grow and make a difference.
 Beyond work, our campuses host a vibrant community and unique environment, enriched by initiativespromoting equality, inclusion, diversity, well-being and sustainability as well as an engaging program ofcultural, sports and community activities throughout the year.
 Read about our employment conditions and employee benefits.
 Informations

items.desc:
Nevral Forensics Intelligence (NFI) | Research Partner Program | REMOTE (worldwide)
NFI is a digital forensics platform for laboratories that keep evidence on their own premises, under their own law. I am the founder. We are building, from first principles, a lawful device-access capability for locked devices, delivered to licensed laboratories only through signed Capability Packs. The software enforces the legal gate itself: a locked-tier extraction is refused unless the operator first records a court-order authorization, bound to the case and the device in a signed, hash-chained record, before any method runs.
Stated plainly: this program starts from zero proven capability, and our public claims stay "no unlocking" until a method is proven. Research runs only on devices the researcher or the company owns.
Instead of a job posting, this is a research exchange. Independent researchers and laboratories who join as research partners receive the NFI platform at no charge while they are active partners, plus Academy access. In return, partners share the device-access research they produce on owned devices: methods, findings, and limits. We validate shared research on our own reference devices to a fixed proof standard, write proven methods into our coverage matrix with the contributor credited, and only then productize them into Capability Packs. Unproven research ships nowhere.
The conditions are the same ones our own team works under, and they do not bend: owned devices only; the court-order gate on every locked-tier extraction; responsible disclosure; and plain disqualifiers, because they are continuing conditions of partnership: no history of selling exploits to brokers for offensive use, no involvement in the stolen-data trade, no work on devices the program does not own.
The bar is evidence, not polish: published vulnerability research on mobile platforms, CVE credits or equivalent credited disclosures, or a verifiable laboratory record. The research tracks are MediaTek, Unisoc, Qualcomm, Apple, Samsung, and passcode recovery, weighted toward the devices our markets actually seize.
Apply: email info@nevrallab.com with links to your published research and your CVE credits, or your laboratory's equivalent record. That evidence is the application.

items.desc: Associated with 2 categories Associated with 2 categories See allSee all Stage-Machine Learning pour la planification proactive des ressources d'un service cloud F/H Associated with 2 categories Data & AI IT & Engineering 44-46 Avenue de la République, 92320 CHATILLON Location: CHÂTILLON,FRANCE 2026-55352 Internship Not Specified Orange SA Publication date : Nov 10, 2026, 6:36PM Contract duration : 6 months Dans ce stage, nous nous intéresserons au «capacity planning » d’un service cloud, qui consiste à anticiper, de manière proactive, les ressources nécessaires à son bon fonctionnement. L’activation des ressources n’étant pas instantanée, une décision trop tardive peut dégrader la qualité de service ; à l’inverse, une réservation excessive augmente les dépenses. S’ajoutent les bénéfices d’une réservation anticipée et les coûts liés aux modifications successives d’un plan de capacités. Le problème sera donc abordé dans une perspective « cost-sensitive » : prendre des décisions qui minimisent l’ensemble des coûts opérationnels, et non les seules erreurs de prévision. Dans le prolongement de nos travaux sur la classification précoce de séries temporelles, nous étudierons une architecture de prise de décision séquentielle inspirée des modèles à espace d’états. Les décisions s’appuieront sur une représentation évolutive du système, tenant compte: (i) des observations disponibles de charge, (ii) de l’incertitude sur la charge future et (iii) des engagements déjà pris pour la réservation de capacités futures. À mesure que de nouvelles informations arrivent, le plan de capacités pourra être conservé ou révisé. L’apprentissage par renforcement fera notamment partie de l’architecture cible, et sera exploré pour tenir compte des conséquences à long terme des décisions. Le stage débutera par un état de l’art sur l’autoscaling prédictif, la prévision probabiliste et la décision séquentielle. Il se poursuivra par le développement d’un simulateur à la fois de données et de modèles synthétiques de prévision probabiliste. L’architecture cible sera ensuite prototypée, permettant la mise au point de différentes stratégies de décision séquentielle et d’apprentissage en ligne. Notamment, la comparaison entre une stratégie myope, minimisant le coût attendu à «t+1», et une politique apprise par renforcement dans le but de minimiser les coûts à long terme fera partie des expérimentations. Enfin, des études d’ablation permettront d’évaluer: (i) l’apport des informations utilisées en entrée de la politique de décision; (ii) l’intérêt de la non-myopie lorsque les coûts de révision sont importants; (iii) la robustesse de l’approche face à une variété d’hypothèses sur les délais d’activation. Ces expérimentations constitueront une première étape scientifique vers une thèse CIFRE. __PRESENT BAC + 5, Master informatique et/ou statistiques ou école d’ingénieur. Fort intérêt pour la recherche et volonté affirmée de poursuivre en thèse CIFRE. Compétences : maîtrise de Python et de Scikit-learn, bonnes bases en probabilités, statistiques et apprentissage statistique. Une première expérience en séries temporelles ou en apprentissage par renforcement serait appréciée __PRESENT Vous serez accueilli au sein d’une équipe composée de chercheurs en Machine Learning et de Data Scientists dans une direction d’innovation. Ce stage est conçu comme une première étape vers une thèse CIFRE, sous réserve des validations nécessaires. __PRESENT Vous rejoindrez l'équipe ADIS (AI & Data Innovation Services) au sein du département AI Factory, le pôle d'expertise et d'innovation en Intelligence Artificielle d'Orange, situé au cœur de l'écosystème de recherche et d’innovation d'Orange Gardens. Notre mission est d'explorer les technologies de pointe, de développer des preuves de concept à forte valeur ajoutée et de construire les briques logicielles qui seront déployées dans les différentes entités du Groupe. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrerez une équipe dynamique et passionnée, où vous collaborerez avec des experts en data, software, cloud et architecture. items.desc: AI & Full-Stack Web Developer Location: Chelsea Harbour, London Working arrangement: Office-based, Monday–Friday Job type: Full-time, permanent Salary: Negotiable depending on experience About the Role We are looking for a highly capable, hands-on AI & Full-Stack Web Developer to join our growing business and take responsibility for the development, management, maintenance and ongoing improvement of our websites, digital platforms and technology infrastructure. This is an opportunity for someone who genuinely understands modern web development, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and digital operations. We operate multiple websites and platforms across property, automotive, technology and consumer services. Our infrastructure includes AWS cloud environments, Next.js applications, integrated Machine Learning APIs and MySQL databases. We need an experienced developer who can work independently, identify problems, implement solutions and take ownership of our entire digital ecosystem. This is an office-based role, five days a week, working directly with management. Key Responsibilities 1. Full-Stack Web Development Manage and develop all company websites and digital platforms. Frontend and backend development. Work with Next.js, React, JavaScript and modern development frameworks. Maintain and improve MySQL databases and backend systems. Develop new features, functionality and integrations. Troubleshoot bugs, errors and performance issues. 2. AWS & Cloud Infrastructure Manage and maintain AWS infrastructure and hosting environments. Review server architecture, security and access permissions. Monitor performance, availability and infrastructure costs. Manage deployments, backups and cloud configurations. Identify vulnerabilities and implement security improvements. Work with external developers and security auditors where necessary. 3. AI & Automation Implement AI solutions across our businesses. Develop and integrate AI APIs and machine learning functionality. Build automated business workflows using n8n, Make, Zapier and similar platforms. Explore and implement AI agents and automation tools. Identify opportunities to streamline operations using AI. 4. SEO & Digital Performance Manage technical SEO across all websites. Improve website speed, indexing and search visibility. Review Google Search Console and Google Analytics. Implement tracking, analytics and conversion improvements. Work on website structure, metadata and technical optimisation. 5. CRM & Digital Operations Manage and improve CRM systems and integrations. Automate lead management and customer communications. Integrate third-party platforms, APIs and business tools. Oversee the technical side of day-to-day digital operations. Skills & Experience Required Strong full-stack development experience. Excellent knowledge of JavaScript, React and Next.js. Practical AWS experience, including cloud infrastructure and security. Experience with MySQL and database management. Knowledge of API development and third-party integrations. Experience with AI tools, LLMs and machine learning APIs. Familiarity with n8n, Make, Zapier or similar automation platforms. Good understanding of technical SEO and website optimisation. Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities. Ability to manage multiple websites and projects independently. The Ideal Candidate We are looking for someone proactive, commercially minded and technically capable who enjoys taking responsibility. You should be comfortable working across different technologies, managing existing platforms, developing new products and finding better ways to use AI to improve business operations. We are not looking for someone who only specialises in one area of development. We need an all-round technology professional who can manage the complete digital environment. Working Arrangements Full-time, Monday to Friday. Office-based position at our Chelsea Harbour premises in London. Working directly with company management. Immediate start preferred. How to Apply Please send the following to ap@aphomesltd.co.uk : Your CV, examples of websites or platforms you have developed, and a brief overview of your experience with AWS, full-stack development and AI automation. We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate real-world experience managing live websites, cloud infrastructure and AI-powered applications. Application question(s): Please only apply for in person position. This is not a remote role Work Location: In person

You will work directly with teams across the business to understand their needs, design the right solution, build and refine it, and take it all the way into production and adoption. The AI Office is led by Maria, our VP of AI Office. You will work closely with the rest of the team and take ownership of AI projects from design and development through to successful implementation. As a Microsoft partner, we use the Microsoft ecosystem as the foundation for our solutions wherever it makes sense, rather than introducing new platforms unnecessarily. Et, aussi, là où les réponses sont à inventer ou à réinventer : lutte anti-drones, cybersécurité Notre esprit Tech et pragmatique, ainsi que notre agilité d’ETI nous permettent d’allier proximité, engagement, agilité et innovation, pour diffuser notre culture à tous les niveaux : dans la relation client, dans le mode de management interne, dans notre engagement social et environnemental… Nous accordons une importance particulière au développement professionnel de nos collaborateurs. Chez CS GROUP, chaque employé bénéficie d'un accompagnement personnalisé pour construire sa carrière, avec des opportunités d'évolution. Nous favorisons la mobilité, la formation continue et encourageons l'innovation à tous les niveaux de l'organisation. Notre culture d'entreprise est fondée sur l'engagement, la proximité et l'excellence technique, offrant à chacun la possibilité de s'épanouir dans un environnement stimulant et bienveillant. Pour plus d’information, retrouvez-nous sur LinkedIin, Facebook & Instagram ou visitez https://www.csgroup.eu/fr/ \n\n Description de l'entreprise CS, filiale du groupe Sopra Steria, est un acteur technologique de référence dans la conception, l’intégration et l’exploitation de systèmes critiques. Présents dans 7 pays avec plus de 2600 collaborateurs passionnés, nous intervenons au cœur des enjeux de souveraineté, de sécurité et de performance, dans des secteurs stratégiques tels que la défense, le spatial, l’énergie, l’industrie, le transport, l’aéronautique et la cybersécurité. Notre différence ? Une expertise unique en systèmes temps réel, des solutions souveraines et durables, et une culture d’innovation forte, portée par 15 % de notre chiffre d’affaires investi en R&D. Nous accompagnons nos clients dans la réussite de leurs programmes les plus complexes, du contrôle aérien à la lutte anti-drones, en passant par les systèmes nucléaires et les centres de contrôle satellites. En rejoignant CS, vous intégrez une entreprise humaine et innovante. Nous livrons bien plus que des systèmes, nous bâtissons la confiance. Nous allons au-delà des besoins exprimés, nous préparons les défis de demain. Plus que de simples experts, nous façonnons l’innovation. Protéger les territoires, anticiper les menaces. Forte de plus de 840 collaborateurs répartis sur l’ensemble du territoire, elle conçoit des systèmes critiques pour l’armée et l’aviation civile. Nos équipes interviennent sur des projets à haute valeur ajoutée : liaisons de données tactiques, lutte anti-drones, surveillance maritime, simulation et entraînement, sûreté aérienne. Grâce à notre expertise et à notre engagement dans des programmes internationaux, nous contribuons activement à la sécurité des territoires. Rejoindre cette Business Unit, c’est contribuer à la protection des citoyens au sein d’un collectif engagé. Description du poste Au sein de la BU Défense & Sécurité de CS GROUP, l’agence Systèmes Opérationnels et Interopérabilité d’Aix-en-Provence recherche un stagiaire de niveau Bac+5 issu d’une école d’ingénieurs. items.desc: Vill du omsätta AI-idéer till testbara prototyper och bidra till nästa generations intelligenta fordonssystem? Här får du möjlighet att arbeta nära verksamhetsexperter och omvandla AI-idéer till konkreta prototyper. Du blir en del av ett utforskande team hos en internationell aktör inom fordonsindustrin, där teknisk genomförbarhet och mätbar nytta står i fokus. Om rollen Driv AI-prototyping och förstudier för framtida fordonssystem. Utvärdera hur AI kan skapa nytta inom exempelvis fordonsdynamik, energihantering och intelligenta användarupplevelser. Arbeta i tidiga utvecklingsfaser med fokus på teknisk genomförbarhet och affärsvärde. Det här kommer du göra Bygga och testa prototyper med verklig eller simulerad data. Definiera och utvärdera KPI: er för effektivitet, prestanda, robusthet och komplexitet. Jämföra resultat med befintliga lösningar och relevanta moderna metoder. Bedöma datatillgång, beräknings- och latenskrav samt integrationskomplexitet. Dokumentera resultat och bidra med underlag för beslut om fortsatt utveckling. Vi söker dig som har Utbildning inom AI, datavetenskap, robotik, teknik eller närliggande område. Tidigare erfarenhet från projekt, examensarbete eller annan praktisk utveckling inom AI och maskininlärning. God förståelse för maskininlärning, utvärderingsmått, överanpassning och experimentupplägg. Erfarenhet av eller intresse för datorseende, mönsterigenkänning eller djupinlärning. Förmåga att strukturera öppna frågeställningar och samarbeta med ämnesexperter. Teknik & Verktyg Python samt PyTorch, TensorFlow eller Keras. Pandas, NumPy och Jupyter Notebooks. MLflow, Git, Docker och grundläggande CI/CD. Meriterande: LangChain, Dify, vLLM och LLaMA-baserade verktyg. Simuleringsverktyg och fordonsdata beroende på användningsområde. Praktisk information Ort: Göteborg. Arbetssätt: Framgår vid dialog. Språk: Engelska.

Do you want to build the coding agent that Swiss Post developers work with every day, and shape what it knows, what it may do and how it gets better? Then you might be exactly who we're looking for. Swiss Post IT is changing how software gets built: AI agents take over a growing part of the work, while people set the intent, review and steer. Our developers already use coding agents today. With you, we turn that into a Swiss Post coding agent an enterprise can rely on. How you make a difference You specify, build, test and ship our coding agent, pre-configured with skills, prompt templates, rules and plugins. In addition, you curate the baseline configuration and our library of skills, so that teams get a version they can trust: reviewed, versioned and easy to roll back. You write evals for skills, prompts and agent workflows, so that every change shows whether it makes the agent better or just different. At the same time you build guardrails into the agent itself, such as permissions, sandboxing and hooks, so that the safe way is also the easy way. You connect our internal systems via MCP and evaluate new large language models against the work our developers actually do. Moreover, you work with the pilot teams and the growing number of engineers who use the agent every day, and turn what you learn into better skills and defaults. What you have to offer You have several years of hands-on software engineering experience, for example in Python, TypeScript, Go or Java, including APIs and CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions. In addition, you have practical experience building with LLMs and coding agents beyond the chat window: skills, prompts, tools, MCP servers or agent workflows that others actually use. You have experience applying GenAI tools pragmatically in real software engineering work, with a clear understanding of where they help and where engineering judgment is still required. Moreover, you bring a security mindset for agents, including secrets, dependencies, permissions, input and output controls and data protection. You have a very good spoken and written command of English and Knowledge of another national language is a plus. You don't need to tick every box. If you bring a strong engineering foundation and have built something real with AI agents, we'd like to hear from you. We care more about how you think and how you learn than about a perfect keyword match. Help us transform our company into the "Swiss Post of tomorrow"! items.desc: Do you want to shape the future of plastics processing intelligent automation? Are you an expert in intelligent automation and data processing and ready to turn ideas into impact and grow with us? VTT might be just the place for you. VTT is one of the leading applied research organizations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning, and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2000 brilliant minds from 55+ different nationalities focus on creating impact through science-based innovation. Get to know us further by exploring VTT's tech & infra . We are now looking for Senior Scientist focusing on intelligent automation to join our materials processing and circular solutions team. In this role, you will strengthen our capabilities in process automation, data acquisition, and data-driven process control for plastics processing and recycling. You will work hands-on with pilot-scale equipment, particularly extrusion and plastics pre-treatment processes, developing solutions that connect process and sensor data with automation, control and online analytics. You will apply data-driven and machine-learning methods to process and sensor data, for example to derive online quality metrics and enable smarter process control. Your work will initially focus on extrusion-based process control and the automation and digitalization of plastics pre-treatment, including washing and sorting. You will also contribute to connecting our laboratory and pilot-scale equipment and their data to broader data architectures. Depending on your interests, there will be opportunities to develop new research directions beyond these initial applications. "We have a healthy work culture where you can be yourself, share your views, and improve things without fear of making mistakes - that’s what makes the work truly meaningful. " -Your new Team Leader Marjaana Mussalo- Our team is located in VTT’s Industrial Chemistry research area and focuses on the development of thermoplastic materials, their processing, and sensor-, spectroscopy- and software-enabled process control methods. Our target is to advance sustainable thermoplastic materials and products with high performance and increased circularity. We have unique pilot facilities for thermoplastic compounding, pre-industrial converting, and material characterization. In addition to these, we have unique pilot opportunities for identifying, sorting, washing and advanced mechanical recycling of plastic waste. The Material Processing and Circular Solutions team works in close collaboration with our customers and other research teams at VTT with business development and customer-oriented approach. The position is located in Tampere. As Senior Scientist, you will: work very closely with process automation and data flows. programme and implement the process automation yourself. process and analyze research data using appropriate digital tools (e.g. MATLAB, Python, R or equivalent). apply your digitalisation experience in plastics processing and/or plastics recycling build professional networks and act as a thought leader in your area of expertise. Who we are looking for: You have a Master of Science degree in a relevant field or equivalent science experience. A doctoral degree is considered as an asset. You have strong expertise and experience in intelligent automation and data processing. For example experience with OPC-UA and programming in Python or MATLAB is especially relevant. You are interested in taking forward interdisciplinary transition of plastics processing towards data driven, model-based, machine learning supported and AI-ready system You have good communication skills in English and ability to build high value research collaboration in the area It’s an advantage if you also have some of the following: Experience with PLC systems, Beckhoff/TwinCAT, Siemens automation, databases, or related industrial data technologies Experience in plastics processing and/or plastics recycling Experience with EU and Business Finland projects Applied expertise in sensor technologies As a person, we hope that you are: Innovative, flexible and adaptable Proactive, efficient, solution-oriented and independent Good at working under pressure A team player with good collaboration skills. With VTT, you’ll enjoy: Visionary work in technology. Fascinating projects, excellent research environment. Great career opportunities, superb colleagues. Support for your well-being. Apply now and join our community of brilliant minds! Please send your CV and answer the short pre-screening questions together with your salary request via our recruitment system as soon as possible but at the latest by 25 November 2026. We will process applications as they come in and fill the position as soon as we find the right candidate. A security clearance procedure may be conducted during the recruitment …

items.desc: Campaign Automation Specialist About our Team Elsevier is a global provider of science and health information, serving more than 30 million scientists, students, and health and information professionals worldwide. Headquartered in Amsterdam, we employ more than 7,000 people across 24 countries and provide information and tools that help customers advance science and health, make critical decisions, improve productivity, and achieve better outcomes. Our Science, Technology and Medical (STM) Journals division manages an extensive portfolio of high-impact scientific journals, with responsibility for their reputation among authors and the quality of published content. More than 80 marketing professionals worldwide collaborate across the organisation to identify opportunities and deliver effective marketing strategies. Within STM Journals, the Email Marketing Operations team supports the set-up and deployment of data-driven email campaigns, primarily for content acquisition and journal author enablement, helping accelerate highly cited open access and subscription growth. The global team of ten covers email production and data management. About the Role We are seeking a Campaign Automation Specialist to support the STM Journals marketing organisation with the set-up and deployment of data-driven email campaigns. The role focuses mainly on content acquisition for Gold Open Access and hybrid journals and includes curating high volumes of target audience data from internal sources. You will improve operational efficiency by developing optimal data workflows and introducing automation where possible. Using a test-and-learn approach, you will continuously refine workflows in line with business objectives. The role reports directly to the Head of Campaign Management in STM Journal Marketing. Responsibilities Analyse and query large datasets using SQL/Python and tools such as AWS Athena, Knime and DBeaver. Develop scalable, reproducible workflows for data extraction, processing, ETL and email campaign segmentation. Partner with campaign owners to translate business objectives into technical requirements and effective audience segmentation strategies. Build and maintain target/content data and automated workflows for recurring STM Journals email campaigns. Set up, test and deploy email campaigns, including appropriate tracking for web traffic and attribution reporting. Develop strong knowledge of core databases and key STM Journals marketing data sources, advising marketers on optimal segmentation and data quality. Interpret complex data and present clear, concise insights to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Manage incoming campaign requests, assess production readiness and collaborate with analytics colleagues to improve shared knowledge and processes. Requirements University degree or equivalent in data analytics, marketing or a related discipline, with at least a few years experience in an analyst or marketing operations role. Experience in data-driven marketing, customer segmentation and handling large datasets, with a basic understanding of data protection standards. Proficiency with data and analytics tools such as Excel, Knime and Tableau. Experience building and executing email campaign workflows using a major deployment platform such as Salesforce or Adobe Campaign. Working knowledge of email and web analytics, A/B testing principles, and email/web technologies across browsers and platforms. Programming/coding skills in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQL and Python. Strong organisation, prioritisation, problem-solving and collaboration skills, with the ability to manage deadlines and multiple priorities. Strong written and verbal communication skills, stakeholder management capability, and an interest in learning new marketing technologies, tools and processes. What We Offer Competitive salary and flexible/hybrid working arrangements. Additional benefits, including memberships to Elsevier’s publications and discounts on books. Access to various training, coaching, and e-learning modules for long-term career development. Engagement in social responsibility programs that leverage knowledge and strengths to improve education, science, healthcare, and environmental sustainability. Work in a Way That Works for You We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals. Working Pattern Working flexible hours – flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive. items.desc: Business Controller – iLottery Location: Krakow, Poland Reports to: VP Group Finance - EMEA At the heart of our organisation is a commitment to delivering innovative, high-quality outcomes that create lasting value for our customers and partners. We foster a collaborative culture grounded in accountability, continuous improvement, and partnership—core to how we operate and succeed. As we continue to evolve our global finance operating model, controllership is increasingly focused on ownership, insight, and business partnership , rather than transactional execution. Within this model, centralised Accounting Operations teams deliver scalable, standardised processes, while Business Controllers act as senior finance leaders accountable for financial outcomes, balance sheet integrity, and commercial insight . This role represents a pivotal opportunity to be the Business Controller for our Lotteries business, which is a key growth driver for Aristocrat, with complex multi-entity operations. You will manage the entire balance sheet and collaborate closely with senior colleagues to drive financial performance, oversee risk, and aid decision-making. You will be at the intersection of finance operations and commercial finance. You will bring challenge, insight, and judgement. You will draw on a centralised Accounting Operations team for transactional and close execution. For a finance leader who thrives in dynamic environments and enjoys combining technical depth with commercial thinking, this is an opportunity to play a critical role in shaping a modern, forward-looking controllership function. What You'll Do Own the integrity, quality, and performance of the balance sheet for the Lotteries business. items.desc: Who we are Mine Environment Management (MEM) is an award-winning specialist geoscience and environmental engineering consultancy headquartered in Wales, UK. In April, MEM joined Ecology Group, a growing group of ecological and environmental consultancies. This partnership brings continued investment in technology, professional development and long-term growth, while allowing MEM to retain the culture we have built since 2018: a highly specialised and motivated technical team working in a supportive, relaxed environment. As part of MEM, you will also have opportunities to collaborate with a wider network of specialists across the Group and further develop your expertise. We provide practical, commercially focused solutions for the global mining industry across the full mine life cycle, from planning and operations through to closure and regeneration. MEM was founded to apply sound scientific principles to the development of innovative solutions for managing mining environments and mine waste. Our team is currently delivering a range of innovative commercial and research projects internationally, often in partnership with specialist UK technical companies and universities. These projects span carbon sequestration, mine water quality assessment and treatment, tailings facility management, operational mine waste management and mine closure planning. To support your professional growth, our leadership team actively encourages and sponsors our geoscientists to author scientific papers and present their findings at major global conferences. Acid and metalliferous drainage: Plan and manage site investigations and environmental geochemistry risk assessments. Operational planning: Review geochemical drill-hole assay databases, block models and waste schedules to develop operational waste placement concepts and facility cover systems. Research, development and publications: Initiate and manage research and development projects including those relating to mine water treatment, with opportunities to prepare scientific papers and conference presentations. You will hold at least a BSc in a geoscience-related discipline and have a minimum of three years’ post-graduate technical experience, ideally within a mining consultancy. Please make clear which pillar you are most interested in. Job description The AI Economics Institute (AIEI) is a joint research organisation of HM Treasury and the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet (OPMC). The AIEI has been established to build and maintain the analytical capability needed to put the UK government at the forefront of understanding AIs economic impacts. Announced by the Chancellor in the March 2026 Mais Lecture and launched in June 2026, it is the first government-backed institute of its kind in the world. AI has the potential to substantially reshape the structure of firms, sectors, and labour markets. The opportunities are extraordinary. AI could drive productivity gains and unlock new sources of growth. At the same time, the transition also carries risks depending on the pace of technological development and how the economy adapts. The AIEI exists to build the data infrastructure, research capability and external relationships needed to assess these impacts rigorously and at pace, and to ensure the resulting evidence informs policy makers. The Institute will assess both opportunities and risks under a range of scenarios, examining how AI affects productivity, labour markets, firms, growth and the income distribution, with particular attention to how the gains are shared across regions, income groups, sectors and generations. The AIEI is not a policy-setting body. UK government departments remain responsible for policy decisions in response to AI. The Institutes role is to improve the quality and timeliness of the evidence and analysis on which those decisions rest. It focuses on priorities where it has a comparative advantage as a research institute at the heart of government, avoiding duplication of work that can happen equally well elsewhere, and engaging widely with academia, business and civil society to inform its work and contribute to public understanding. The AIEI is modelled on the AI Security Institute, particularly in its research focus, its approach to bringing in external talent, and its access to advanced tools. It is a small, high-calibre organisation, planning to grow to around 35 FTE by the end of its first year. It will bring together talented civil servants with Research Economists who have hands-on experience of delivering frontier economic research. It is chaired by Nobel Prize winning economist and former Chief Economist of the IMF, Simon Johnson. A world-first ambition is to link private sector data, including AI usage data, to government administrative data, providing a unique and rich data ecosystem for empirical research. The Institutes ambitions for developing world leading macroeconomic modelling capability are similarly high. The two research pillars The AIEIs research function is organised around two complementary pillars set out in the published prospectus. All four role types in this campaign are being recruited into one of these two pillars, depending on the specialism of the candidate: Data & Empirical Research - developing the data infrastructure, measurement frameworks and empirical research needed to establish an evidence-based picture of AIs economic effects as they develop, including causal analysis of AIs impacts on productivity, labour markets, firms and workers. Modelling & Scenarios - connecting potential pathways for AIs development and adoption to economy-wide outcomes, building cutting edge economic models and plausible but stretching scenarios, testing assumptions, and ensuring policy conclusions are robust to the uncertainty that remains. items.desc: Job title: Research Assistant – Mental Health Mapping (INTERNAL POST) Department: Anthropology, Media and Gender Studies Contract Type: Casual – 12 weeks (14/12/[2026 and 14/05/2027) Grade:6 Salary: £22.34 – £22.87 per hour inclusive of London allowance and holiday pay Location:Centre for Anthropology and Mental Health Research in Action (CAMHRA) Hours: 15 hours per week, 180 hours total SOAS University of London is the leading Higher Education institution in Europe specialising in the study of Asia, Africa and the Near and Middle East. SOAS University of London is positioned to play a leading role in reimagining higher education globally, with a new strategic plan in place as the basis for the renewal and revitalisation of the School which commits SOAS to both student responsiveness and research intensity. SOAS is moving towards a new model of international partnerships which is responsive to the transnational character of our global challenges. A bout the Role CAMHRA already collaborates with SOAS researchers from Anthropology, Media and Gender Studies. However, we do not have a complete mapping of colleagues across other SOAS departments and schools who work on distress, wellbeing, recovery, displacement, spirituality, care and addiction, perhaps without labelling it as mental health research. A wider, more epistemically diverse network of researchers across SOAS will help to ensure CAMHRA’s sustainability as a research centre, and support future applications for inter-disciplinary mental health research funding. MAP-MH@SOAS will systematically identify SOAS researchers who are interested in collaborating with CAMHRA. It will also develop an approach for critically articulating the economic benefit of mental health research, an increasingly important requirement for UKRI funding. It will convene two half-day workshops with CAMHRA colleagues to test where collaboration is possible. WP1: Mapping (December 2026 – May 2027). A research assistant with a critical mental health research background, supervised by Harriet Mossop (CAMHRA R&D Officer), will identify SOAS researchers outside SAMG whose work includes mental health. A long-list will be produced from a systematic, AI-enabled review of researchers’ Worktribe research profiles using key words (distress, wellbeing, etc). A short-list will be compiled from publication abstracts and conversations with researchers. Outputs: (1) a directory of short-listed researchers giving each researcher's focus, career stage, region, department, methods, and appetite for collaboration. EDI data will be collected with permission. (2) A visual map ‘MAP-MH@SOAS’ of the cross-SOAS mental health research ecology. (3) A document explaining and mapping this methodology for RKE to use across other research fields. . About the Department CAMHRA, located in the Department of Anthropology, Media and Gender Studies, is funded by a five-year Research England Expanding Excellence grant to develop infrastructure for anthropological research into mental health; the first such infrastructural funding to be received by SOAS. CAMHRA’s discipline-specific research is gaining strong traction with mental health providers, community groups and funders; increasingly, the Centre is also bringing anthropological approaches to collaborative, interdisciplinary work, and embedding About you You can find further information on the key criteria for the role in the Job Description and Person Specification, along with a full list of duties and responsibilities, which can be found on the SOAS website What We Offer: We are committed to providing a supportive and rewarding work environment. Flexible Working Arrangements: We recognise the importance of flexibility and offer options to help you manage your professional and personal commitments effectively. Health and Well-being Initiatives: Take advantage of our cycle to work scheme, eye tests, and season ticket loan to support your health and mobility. Enhanced Family Leave: We offer enhanced maternity, paternity & partner leave, and shared parental leave to support you during significant life events. Employee Assistance Programme: Access our confidential EAP for advice and support whenever needed. Discounted Gym Membership: Maintain your fitness with our discounted gym membership. We already work with several banks and lenders, and the AI we’ve built for them is award-winning. We’re looking for a product-focused AI developer, early in their career, who wants to build AI that people rely on. You’ll work closely with our AI experience lead, who shapes what Coach should do for an owner and how we judge whether it helped. Your part is to build it well, and to raise it early when part of the design doesn’t hold up once you see the data or how the model behaves. Coach works inside regulated institutions, so its answers have to be accurate, grounded in the owner’s own data and safe to show a customer. We’ll teach you the regulatory side of that work; prior experience in financial services isn’t needed. What you’ll work on Build and improve Coach’s AI features, including the insights and suggested actions owners see and the conversations they have with Coach, from prompt and retrieval design through to production code. Work with our AI experience lead to turn a design for how Coach should help an owner into something that works on real transaction data, and propose changes when the build shows the design needs them. Write evaluations for the features you build, so we can show both whether an answer is technically correct and whether an owner would find it useful. Build in the safeguards that regulated AI needs: answers grounded in the owner’s own data, guidance kept clear of financial advice, careful handling of personal data, and a clear point where a person takes over. Ship to production with the engineering team, working mainly in Python and TypeScript on Azure, with AI coding tools as a normal part of how we build. Look at how owners actually use what you’ve built, and bring what you learn into the next version. What we’re looking for Evidence that you’ve built and shipped software that uses large language models, whether at work, in research or in your own projects. A product focus: you judge your work by whether it helps the business owner using it, and you raise it when a specification won’t serve them well. Solid programming skills, ideally in Python, and a working understanding of how LLM applications fit together: prompting, retrieval, tool use, structured outputs and the ways each can fail. A habit of testing your own work, checking outputs against what should happen and looking for the cases where a system breaks. Clear writing about technical choices and trade-offs, so that colleagues outside engineering can follow your reasoning. This role suits someone in their first few years of building software, or someone who has recently finished a degree or master’s with substantial projects behind them. Experience with evaluation tools, Azure or a regulated industry would help. What success looks like In your first three months, you’ll understand how Coach works for an owner and for the bank behind it. You’ll have shipped improvements to at least one AI feature in production, and built the evaluations that show whether those improvements helped owners. As you build experience, you’ll take ownership of larger AI features from first design through to evaluation in production, with a learning plan you choose and agree with us. Pay and location €40,000 to €50,000, depending on experience, plus equity in Narrative. Full-time, hybrid working with three days a week in our office near the Harcourt Street Luas stop. Agreed time for learning, fortnightly progress reviews and regular one-to-ones. How to apply Send your CV or LinkedIn profile, a link to GitHub or any code you’re happy to share, and a short note about something you built with a language model: who it was for, how you checked it worked for them, and what you changed as a result. If you have a disability and need an adjustment to take part in the hiring process, such as extra time on an exercise, questions in advance or a different interview format, tell us at any stage.

items.desc: Turn data into insight and innovation that drives commercial outcomes. Joining the Data Analytics team, you will work at the intersection of technology, analytics and markets, developing data-driven solutions that help Commodities and Global Markets identify opportunities, enhance decision-making and unlock value across a global business. Working directly alongside front-office teams, you will gain exposure to real-world challenges and contribute to cutting-edge initiatives spanning data science, machine learning and quantitative analytics. We are a global financial services group operating in 30 markets with 57 years of unbroken profitability. At Macquarie, you’re empowered to shape a career that is fulfilling and creates value. You will bring your insights and expertise to the task at hand and feel supported as you make your own kind of impact for a better future. What role will you play? As a Junior Developer / Analyst within the Data Analytics team, you will apply your technical expertise to develop analytical tools, data products and quantitative models that support business growth and enhance decision-making across Commodities and Global Markets. Working closely with traders and business stakeholders on the trading floor, you will transform complex data into actionable insights, contribute to machine learning and anomaly detection initiatives, and help build scalable solutions that improve the visibility and management of client opportunities and business performance. Leveraging a broad technology stack, you will collaborate with colleagues across the business to deliver innovative analytics capabilities while developing deep domain expertise in global markets and data-driven problem solving. If you require additional assistance, please let us know during the application process.

items.title: Internship program 2027 - AI and ML Engineers
items.card: What you will do: Support the development and evaluation of Machine Learning models using Python and frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and scikit-learn. Work with structured and unstructured data in Databricks and enterprise data platforms, helping prepare datasets and engineer features for ML solutions. Assist in building and maintaining reusable ML pipelines for model training, testing and deployment.
items.desc: We’re looking for motivated ML and AI Engineer interns, located in Sofia! Who is this for? This internship is designed for currently enrolled undergraduates in their second, third, or fourth year of degree-level education, ideally with an interest in Information Systems, AI Technologies, Data Science, Machine Learnings, or related fields. 1/ ML Engineer Intern What you will do: Support the development and evaluation of Machine Learning models using Python and frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and scikit-learn. Work with structured and unstructured data in Databricks and enterprise data platforms, helping prepare datasets and engineer features for ML solutions. Assist in building and maintaining reusable ML pipelines for model training, testing and deployment. Contribute to model experimentation, performance analysis and continuous improvement activities. Learn and apply MLOps practices, including version control, testing, CI/CD and model lifecycle management. Collaborate with Data Scientists and ML Engineers to help transition analytical models into scalable production solutions. Explore machine learning techniques such as forecasting, classification and predictive analytics to address real business challenges. Partner with colleagues across Data & Analytics and business teams to understand business needs and support data-driven decision making. What you will learn: End-to-end Machine Learning lifecycle and MLOps practices. Enterprise-scale AI and analytics platforms, including Databricks. Modern software engineering practices used for ML solution development. How Machine Learning creates value across commercial, supply chain and operational functions. 2/ AI Engineer Intern What you will do: Support the development of Generative AI applications and AI-powered solutions using Large Language Models (LLMs). Assist in building Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions that connect AI models with enterprise knowledge, documents and data sources. Contribute to the development and testing of AI agents and intelligent workflows that automate tasks and improve business processes. Gain hands-on experience with Azure AI Foundry, Databricks and Microsoft AI technologies while working on real business use cases. Help integrate AI capabilities into applications and platforms through APIs and enterprise services. Participate in evaluating AI solutions for quality, performance, cost efficiency and Responsible AI compliance. Support experimentation with emerging AI technologies and the rapid development of proofs of concept (PoCs). Collaborate with AI Engineers, Data Scientists and business stakeholders to identify opportunities where AI can create measurable business value. What you will learn: Generative AI, LLMs, RAG architectures and AI agent development. Enterprise AI engineering practices and modern AI platforms. Responsible AI principles, security and governance requirements. How AI solutions are designed, built and deployed in a large global organization. What You’ll Bring: Fluency in English. Knowledge of one of the following languages is also an advantage: French, Dutch, German, or Spanish. A proactive attitude and strong communication skills. Attention to detail and a passion for delivering high-quality service. Interest in AI or/and Machine Learning. Ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Why Join Us? This is a 9-month program, designated to take place during 2027 (expected between Feb–Nov) and will adapt to the company’s ways of working at that point in time. The program allows flexibility for interns to choose between full-time and part-time schemes. You’ll receive personal mentoring and support, as well as access to multiple networking opportunities. What Happens Next? Due to the high volume of applications, the selection process may take longer than usual. Candidates who meet the requirements will be invited for Excel test and interview with members of our team.
