items.desc: Zensai’s AI Office leads the company’s AI Roadmap, focusing primarily on high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that bring teams together to solve shared business challenges and create value across Zensai. As our Junior Data & AI Solution Developer , you will build the data connections, platforms and solutions that make this possible, working from the first conversation about a problem through to production. The AI Office is led by Maria, our VP of AI Office, and currently consists of five people, with plans to grow to eight. You will work closely with the team across projects and gradually take on greater ownership, with the opportunity to lead AI projects end-to-end, from idea and design through development, implementation and business adoption. Projects could include bringing different data sources into Microsoft Fabric, creating semantic models that give teams consistent figures, or connecting AI agents to reliable information. The work takes business understanding as well as technical skill: asking the right questions, explaining technical choices clearly and making sure what you build works reliably for the people using it. What You’ll Be Doing Design and build data-driven AI solutions, intelligent workflows and automation across business functions Develop data capabilities in Microsoft Fabric, working across OneLake, lakehouses, data pipelines and semantic models Build integrations between business systems, services and data platforms, using APIs and modern integration patterns. Create trusted, reusable data products and foundations that support analytics, AI and other solutions. Build and experiment with AI agents and agentic solutions that use business data, context and tools to support workflows and decision-making. Support solutions after deployment through governance, monitoring, troubleshooting and continuous improvement This is not a traditional data role focused primarily on reporting or maintaining pipelines. It is for someone who enjoys connecting data, platforms and applied AI to build solutions that create real business value and run reliably in production. What You Bring A technical foundation in data engineering, data science, software development or a related field, gained through studies, work or hands-on projects. Practical experience with SQL and Python, including ETL, data pipelines and integration. Familiarity with Git and version control, and an interest in building AI-powered and agentic solutions. An interest in solving business problems, asking good questions and building solutions that work in practice. A curious, learning-oriented mindset, willing to experiment with new technologies and work through unfamiliar problems. Process Apply in just a few minutes, no cover letter required. We review applications weekly and keep you updated throughout the process. Learn more about how we hire at Zensai here! At Zensai, performance, learning, and motivation go hand in hand. In this video, our Chief Human Success Officer, Nina Carøe, shares how we connect human ambition with real business impact The benefits! Full Flexibility : Work where and when you do your best! Morning person or night owl? Home office or office vibes? You decide. Learning: 10% of your working time dedicated to development. Built in, not squeezed in. Pension & Health: We’ve got you covered—literally. Enjoy a robust pension plan that includes life insurance, and coverage if life throws a curveball like loss of work capacity or serious illness. Plus, our health insurance takes care of hospital stays, surgeries, physical therapy—you name it. Peace of mind, sorted. Laptop & Company Phone: Stay connected with a Laptop & iPhone on us. Need a subscription? We’ve got that too. Lunch & Snacks: Feels more like fine dining when we go to lunch, including tasty meals, snacks, and drinks. Your taste buds will thank you! About Zensai Zensai is a global team of around 200 people across Europe, the US, and ANZ. We believe people should have the opportunity to keep learning, feel connected to their workplace, and do their best work. That’s why we created the Human Success Platform. Built into Microsoft 365 and powered by AI, it helps companies turn learning, engagement, and performance into a natural part of everyday work.

items.desc: Lieu du stage : Valbonne (Sophia-Antipolis, 06) Au sein du département Corporate Strategy & Research, vous intégrerez l'équipe Living Twins for Practitioners, riche de compétences en médecine, biologie, mathématique et informatique, et qui conduit plusieurs projets en oncologie, neurologie et cardiologie. Dans le cadre de la diversification de nos activités en santé, vous ferez partie de l’équipe « Clinical Decision » et serez responsable de la mise en place de méthodes basées sur du Deep Learning et des statistiques permettant d’aligner des espaces de variables cliniques tabulaires hétérogènes entre différentes sources de données ; de déployer un modèle prédictif de survenue d’évènements cliniques sur des bases de données de dimensions variables ; et d’évaluer la robustesse et les performances du modèle prédictif face à l’absence ou au changement de variables. Vos missions Le but de ce stage sera de développer une méthodologie d’adaptation de domaine hétérogène (HDA) pour permettre le transfert de modèles prédictifs entre des bases de données cliniques tabulaires ne possédant pas exactement les mêmes variables. L’évolution de la maladie d’un patient peut être vue comme une succession d’évènements cliniques, en particulier dans le domaine de l’oncologie (rechute d’un cancer, décès du patient …). Un de nos objectifs est de développer des modèles permettant de prédire la survenue d’évènements cliniques au cours du temps de suivi du patient, et ce pour les différentes sources de données que nous pouvons avoir. Cependant, le déploiement d’un modèle prédictif sur différentes sources de données se heurte à l’hétérogénéité des données tabulaires : un hôpital peut enregistrer certains marqueurs spécifiques tandis qu’un autre utilisera des marqueurs différents pour une même pathologie, modifiant la dimensionnalité des données et empêchant l’utilisation d’une architecture de Deep Learning fixe. L’utilisation de techniques récentes d’adaptation de domaine, telles que le transport optimal ou des auto-encodeurs asymétriques, permet de projeter ces bases aux variables disjointes dans un espace latent commun afin d’exploiter les données sans altérer la structure du modèle prédictif. L’enjeu de ce stage sera alors de concevoir un pipeline complet capable d’aligner ces distributions tabulaires hétérogènes, puis d’évaluer la capacité du modèle à prédire la survenue d’évènements cliniques sur une nouvelle source de données. Votre contribution consistera à : Effectuer un état de l’art des méthodes d’adaptation de domaine hétérogène et de transport optimal appliquées aux données tabulaires ; Implémenter un algorithme permettant d’aligner ces bases de données cliniques tabulaires ; Comparer la méthodologie développée avec les approches existantes de la littérature ; Effectuer une synthèse des résultats obtenus. Vos Qualifications Actuellement en Master 2 / Bac+5 en Ecole d’ingénieur ou Université, vous recherchez un stage de 6 mois. Compétences techniques souhaitées : Statistiques / Mathématiques appliquées Machine learning / Deep learning Langage python et bonne connaissance d’un framework de Deep Learning (Tensorflow, Pytorch) Anglais courant Une connaissance en biologie et/ou en médecine est un plus. Qualités appréciées pour la bonne démarche de ce stage : Autonomie, Motivé, Esprit critique, Esprit d'initiative, Bon sens de la communication Nous rejoindre c'est aussi Intégrer une entreprise scientifique au cœur de l’innovation technologique, portée par une forte croissance depuis plus de 40 ans. We believe that our people are our number one asset and we want all employees to feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work every day. Within Information Security we blend risk strategy, digital identity, cyber defense, application security and technology solutions as we consider the entire security lifecycle. You will join a team of hardworking, security-focused individuals dedicated to supporting, protecting, and enabling the business through innovative, secure solutions that provide speed to market and business value. The opportunity The Technology Assurance, Risk, and Policy (TARP) function within Information Security strives to create and promote a holistic Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) program by creating a robust, resilient, and proactive governance framework, supported by a strategic risk management approach and stringent compliance structures. It aims to integrate and align its GRC initiatives in line with the global firm’s objectives and emerging threats within the cybersecurity landscape. Furthermore, the Policy, Risk, and Controls (PRC) Enablement & Awareness team aims to manage the human element of risk through Human Risk Management, which involves security awareness, training, culture, and behavior management. Your Key Responsibilities The Global Behavioral Analytics & AI Specialist sits within the Human Risk Management function and leverages artificial intelligence, data science, and behavioral science to measure, model, and manage human risk across EY. This role is the analytical and AI engine behind the security culture program—turning behavioral signals, engagement data, and risk indicators into insight that helps the organization understand why people behave the way they do and how to manage those behaviors at scale. Reporting to the Global Security Culture and Engagement Lead, this individual will partner across the awareness, learning, training, and simulation teams to build the metrics, models, and AI-enabled capabilities that quantify culture and behavior change. Beyond measurement, they will act as an AI-forward thought partner for the entire Human Risk Management team—identifying practical, responsible ways to apply AI both for intelligence and for service delivery. A successful applicant is analytical, curious, and technically fluent, combining rigor in data and AI with a genuine understanding of human behavior. They are comfortable operating in ambiguity, shaping a brand-new capability, and translating complex analysis into clear, actionable stories for non-technical audiences. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English are essential. Key responsibilities include: Maintain and optimize a human risk measurement framework, defining the metrics and indicators that quantify security behaviors, culture, engagement, and human risk across the organization. Leverage AI to analyze behavioral data, identify patterns and human risk indicators, and model or predict where risky behaviors are most likely to occur. Work with stakeholders to consolidate data from across the Human Risk Management program into reporting that tells a clear, connected story. Serve as the AI-forward thought partner for the Human Risk Management team, identifying responsible and practical ways to apply AI for both intelligence (measurement, prediction, insight) and service offerings (e.g., AI-powered solutions that reinforce secure behaviors). Partner with the Security Culture and Engagement Lead to translate behavioral insight into targeted interventions, campaigns, and reinforcement strategies. Develop executive-ready reporting, visualizations, and recommendations that communicate human risk trends, program effectiveness, and return on investment to senior stakeholders. Design and analyze surveys, assessments, experiments, and A/B tests to evaluate the impact of behavior change initiatives and continuously improve them. Ensure that data and AI are used responsibly, ethically, and in line with EY privacy, data protection, security, and governance requirements. Stay informed on developments in behavioral science, data science, AI, and human risk measurement, bringing new methods and innovation into the program. Skills And Attributes For Success Strong analytical and data science skills, with the ability to work with behavioral, engagement, and risk data to generate meaningful insight. Hands-on familiarity with AI and machine learning concepts and tools, and a track record of applying them to solve practical problems. Understanding of behavioral science, psychology, or human risk principles and how they translate into measurable behaviors. Ability to translate complex data and AI analysis into clear, compelling narratives for non-technical and executive audiences. Strong data visualization and storytelling skills. Curiosity, creativity, and a bias toward experimentation and continuous improvement. Ability to collaborate across functions, …

items.desc: Job ID : 7052 Do you want to build AI solutions that create real business impact? Join Nordea Pension's new Centre of Excellence for “NewTech & Optimisation” and help accelerate AI adoption across customer journeys, operations and business processes. As an AI Developer, you will build AI solutions for prioritised use cases as part of a fixed, dedicated team. You will work with modern AI technologies, reuse Nordea Group platforms where relevant and ensure solutions operate within established AI governance, architecture and data frameworks. You will help convert strategic priorities into scalable AI solutions, starting with high-impact use cases across customer onboarding, customer screening, and core pension administration processes. About Our Team Welcome to Technology in Nordea Pension Denmark, where we build solutions for customers and colleagues that help deliver on Nordea's strategic ambitions. Nordea Pension is one of Denmark's leading pension providers and is currently undergoing an ambitious transformation. To accelerate our ambitions, we are establishing a new Centre of Excellence for "NewTech & Optimisation", focused on AI, automation, operational excellence, and digital innovation. The "NewTech & Optimisation" Centre of Excellence is a dedicated team within Business Technology focused on driving AI adoption, process optimisation, automation and digital innovation across Nordea Pension Denmark. Our mission is to create measurable business value by accelerating AI adoption, improving customer journeys, increasing operational efficiency, and enabling new ways of working. Collaboration. Ownership. Passion. Courage. These are the values that guide us in how we work and how we make decisions – and that we imagine you share with us. Main responsibilities in this role: This is a unique opportunity to design, build and scale AI-powered solutions across Nordea Pension, helping transform innovative ideas into production-ready capabilities that create measurable business value. This role is focused on: Designing, developing and deploying AI-enabled solutions. Building agentic and LLM-based applications. Integrating AI solutions with business processes and digital services. Reusing and leveraging Nordea Group AI capabilities and platforms. Ensuring solutions comply with AI governance and architecture principles. Collaborating closely with business stakeholders and technology teams. Monitoring solution performance and driving continuous improvements. Who You Are This role requires strong AI engineering skills combined with curiosity, innovation and the ability to translate business challenges into scalable technical solutions. Your background and skills include: AI/ML engineering experience. Experience with Generative AI, AI agents and large language models (LLM). Software engineering and cloud development experience. Knowledge of APIs, integrations, and modern development practices. Ability to work across business and technology domains. It would be ideal if you also have: Experience deploying AI solutions into production environments. Experience with Azure AI Services, cloud-native architectures or similar platforms. Experience integrating AI solutions into existing applications and business processes. Experience working with governance, security and compliance requirements. Experience from financial services, pensions, insurance or another regulated industry. What We Offer Significant influence on how AI solutions are designed, developed and scaled across Nordea Pension. The opportunity to help build a new Centre of Excellence from the ground up. Exposure strategic AI, automation and transformation initiatives. Close collaboration with stakeholders across business and technology. A flexible, collaborative, and learning-oriented work environment. People come here when they want to get somewhere. For some, it’s to take their career to the next level. For others, it’s to break new ground within their area of expertise – in other words, with us, you will always move forward. A culture that fosters performance and growth in one of the largest Nordic banks, offering various opportunities to evolve, develop and learn from brilliant colleagues with diverse backgrounds in a vibrant working environment. Hybrid working model – we believe in the value of bringing people together and at the same time we embrace the freedom of flexibility. Diversity and inclusion are a natural part of our daily work. We know that an inclusive workplace is a sustainable one. We genuinely believe that our diverse backgrounds, experiences, characteristics and traits make us stronger together. Every day we strive to find new ways to improve diversity and inclusion within our community e.g. we have signed the European Diversity Charters in the countries where we operate to show our commitment and engage with others to continue learning and improving. If this sounds like you, get in touch! Next steps Submit your application no later than …

items.desc: We are looking for an Software Engineer (AI Development Experience) – SDLC (m/f/d) to support our organization in automating our Software Development Life Cycle through AI Orchestration across all interfaces. You will work at the intersection of technology, business departments, and organizational transformation. Your work will have a direct impact on how AI is used in practice across the company, how processes are made more efficient, and how we further develop and transform our Software Development Life Cycle. Your Job Analyze and optimize the SDLC and CI/CD pipelines across all areas of software development (Platform, Security, Backup, Compliance). Identify and prioritize suitable AI and automation use cases with a focus on agentic workflows, model routing, and memory and context architectures towards Level 5 AI. Design, develop, and implement AI-based workflow solutions. Integrate automations into existing systems and processes. Support all teams in the AI transformation of software development. Deliver training sessions, workshops, and onboarding sessions. Create internal documentation, playbooks, tutorials, and best practices. Advise technical teams on the use of AI. Contribute to AI governance, data protection, compliance, and the responsible use of AI. Measure the impact, adoption, and ROI of implemented automations. Continuously improve existing solutions based on feedback and metrics. Your Profile Experience in analyzing and automating software development processes. Hands-on experience with AI tools, APIs, enterprise tools, and scripting. Good knowledge of Python or a comparable scripting language. Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences. Experience delivering training sessions, workshops, or enablement programs. Strong communication and consulting skills. A pragmatic, solution-oriented, and business-oriented way of working. Awareness of data protection, security, compliance, and AI governance. Fluency in German and English, both written and spoken Your Benefits Temporary Employee Exchange Program – we support you in working from our global office locations while exploring the world (e.g., Malta, Madrid, Montréal, Washington, D.C.). Work-from-home option and flexible working hours. Team events like laser tag, an escape room, or a get-together at our own legendary beer truck in Hanover – let yourself be surprised! Be-Active Bonus – we subsidize your gym memberships. Whether by car, public transport, or bike – we make your commute easier with free parking (Hannover), a discounted Jobticket, or bike leasing. Employer contribution to the company pension plan. Referral Bonus: €1,500 for every successful candidate referral. And of course, the usual standards like 30 days of vacation, permanent contracts, development opportunities, coffee, tea, soft drinks & fresh fruit, office dogs, no dress code, and much more!

items.desc: Who are we: KBC Global Services is the engine behind KBC Group – a leading bank-insurance group with over 41,000 talented employees serving more than 12 million clients across Europe. Since 2021, we have been supporting the digital transformation of KBC Group providing software development, QA, AI and other IT solutions working on a wide range of projects combining classical IT with digital banking. We are investing heavily in Artificial Intelligence to help our employees work smarter, faster, and more efficiently and create an optimized claim handling-experience for our customer. Within the Claims Insurance ART, we explore, develop, and implement AI Agents that support employees in handling claims, analyzing complex files, and executing operational processes. These AI Agents combine information from multiple sources, including modern applications, documentation, and our mainframe environment, to provide contextual support throughout employees' daily activities. We work according to the principles of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) , where business value is at the center of everything we do, and multidisciplinary teams collaborate to deliver innovative solutions for our customers and employees. To further strengthen this ambition, we are looking for an AI Agent Engineer who can bridge the gap between business, AI technology, and our existing application landscape. What does this role involve? As an AI Agent Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and implementing AI Agents that support employees within Claims Insurance in their daily activities. You understand both the technical capabilities of AI and the business processes within claims management, and you know how to connect these worlds effectively. You will work closely with business experts, architects, developers, and operational teams to create AI solutions that deliver tangible value to our employees. You will work on cutting-edge AI initiatives, including the development of AI agents, integration with our mainframe and deployment of scalable data-driven solutions. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a collaborative environment and is passionate about AI innovation. As our AI Agent Engineer , you would have the following responsibilities: AI Agent Development: Design, build, and optimize AI Agents using modern AI technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs), Agentic AI, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Business & Claims Understanding: Develop a solid understanding of Claims Insurance processes and translate operational challenges into practical AI solutions that support employees. System Integration: Work with large-scale big data pipelines and real-time data processing. Integrate with AWS Bedrock and other LLM-based platforms to build intelligent agents. Develop and maintain infrastructure using Terraform and AWS services. Deployment & Operations: Build solutions that can be deployed through KBC’s Execution Garden platform, taking into account scalability, monitoring, security, and maintainability. Responsible AI: Contribute to security, compliance, privacy, and the proper application of AI governance within KBC. Collaboration: Work closely with business stakeholders, architects, platform teams, and fellow engineers to successfully bring innovative AI solutions into production. Key competences that will help you succeed: Proven experience with AWS cloud services (e.g., Lambda, S3, Bedrock). Experience developing software solutions in Python. Strong knowledge of Terraform and infrastructure-as-code practices. Experience with AI solutions, Machine Learning, or Generative AI. Experience integrating APIs and connecting data across various systems. An interest in or experience with claims management and insurance processes. Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate complex business challenges into practical AI-driven solutions. Excellent communication skills in English. A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for working in multidisciplinary agile teams. Nice to have: Knowledge of AI Agent frameworks. Knowledge of mainframe environments (COBOL, DB2, CICS, MQ, etc.) is a strong asset. What do we offer? A unique opportunity to help shape the AI strategy of KBC Insurance. The chance to build AI Agents that are used daily by hundreds of employees within Claims Insurance. An innovative environment where business, data, and technology come together. Collaboration with experts in insurance, AI, data, and software engineering. A challenging role with plenty of room for initiative, innovation, and personal growth. The opportunity to work with the latest AI technologies and enterprise AI platforms. Being part of KBC, you will enjoy plenty of benefits: Work-Life balance: 25-day annual paid holiday; regular team buildings and company parties; Personal Care: Additional medical insurance and pension plan; Fully covered Multisport card; Food Vouchers : Digital food vouchers, which you can use in hypermarkets …

With an Atlassian focus, develop platforms and workflows using Forge, Rovo and CI/CD so
items.desc: You love building something people can actually use: the moment an integration works, an agent takes a tedious task off someone’s hands, or an idea becomes a useful tool. At XALT, you work closely with the people you build for, taking their solution from the first conversation into production. Your customers will be enterprises and public-sector organisations. Your focus will be AI agents with XALT Northstar or development platforms in the Atlassian ecosystem. We will work out together which area fits your experience and interests; working across both is possible. What you learn in customer projects will feed back into our own products. What we are working towards We want to help companies use AI to improve the work people rely on every day. We combine consulting, software development and our own products to make that happen. What excites us is seeing a technical idea become something people can count on. What you will do Turn business problems into practical technical solutions together with the customer. Write production code and integrate agents into existing systems and workflows. With a Northstar focus, build and operate personal and operational agents using MCP servers, Agent Skills, evals, guardrails and observability. With an Atlassian focus, develop platforms and workflows using Forge, Rovo and CI/CD so development teams can use agents reliably. Take solutions into production, evaluate their quality and improve them based on actual use. Bring insights from customer projects into our products. What you bring Experience writing and reviewing production code, for example in TypeScript or Python, across both backend and frontend Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers and CI/CD, for example AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform or GitLab Practical experience with LLMs and agentic systems, including evals that detect errors and regressions At least one agent or AI workflow you have built yourself and put into production , which you can demonstrate live during the application process (see “Your AI example”) Enjoyment of working directly with customers and the ability to make reasoned technical decisions with incomplete information Business-fluent German and English What we offer Unlimited tokens for Claude, OpenAI and the latest, most advanced AI tools €70,000–100,000 gross per year , depending on experience; we are open to going beyond this range for exceptional senior candidates with a proven record of running agents in production The opportunity to follow your solutions from the first conversation into customers’ daily work and see the difference they make Professional exchange within the team, across the Atlassian ecosystem as a Platinum Partner, and through the XALT AI Circle and IT Revolution Your working arrangements We value working together in the office: developing ideas, learning from one another and talking things through in person. Living in or around Munich or Leipzig is therefore a plus. Remote work is also possible. If you live further away, we would still love to hear from you. Together, we will discuss an arrangement that works for you, your team and the role. Full-time Work within an international company with teams in Munich, Leipzig, Manila and New York Our professional community Exchanging ideas with others is part of what we enjoy about this work. For our XALT AI Circle in Munich in autumn 2026, we have invited Peter Steinberger of the OpenClaw Foundation to discuss personal agents. In October 2026, Philipp Göllner spoke at the Enterprise AI Summit in Charlotte about how our team built a Chief of Staff agent. We plan to represent XALT again at the summit in Portland in May 2027. For a closer look at our work, see Philipp’s talk from Charlotte. Your AI example We would like to understand how you approach problems and what you have learned along the way. Bring a process you have automated yourself with AI and show it to us live. Walk us through your contribution, whether the workflow works consistently, and what has measurably improved. We are also interested in its limitations and how you check the results. One example is enough; you can recreate it with test data. Please do not share confidential information or protected code. Your application Does this sound like work you would enjoy? We would love to hear from you. Send your CV to careers@xalt.de and tell us what you would like to work on. The conversation should also give you room to ask about the team, your responsibilities and what you need to do good work. We will discuss the interview arrangements and your AI demonstration with you personally. You can also send any questions beforehand to careers@xalt.de.

items.desc: We want to make investing easier, more accessible and help people feel good about investing. Technology is central to making that happen, and Generative AI is becoming an increasingly important part of how we innovate at AJ Bell. We’re looking for a Software Engineer (GenAI) to join our growing GenAI Engineering team, building AI-powered solutions that solve genuine business problems and deliver value for our customers and colleagues. You’ll have the freedom to experiment with emerging technology, develop your expertise and help influence how we adopt GenAI across the business. You’ll work within a collaborative, cross-functional engineering team, with the opportunity to contribute across our technology stack and propositions. What We're Looking For We’re looking for a motivated and curious Software Engineer with strong Python development skills and a genuine interest in Generative AI and large language models. You’ll help us design, build and deliver production-grade GenAI solutions across the business, working with modern LLMs, AI platforms and emerging agentic technologies. We’re looking for someone who is curious about AI and LLMs, keeps up with how the technology is evolving, and enjoys experimenting and learning. You’ll be excited by what GenAI can make possible, while applying sound engineering judgement and focusing on building solutions that are simple, robust and deliver real value. Key Technical Skills Strong knowledge and experience of Python, its libraries and tooling Experience working with industry-leading large language models, particularly OpenAI and Anthropic Solid understanding of RESTful API design and implementation Experience with Git-based source control and modern software engineering practices Experience in AI-assisted development, using tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code It would be great if you also have Experience building and operating solutions in the cloud, preferably AWS Practical knowledge of GenAI architecture and engineering patterns Familiarity with GenAI platforms and tooling such as Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore and LiteLLM Experience with CI/CD and containerisation Experience taking GenAI applications from proof of concept through to production What You'll Bring Curiosity about LLMs, GenAI and emerging AI technologies, with a willingness to experiment, learn and develop your knowledge Strong technical problem-solving skills The ability to work effectively with engineers and business stakeholders A pragmatic engineering mindset, balancing innovation with business value A collaborative, proactive and adaptable approach to working in an evolving technology environment About AJ Bell At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good. That means creating an experience where customers feel confident, secure and supported; whether they’re investing for the first time, saving for retirement or managing their investments with the help of a financial adviser. Technology plays a huge part in making that possible. We’re one of the UK’s fastest-growing investment platform businesses, trusted by everyone from professional financial advisers to first-time investors. Today, more than 762,000 customers trust us to manage more than £121.5 billion of assets. That trust is something we take seriously. Our technology needs to work hard behind the scenes to make investing feel simple, reliable and secure. From the platforms our customers interact with to the critical systems and processes that support our business, we're continually looking for better ways to use technology to deliver a great experience. As a Software Engineer(GenAI) at AJ Bell, you’ll have the opportunity to help build the technology that drives our success. We're proud to be recognised as one of the UK's Best 100 Companies to Work For for six consecutive years, and a Great Place to Work® for the past two years, a reflection of our supportive and collaborative culture. What We Offer 25 days holiday, increasing with service, plus buy/sell scheme and bank holidays 6% pension with matched contributions Discretionary bonus scheme Share schemes, including free shares and BAYE Health Cash Plan and discounted private healthcare Free onsite gym Enhanced family leave, subject to qualifying criteria Travel and bike loan schemes Employee Assistance Programme Life at AJ Bell Regular social events including summer and Christmas parties Learning and development opportunities tailored to you Casual dress code Friendly, supportive team environment Our ways of working At AJ Bell, our people are the heart of our culture. We believe in building strong connections by working together. That's why we offer a hybrid working model, where you'll spend a minimum of 50% of working time per month in the office. For new team members, an initial period will be spent full-time in the office to help you immerse yourself in our business and build valuable relationships with your colleagues. Inclusion & diversity We’re committed to creating …

items.card: The role: Join us as a Product Engineer to build a new product within Brevo called Brevo OS. Brevo OS is a startup inside Brevo: a team of six, a product we started from an empty repository earlier this year, and the feel of a small company within the big one. The product works, the first customer deployments are beginning, and a great deal is still undecided — so the people who join us now will shape what it
items.desc: At Brevo, we’re not just building a CRM. With our technology, we’re helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. From emails and SMS to WhatsApp, Chat, and Marketing Automation, our tools are intuitive, powerful, and built to scale with every ambition. We give businesses a clear view of the customer journey, so they can focus on what matters: connection. As a certified B Corp , we’re proud to grow with purpose, committed to high standards of social and environmental impact, not just performance. Today, more than 500,000 businesses across 180 countries —from NGOs like Amnesty International to global brands like Carrefour, eBay, Louis Vuitton, and Michelin—trust Brevo to engage their audiences, cut through complexity, and deliver results. Our reliable technology and 75+ integrations help them create unparalleled customer experiences, without the usual tech headaches. We recently exceeded 200m ARR and reached a major milestone by becoming a Unicorn , backed by strong growth and global expansion - and we’re just getting started! The role: Join us as a Product Engineer to build a new product within Brevo called Brevo OS. Brevo OS is a startup inside Brevo: a team of six, a product we started from an empty repository earlier this year, and the feel of a small company within the big one. The product works, the first customer deployments are beginning, and a great deal is still undecided — so the people who join us now will shape what it becomes. It's an AI-native operating system for small businesses: a system of agents that helps a solopreneur, a hair salon or a building contractor run their whole business — clients, contracts and signature, invoicing, their website, their inbox. Modules get added the way an ERP grows, except the whole thing is built around agents from the ground up. Your Impact at Brevo: Turn a very high level business need into something real : understand the function, define the users, the smallest useful version, the entities and their lifecycles, the permissions and constraints that matter, and what to build versus integrate Decide which of our platform primitives to extend rather than reinvent, then build it, ship it, watch it in production, and improve it Work across product management, frontend, backend, data modelling, infrastructure, and AI. Everyone arrived with a specialism and nobody is confined to theirs; product thinking and business analysis is part of everyone’s job Build almost entirely through coding agents: Claude Code is the workflow, not a pilot running alongside it, for implementation, codebase exploration, documentation, debugging, and operations Decompose problems into work an agent can actually execute, give it context without over-constraining it, and tell the difference between correct and merely plausible Verify with tests and instrumentation, not vibes, and keep a large generated codebase coherent Work day to day in TypeScript, Kubernetes, and agentic frameworks Who you are: Around 2-5 years of professional engineering experience. We care more about your slope than your years Real depth in something, and no attachment to staying there. Bring what you're genuinely strong at — the team compounds those — and expect to spend a good part of your time well outside it Coding agents already central to how you work. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, something equivalent. Not "I've generated the Unit Tests" — real delegation of substantial work, and real review of what comes back. Scepticism about generated output is a feature of this job, not a problem Evidence you've owned a problem, not just implemented a ticket — something you helped define, drove, shipped and then lived with in production. Product questions are your questions too At your best when the brief is one sentence and the plan is still moving. We're learning what this product is, so priorities change often. The mission doesn't English. We're an international team working across France and India, and English is our working language. French is not required If you don't meet all the requirements above but believe this opportunity matches your expectations and experience, we still encourage you to apply! Why people love working at Brevo: A place to grow, together: Join an international team in a bright, collaborative office located in a vibrant neighbourhood Practical perks for everyday balance: RTT days off, 50% public transport reimbursement, Sustainable Mobility Package (whether you ride a classic bike or go electric, we support your choice to commute greener) and daily Swile meal vouchers (€12.50/day) Learning, every step of the way: Access to English classes and 155,000+ courses on Udemy, plus a strong internal culture of knowledge-sharing and support Flexible for life: A remote-friendly setup, budget to support your home workspace, and relocation assistance for international talents Wellbeing that works: Top-notch private healthcare (70% covered), 6-week second-parent leave, …

items.title: AI Growth Ops
items.card: You will work most closely with the engineers building the platform, the product team defining how operators use it, and the operators who rely on it every day. QA and operations is how the whole team knows the platform can be trusted. The opportunity You will own day-to-day operations and QA for our internal growth platform. You test it, catch problems before our customers do, keep approvals and exception queues
items.desc: Building the Future of Open Finance Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. The team Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Growth at Kraken is being rebuilt around an AI-native platform. Instead of people manually building audiences, writing copy, adjusting budgets, and scheduling sends, agents find opportunities, make decisions, and execute across paid, organic, and lifecycle channels. They learn from every result and keep going. People still run the system. Operators use a central hub to set the rules the agents follow, review and approve what they produce, and handle exceptions when something doesn’t fit. The platform also has to work across many markets and languages, and it operates in a regulated industry, so there are compliance checks and approval steps built in. The team is a small, cross-functional group of growth, product, and engineering people who build this platform and run it day to day. We ship often, learn fast, and raise the quality bar with every release. You will work most closely with the engineers building the platform, the product team defining how operators use it, and the operators who rely on it every day. QA and operations is how the whole team knows the platform can be trusted. The opportunity You will own day-to-day operations and QA for our internal growth platform. You test it, catch problems before our customers do, keep approvals and exception queues moving, and report on how it’s performing. You will work closely with product, engineering and operators to make sure the platform works and keeps working. This is a hands-on, detail-focused role. You will spend your days in the product, testing what’s new, checking what should already work, and writing up what you find so it gets fixed. Test the platform regularly. Cover new releases, rule changes, and edge cases, and run regression checks to make sure existing features still work. Find bugs and document them clearly, with steps to reproduce, severity, and impact. Follow them through until engineering fixes them and you’ve verified the fix. Monitor platform performance and agent activity, flag anything that looks wrong, and escalate it to the right person. Work the approval queues daily. Keep items moving and make sure nothing is left unreviewed. Check agent output against defined checklists and standards, and escalate anything unclear or risky.Note where flows are confusing or inconsistent, and flag them to the team. Write and maintain documentation: test plans, QA checklists, runbooks, and release notes. What You Bring Experience in QA, testing, operations, support, or analytics, ideally on a software product or complex system Exceptional attention to detail. You notice what others miss and double-check your work. A structured approach to testing. You can create and follow a test plan, and think about what could break. Clear written communication. Your bug reports and documentation should be easy for anyone to follow. Comfort with data. You can read a dashboard and tell when a number looks off. Fast learner. You pick up new tools and systems quickly and ask thoughtful questions. AI-native habits. You use AI tools in your own work every day, and you’re curious about where they get things wrong. Prompt engineering curiosity, you don't need to be an engineer, but you are willing to learn how to communicate with AI systems precisely and improve their outputs Reliability. You keep to a routine, keep your queues clear, and tell people early when something is stuck. Nice to haves Experience testing software products or AI and LLM-based tools Familiarity with Jira, Mixpanel, or similar tools Exposure to marketing, CRM, or lifecycle messaging workflows Interest in fintech or crypto Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. Our commitment Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right …

 ELSP, (Electrification Smart Power) division d’ABB développe et commercialise des solutions innovantes pour la protection et la commande de l’énergie électrique. L’usine de Chassieu est un centre de compétences reconnu, spécialisé dans la conception et la production de contacteurs.
 Présent sur des marchés industriels variés, le site propose des solutions essentielles à la performance et à la fiabilité des installations électriques. Il regroupe des expertises complémentaires, de la R&D à la production, en passant par les fonctions support.
 En s’appuyant sur une forte ouverture à l’international, avec plus de 95 % de sa production destinée à l’export, le site évolue dans un environnement dynamique, tourné vers l’innovation et la collaboration avec de nombreux pays.
 Rejoindre Electrification Smart Power à Chassieu, acteur industriel innovant et tourné vers l’international, c’est contribuer au développement de solutions technologiques au service de la performance industrielle et de la transition énergétique.
 Dans le cadre du renforcement de notre équipe R&D basée à Chassieu, nous recherchons un Ingénieur R&D Firmware pour contribuer au développement de notre nouvelle génération de contacteurs industriels.
 À ce poste, vous participerez à la conception et au développement de logiciels embarqués assurant le pilotage intelligent des bobines d'actionnement de nos produits. Votre objectif sera de garantir des performances optimales, une grande fiabilité et une consommation énergétique maîtrisée. Vous évoluerez dans un environnement international et collaboratif, tout en bénéficiant d'une réelle autonomie dans la conduite de vos projets.
 Vos responsabilités 
 Concevoir, développer et maintenir les logiciels embarqués destinés aux systèmes de commande de contacteurs industriels.
 Définir et implémenter des algorithmes de contrôle pour la gestion des bobines d'actionnement, en veillant aux performances, à la fiabilité et à l'efficacité énergétique.
 Réaliser les tests unitaires, d'intégration et système afin de garantir la qualité et la robustesse des développements.
 Collaborer avec les équipes pluridisciplinaires pour intégrer les solutions firmware aux nouveaux produits.
 Documenter les développements, partager les résultats techniques et contribuer aux activités de propriété intellectuelle, notamment aux dépôts de brevets.
 Assurer une veille technologique active afin d'identifier les innovations susceptibles de soutenir les futurs projets R&D et les orientations stratégiques du groupe.
 Participer à des réseaux techniques internes et externes afin de développer et enrichir son expertise.
 Piloter les activités de développement firmware, notamment en matière de planification, gestion des risques et coordination avec les fournisseurs et les équipes transverses.

 Ce stage, d'une durée de 4 à 6 mois, débutera idéalement en début d'année 2027 (cette période est indicative et pourra être ajustée).
 Vos principales missions consisteront à : 
 - Comprendre les besoins de nos clients ainsi que la nature des menaces internes.
 - Réaliser une veille technologique sur les solutions existantes de détection de menaces internes.
 - Proposer et développer des solutions basées sur le Machine Learning pour modéliser les comportements des utilisateurs afin d'identifier leurs comportements anormaux (indicateurs d'une menace potentielle).
 - Déployer les solutions proposées sur une plateforme dédiée et évaluer rigoureusement leurs performances.
 - Analyser les données et collaborer avec les équipes IT et Data pour intégrer des données structurées et non structurées depuis diverses sources.
 - Garantir le développement de solutions responsables et en accord avec les principes d'IA éthique d'Airbus.

 - Compréhension des enjeux techniques du monde passionnant de la cybersécurité.

 Compétences techniques :
 - Solides connaissances en statistiques, Data Science et Python,
 - Expérience dans le développement d'algorithmes de Machine Learning,
 - Des connaissances en Cybersécurité seront un véritable atout.
 Soft skills :

 - Autonomie et proactivité,
 - Excellente capacité à travailler en équipe et à partager ses connaissances avec la communauté.

 - Anglais : Niveau avancé

This model will be the core building block and the starting point initiated during the conceptual phase of any future air platform and shall be used during the whole development phase (typically a V&V cycle). This model will be part of a more general Digital Twin model.
 Task and activities to be carried out

 Develop of a generic digital model for an air vehicle (manned and unmanned). This air vehicle shall model shall start with the definition of Use Cases at level L-1 (collaborative air vehicle functions with legacy platforms) and L0 (System of System collaborative functions with other air vehicles covered by the generic air vehicle).
 This generic digital model shall be based in the appliance of Model Based System Engineering for developing a SysML v2model of the Functional, Logical and Technical architectures at Level1 (air vehicle), L2 (major systems) and L3 (sub-systems), including structural and behavioural diagrams.
 Adoption of MOFLT (Mission, Operational, Functional, Logical and Technical architectures) Airbus’ profile and development of other specific profiles that could be required.
 Validation of the model according to general SysMLv2 rules profile specific.
 Definition of the main L1 functional tests required for supporting a certification process.
 Simulation running of the whole model (from L0 – System of Systems level up to L3 – equipment level -) to support decision-making for the trade-off revealed during the tailoring of the generic model for a particular air vehicle
 Integration of the model in a more general Digital Twin model.
 Knowledge to be acquired by the student

 Structuring workflows and implementing modelling methodologies within a newly established, high-tech engineering environment.
 Developing a deep understanding of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) principles and their practical application in harmonizing complex design lifecycles and technical architectures to be part of an air vehicle.

 We are looking for recent graduates from different disciplines interested in developing their professional career in the aeronautical sector. The current context demands different ways of looking, thinking and relating.
 The selection process will be during October 2026 until February 2027. 
 What does this internship consists in? 
 Together with Camilo José Cela University, Airbus has developed an exclusive program (Discover) designed for those interested in the best training in new areas of knowledge essential to be able to develop as professionals of the future.
 You will have the opportunity to study a Master, organized in three training blocks, that will allow you to Discover the skills most in demand today. It will be combined with an 11 month internship at Airbus in an area related to your degree, where you can learn and complete your academic background.
 The start of the internship will be in early March 2027, and will last 11 months (August disabled for all purposes). It is a full-time experience (40h/week), in which you will receive an attractive study grant.
 Internship Job Description: 
 The student will carry out this internship within the stress method and design value team (1ACAAS) at Airbus, which develops sizing methods applicable to the whole Airbus aircraft family. The student will be located in Getafe but will be integrated into a fully transnational team.
 The project will be based on advanced composite unfolding analysis for composite structures. Composite angles are increasingly substituting metallic angles in structural part design, with CFRP L-angles found at numerous locations within modern aircraft structures. The primary reason is structural simplicity, as angles can be integral to the structural part, reducing the elements in the joint, which directly translates to reduced weight and the avoidance of corrosion issues. However, the complex physical behavior of these angles, particularly under delamination and in-plane stresses, must be understood in detail. 
 Project :
 The intention of this project is to deep-dive into the stress states governing induced unfolding failure mechanisms. Taking analytical models (Lekhnitskii, Ko-Jackson) as the basis, the student will aim to build a robust prediction model considering several phenomena identified in recent studies.
 During the project, the student will:
 Analyze the experimental data to capture in-plane failures.
 Study analytical crack stress models and develop FEM to support analytical formulations.
 Explore free edge effect and incorporate this phenomenon into the stress field calculations and prediction models.
 Investigate thermal curing stresses and how they can be modelled to measure their effect on the stress field and failure envelope.
 Progress towards building a prediction model that, under general loading conditions, can determine the structural Reserve Factors.
 Required skills #AirbusDiversity 
 As a successful candidate, you will be able to demonstrate the following skills and experience:
 Educated to degree level (or equivalent) in Aerospace Engineering
 Ability to work in complex and international environments.
 Structural stress analysis, particularly in Composite materials. Structural stress methods
 Analytical and problem-solving skills
 Programming languages (C+/Fortran/Python)
 Final Element modelling techniques (Abaqus, Nastran, Hypermesh)
 Language Skills: Negotiation level of English, Spanish

We're seeking a skilled Navigation Signal Experimentation Engineer to join our Airbus Navigation Team at the Ottobrunn premises in Taufkirchen, Germany.
 As part of our expert team, you'll contribute directly to the design, implementation, verification and experimentation of next-generation navigation signal concepts and services. This isn't just a job; it's a chance to work alongside the best in the field, with over 25 years of experience in developing Europe’s satellite navigation systems, EGNOS and Galileo.
 Your location: 
 Our site is just a stone's throw away from Munich, the beautiful capital of Bavaria. You are into sports and other outdoor activities? The Alps and Lake Starnberg are within an hour’s reach, offering a multitude of recreational options.
 Our Benefits for You

 Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.

Your Mission, Should You Choose to Accept It: 
 You'll be a vital contributor to the navigation signal team, ensuring the flawless performance of the navigation signal-in-space through experimentations. Your core responsibilities will include:
 Prototyping: Define architecture of prototype testbeds for next-generation navigation signals.
 Development: Design, develop and implement novel signal processing algorithms or modules for various navigation signal modulations (e.g. CDMA and OFDM).
 Assembly, Integration and Test: Integrate and test hardware and software components for real-time signal experimentation, and functional verifications.
 Experimentation: Plan, develop (test cases and test procedures) and execute experimentation test campaigns.

 Problem-Solving: Investigate and resolve non-conformances occurring throughout the signal generation, transmission and reception chain.
 Who We're Looking For:

 A Master's degree in Navigation, Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related field.
 A minimum of 2 years of professional experience in innovative projects, preferably with Galileo or other Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), LEO-PNT and 5G positioning.
 Solid expertise in real-time navigation signal processing implementation and experimentation, including digital signal processing (CDMA and OFDM signals), modulation, navigation receiver algorithms, 5G positioning protocol stack, software-defined radio (SDR), real-time data processing modules, and over-the-air signal transmission and reception.

 Excellent communication skills in English and the flexibility to work effectively within an international team.

We support the A400M Military Test and Support Facility (MTSF) by providing simulation models that enable the verification and certification of avionics at software, equipment, and system levels. Job Description: 
 An opportunity for a Microwave Instrument Systems Engineer has arisen within Airbus Defence and Space, Getafe (Madrid).
 The selected candidate will join the Microwave Instrument Future Projects and Proposals Team . This department is in charge of the definition, engineering, and proposal preparation of active and passive microwave instruments—such as passive microwave radiometers, synthetic aperture radars (SAR), scatterometers, and reflectometry—for future Earth Observation space missions.
 Working within a multidisciplinary and transnational engineering environment, the jobholder will reinforce our Systems Engineering capabilities, taking part in current running studies and leading technical trade-offs to shape the next generation of space remote sensing systems.
 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The main tasks of the jobholder will be:
 System Definition & Requirements: Analyze mission requirements and translate them into end-to-end system and sub-system architectures, ensuring overall system coherence, establishing system budgets, and conducting key concept trade-offs.
 Technical Team Leadership: Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams (mechanical, thermal, RF, etc.) throughout the study phases, providing expert support on microwave payload aspects.
 Performance & Data Processing: Assess end-to-end instrument performance and define on-board and on-ground data processing needs in coordination with ground processing development activities.
 Verification, Validation & Industrialization: Define and implement on-ground and in-orbit verification and validation (V&V) approaches, and manage industrial contracts for sub-system level equipment.
 Proposals & Roadmaps: Contribute to the elaboration of proposals for future Earth Observation missions (including development concepts and industrialization) and support Airbus technology roadmaps.
 Customer Interface: Act as a technical point of contact with Airbus customers (such as ESA) and actively participate in project review meetings.
 SKILLS 
 Is your profile aligned to the following list of skills? Apply! We are looking forward to know you:
 Education: Degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Physics, or a related discipline.
 Experience: At least 3 years of experience in remote sensing microwave instruments development and space systems engineering.
 Soft skills: High adaptability to work autonomously or in small, multidisciplinary, and transnational teams; strong ability to manage workloads across multiple projects and availability for frequent business travel.
 Languages: Negotiation level in English (written and spoken).
 Technical knowledge: Strong knowledge of space systems engineering, ESA program phases and development cycles, and verification/validation campaigns.
 Valuable / Nice to have: Fluent Spanish; knowledge of active/passive microwave instrument concepts (SAR, altimetry, radiometry), active/passive antennas, RF engineering, and standard electrical interfaces; international project experience.

items.loc: Munich - Berlin - London - Paris - Warsaw - Tallinn
items.card: The role At Helsing we use simulation to train and test autonomy at scale, long before anything touches real hardware. You will be part of a team that owns a system for simulating large-scale 3D worlds containing hundreds of actors, rendered in real time. You will work on the internals of the simulation stack, including modelling of vehicles and other actors, integration of high-fidelity models from domain experts,
items.desc:
Who we are 
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. 
 As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously. 
 We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 
 The role 
 At Helsing we use simulation to train and test autonomy at scale, long before anything touches real hardware. You will be part of a team that owns a system for simulating large-scale 3D worlds containing hundreds of actors, rendered in real time.
 You will work on the internals of the simulation stack, including modelling of vehicles and other actors, integration of high-fidelity models from domain experts, sensor and environment simulation, networking, and interfacing with other components in a distributed system.
 Typical examples of day-to-day responsibilities include:
 Building and maintaining simulation platform internals: subsystem architecture, replication and multiplayer, performance profiling, and the interfaces used by other systems to orchestrate simulation.
 Composing simulated platforms from sensor, communications, situational awareness, effector, and control-loop models, and reasoning about the underlying physics such as flight dynamics, rigid-body behaviour, collision, and line of sight.
 Owning the trade-off between fidelity, throughput, and engineering cost, choosing the right point for each use case and validating the result against subject matter experts, integration tests, or downstream outcomes.
 Integrating 3D models, animations, and effects from our Content Engineers into the simulation.
 Investigating simulation bugs in order to bridge the gap from our simulation to a reference model.
 The day-to-day 
 You will write production code that shapes both the simulation platform and the models running inside it, and you will decide how each piece of work is validated.
 You will also translate mission requirements from subject matter experts into reusable simulation models, and make sure those models remain useful to the teams using simulation as part of their stacks.
 You will contribute to high-impact projects and collaborate with people across many teams and backgrounds.
 You should apply if you 
 Have built real simulations well beyond toy projects, especially with game engines such as Unreal, Unity, or Godot, including gameplay frameworks, replication, and profiling tooling.
 Write production code and bring proper software engineering practice into simulation work, including version control discipline, resolving ambiguity, and designing for the long term rather than the next demo.
 Reason fluently about the trade-off between physical fidelity and simulation throughput.
 Translate input from domain experts into models and behaviours, and know when real-world fidelity is needed and when it is expensive noise.
 Judge a simulation by what it enables rather than by whether it passes its tests, and treat a simulation that quietly misleads its users as a serious failure.
 Note: We operate at an intersection where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. 
 Nice to have 
 Experience with entity-component-system architectures or agent-based modelling.
 Experience with distributed simulation standards such as HLA, DIS, RPR-FOM, NETN, or FMI.
 Background in physics-heavy simulation, for example CFD, finite element methods, multi-body dynamics, or trajectory and 6DoF modelling.
 Experience with RF, electronic warfare, or radar simulation, including propagation and signal processing chains.
 Familiarity with reinforcement learning environment APIs, or with software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop validation.
 Experience with Rust, CUDA, or MATLAB and Simulink.
 Helsing's Candidate Privacy and Confidentiality Regime can be found here .

items.desc:
About Us

Axelera AI https://www.axelera.ai is a fast-growing fabless semiconductor company headquartered in the Netherlands, building high-performance, energy-efficient AI acceleration hardware and software (Metis and Europa product lines). We operate across the EU, the UK, Switzerland and the US, and are building a finance function ready to scale to public-company standards.



Position Overview

We are looking for an enthusiastic and highly organised Office & Community Specialist to support our growing Bristol office. This is an initial 6-month contract opportunity, with part-time hours (6-8 hours per week) and an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys creating a welcoming office environment while supporting community initiatives and local office operations.

You will report directly to an Office & Community Lead (Erika), who is based in the Netherlands, and work closely together to ensure smooth day-to-day operations in Bristol as our newest office location is established.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking ownership of local office activities, building connections with colleagues, and ensuring that everything behind the scenes runs smoothly.


What You'll Do

1) Office Operations

 - Be the local point of contact for day-to-day office needs and ensure the office remains well-organised, stocked, and ready to welcome employees and visitors: ensure clean, organized and safe work environment. Pick up and take action on requests related to the office and facility tasks directly with the external and internal parties.

2) Purchasing & Vendor Coordination

 - Manage purchases with local suppliers for office supplies and daily necessities.

 - Ensure smooth organisation of fruit deliveries and other regular office services, like cleaning and waste management.

 - Coordinate monthly grocery and coffee supply orders.

3) Community & Event Support

 - Help foster an engaging and welcoming workplace culture: work together with the local team and be present in the office.

 - Support onboarding activities: access control, badge assignment and desk preparation.

 - 3-4 times a year: Support local community-building initiatives, celebrations, workshops and office activities in Bristol. Research venues, make reservations, and assist with logistical arrangements for team dinners and gatherings.



Your profile:

 - Organized & Reliable: Able to prioritize tasks independently and maintain attention to detail in a dynamic environment.

 - People Person: Strong communication and interpersonal skills with a proactive and service-oriented mindset.

 - Ownership: Comfortable taking initiative and ensuring local office activities are completed efficiently.

 - Tech-Savvy: Comfortable with Microsoft Office and quick to learn new digital tools and systems.

 - Professional background: Preferably prior experience in office administration, facility support, hospitality, or a similar role.

 - Right to work in the UK. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.


What We Offer:

 - An open, creative culture that encourages innovation and collaboration, where freedom and responsibility go hand in hand.

 - The opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, international technology company.

 - A supportive and people-focused work environment where your contributions make a real impact.

The Electrical Engineering Group (EN-EL) at CERN is responsible for the electrical power-distribution network (from 400 kV to 400/230V), for the fibre-optics infrastructure, and for signal and DC-power cabling for the accelerator complex.
 You will join the electrical Design and Documentation Office (EN-EL-DDO). You will take on a support electrical designer role. This will include the creation and modification of electrical drawings, design of low voltage distribution networks, cable sizing, equipment sizing, LV protection studies and the general support to senior electrical designers. With time you will be required to take on design tasks of increasing complexity. In addition, you will oversee various quality-related activities within the Design Office, such as the management of the printing office and the maintenance and updating of templates.
 This is the perfect opportunity for a junior technician to further establish their existing knowledge of low voltage distribution circuits by putting it into practice.
 Your responsibilities: 
 Preparing design drawings using CAD software.
 Preparing calculation notes using ElecCalc/Caneco BT or similar.
 Preparing bills of material and cabling tables for electrical-related equipment in Excel.
 Updating excel based design templates.
 General quality related tasks in the design office.
 Your profile: 
 Demonstrated experience in: 
 The design of Low voltage distribution networks, cable sizing and selectivity studies.
 Producing drawings in AutoCAD or similar.
 The intermediate level of Microsoft EXCEL.
 Skills: 
 An understanding of low voltage distribution networks (selectivity, completing calculation notes, knowledge of European LV standards, protection, protection of circuits for indirect contact, knowledge of different types of earthing systems).
 An understanding of power systems; voltage drop calculations, short circuit calculations, understanding fault levels, dimensioning of cables.
 Experience on low voltage design calculation tools (ElecCalc, Caneco or similar software).
 Proficient in AutoCAD or similar.
 Proficient in Microsoft Excel.
 Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
 Beneficial skills/or knowledge: 
 Experience on the design of lighting systems for buildings and external areas using DIALux.
 Experience with E-PLAN or similar software.
 Experience in the design of medium voltage distribution networks.
 Motivated candidates without direct design office experience would still be considered.
 Eligibility criteria: 
 By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma .
 You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
 Applicants with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree are not eligible.

Job closing date: 22.11.2026 at 23:59 CET. 
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
 Target start date: 01-January-2027
 This position involves:
 Work in Radiation Areas.
 Interventions in underground installations.
 A valid driving licence.
 Job reference: EN-EL-DDO-2026-218-GRAE

 Global Benefits 
 A monthly stipend of 4687 Swiss Francs per month (tax free).
 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.
 Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.
 Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.
 A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.
 Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months.
 On-the-job and formal training including language classes.

Solution Architect

 Master or Bachelor in Biomedical Engineers, Telecommunications, IT or similar.
 3+ years in a similar role and experience in healthcare environment/ medical devices industry.
 You are fluent in both Spanish and English.

 Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards (HL7 v2, FHIR, DICOM) and experience in integrating medical devices with clinical systems and platforms.

 Practical experience with generative AI and intelligent agents applied to the automation and optimization of processes and workflows.

Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

items.desc:
Mission 
 The Molecular and Chemical Immunoengineering Group at EPFL develops molecular technologies to understand and engineer immune recognition and signaling. Our research combines protein engineering, chemical biology, molecular biology, and cell-based approaches to study T-cell recognition, post-translationally modified antigens, and synthetic immune-receptor signaling. 
 To support our expanding experimental program, we are seeking a motivated and experienced laboratory technician with strong expertise in mammalian cell culture and cell-based assays. The successful candidate will work closely with postdoctoral researchers and students across several projects and will play an important role in establishing robust and reproducible cell-based experimental workflows in the laboratory. 
 Main duties and responsibilities 
 Mammalian cell culture: Maintain and expand mammalian cell lines, including routine culture, freezing, thawing, cell banking, and quality control. 
 Cell-based assays: Perform routine signaling and functional assays, including stimulation experiments, dose-response and time-course assays, cell viability and proliferation measurements. 
 Flow cytometry: Perform sample preparation, staining, acquisition, and basic analysis for flow cytometry and phospho-flow experiments. 
 Cell engineering: Carry out transient transfection and lentiviral transduction and assist with the generation and maintenance of engineered stable cell lines. 
 Primary immune-cell work: Assist with isolation, culture, stimulation, and analysis of primary human immune cells, particularly T cells, when required. 
 Molecular biology support: Perform routine cloning, plasmid preparation, PCR, sequencing preparation, and related molecular biology procedures. 
 Experimental support: Work closely with researchers to establish standardized protocols and perform routine or repeated experiments supporting ongoing research projects. 
 Laboratory organization: Maintain cell stocks, reagents, inventories, and experimental records; assist with ordering and general laboratory organization. 
 Safety and compliance: Ensure adherence to EPFL biosafety guidelines and laboratory procedures and contribute to maintaining a safe and well-organized working environment. 
 Equipment maintenance: Assist with routine maintenance and coordination of servicing for relevant laboratory equipment. 
 Profile 
 Required qualifications 
 BSc, MSc, CFC/EFZ, or equivalent training in biology, biotechnology, bioengineering, immunology, or a related life science field. 
 At least two years of hands-on laboratory experience in an academic, clinical, or industrial research environment. 
 Strong practical experience with mammalian cell culture. 
 Experience with standard molecular and cell biology techniques. 
 Experience with flow cytometry. 
 Experience with viral transduction, transient transfection, and generation of stable cell lines. 
 Careful and reproducible experimental work with excellent attention to detail. 
 Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple routine workflows in parallel. 
 Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with researchers in an international and multidisciplinary team. 
 Good command of English. 
 Desirable qualifications 
 Experience with isolation, thawing, culture, and handling of human PBMCs and primary T cells is a strong advantage. 
 Experience with immune-cell activation, stimulation, and functional assays. 
 Familiarity with phospho-flow cytometry or reporter cell systems. 
 Experience with protein-based assays such as ELISA, Western blotting, or related biochemical techniques. 
 Experience with molecular cloning and recombinant DNA techniques. 
 Familiarity with automated or high-throughput experimental workflows. 
 French language skills are an advantage but are not required. 
 We offer 
 A stimulating position at one of the world’s leading research universities. 
 A dynamic, international, and collaborative working environment at the interface of molecular immunology, protein engineering, and chemical biology. 
 The opportunity to contribute to multiple cutting-edge research projects in immune recognition and synthetic immune signaling. 
 Close interaction with scientists from diverse backgrounds and access to EPFL’s state-of-the-art research and core facilities. 
 Opportunities for professional development, including technical and language training courses. 
 Family-friendly policies and flexible work arrangements supporting work–life balance. 
 Informations 
 Contract Start Date: As soon as possible (negotiable) 
 Activity Rate: 50–100% (negotiable) 
 Contract Type: CDD 
 Duration: 1 year, renewable 
 Workplace: EPFL, Lausanne, Switzerland 
 Application materials: CV, short motivation letter, and contact information for 2–3 references 
 For additional information please contact: Dr. Aerin Yang (aerin.yang@epfl.ch)
